minnanocraft.token.verdant.desc: The Japanese 新緑 (shinryoku) merges 新 (new) + 緑 (green), denoting fresh green foliage; in Minecraft, the verdant hue mirrors the vivid color of newly sprouted leaves.
minnanocraft.token.verdant.example: 森の中で新緑の葉が揺れる (Mori no naka de shinryoku no ha ga yureru) - The fresh green leaves sway in the forest.
minnanocraft.token.light_gray.desc: 薄灰 (usugai) combines 薄 (thin, light) + 灰 (ash, gray); it denotes a pale gray reminiscent of ash, matching the light‑gray stone textures in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.light_gray.example: 洞窟の壁は薄灰の岩で覆われている (Doukutsu no kabe wa usugai no iwa de oowareteiru) - The cave walls are covered with light‑gray stone.
minnanocraft.token.red.desc: 赤 (aka) means red; in Minecraft it appears in Redstone circuitry, lava, and red sand.
minnanocraft.token.red.example: 赤い岩が洞窟の底に光る (Akai iwa ga doukutsu no soko ni hikaru) - Red rocks glow at the bottom of the cave.
minnanocraft.token.red_1.desc: レッド (reddo) is a katakana transcription of the English word “red”, marking it as a gairaigo; in Minecraft it labels red‑colored entities.
minnanocraft.token.red_1.example: レッドの羊が草原を走る (Reddo no hitsuji ga soogen wo hashiru) - Red sheep run across the plain.
minnanocraft.token.lime.desc: 黄緑 (kimidori) combines 黄 (yellow) + 緑 (green), denoting the yellow‑green hue of the Lime dye in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.lime.example: 黄緑の葉が光る (Kimidori no ha ga hikaru) - The lime‑green leaves shine.
minnanocraft.token.cyan.desc: The term 青緑 (ao-midori) merges 青 (blue) and 緑 (green), mirroring the teal hue of cyan blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.cyan.example: 青緑の羊が川を渡る (ao-midori no hitsuji ga kawa wo wataru) - A cyan sheep crosses the river
minnanocraft.token.light_blue.desc: 空 (sora) means sky; the light‑blue blocks evoke the sky’s pale color in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.light_blue.example: 空のブロックで塔を建てよう (sora no buroku de tou wo tateyou) - Let's build a tower with light‑blue blocks
minnanocraft.token.ochre.desc: 黄土 (oodo) combines 黄 (yellow) and 土 (earth), describing the earthy hue of ochre blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.ochre.example: 黄土の砂漠で金鉱石を探す (oodo no sabaku de kin kooseki wo sagasu) - Search for gold ore in the ochre desert
minnanocraft.token.brown.desc: 茶 (cha) means tea; it also denotes the brown shade of wood and soil blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.brown.example: 茶色の木材で家を作る (chairo no mokuzai de ie wo tsukuru) - Build a house using brown wood
minnanocraft.token.gray.desc: 灰 (hai) means ash/gray, matching the gray stone and ash blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.gray.example: 灰のブロックで道を敷く (hai no buroku de michi wo shiku) - Lay a path with gray blocks
minnanocraft.token.pearlescent.desc: The term 真珠 (shinjuu) combines 真 (shin, "true") and 珠 (ju, "pearl"), echoing the pearlescent sheen of prismarine blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.pearlescent.example: I found a block with a pearlescent sheen at the ocean floor (Watashi wa kaitei de shinjuu no yoona kootaku no burokkku wo mitsuketa) - I found a block with a pearlescent sheen at the ocean floor.
minnanocraft.token.purple.desc: 紫 (murasaki) means "purple" and designates the dye that colors blocks such as amethyst and purple wool in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.purple.example: A flag made of purple wool waves in the cave (Murasaki no yoomoo de tsukutta hata ga dookutsu ni yurete iru) - A flag made of purple wool waves in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.yellow.desc: 黄 (ki) means "yellow", the hue of gold and the golden sand that glitters under sunlight in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.yellow.example: Yellow sand shines, leading to the gold vein (Ki no suna ga hikari, kin no koomyaku e michibiku) - Yellow sand shines, leading to the gold vein.
minnanocraft.token.green.desc: 緑 (midori) means "green", the color of leaves, vegetation, and emerald blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.green.example: Green leaves glow within the forest (Midori no ha ga mori no naka de hikatte iru) - Green leaves glow within the forest.
minnanocraft.token.blue.desc: 青 (ao) means "blue", the hue of water, lapis lazuli, and the sky that surrounds the Minecraft world.
minnanocraft.token.blue.example: Blue water fills the cavern, reflecting light (Aoi mizu ga dookutsu wo mitashi, hikari wo hansha suru) - Blue water fills the cavern, reflecting light.
minnanocraft.token.orange.desc: The term 橙 (daidai) denotes the orange citrus fruit, matching the hue of orange sheep in Minecraft, created by dyeing wool with orange dye.
minnanocraft.token.orange.example: 橙の羊が草原で跳ねている (Daida no hitsuji ga sougen de hanete iru) - Orange sheep are hopping across the plains.
minnanocraft.token.black.desc: 黒 (kuro) means 'black', a shade linked to coal and squid ink, employed for black blocks such as black wool or black concrete in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.black.example: 黒い洞窟の壁に光が差す (Kuroi doukutsu no kabe ni hikari ga sasu) - Light shines on the walls of the black cave.
minnanocraft.token.white.desc: 白色 (shiroiro) merges 白 (shiro, 'white') and 色 (iro, 'color'), denoting the pure white of snow blocks and white wool in the game.
minnanocraft.token.white.example: 白色の雪が山を覆う (Shiroiro no yuki ga yama wo oou) - White snow covers the mountain.
minnanocraft.token.pink.desc: 桃 (momo) refers to the peach fruit, whose pink hue matches the pink wool block crafted with pink dye in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.pink.example: 桃の花が咲く森で羊を見つけた (Momo no hana ga saku mori de hitsuji wo mitsuketa) - I found a sheep in the forest where peach blossoms bloom.
minnanocraft.token.pink_1.desc: 桜 (sakura) denotes the cherry blossom, a light pink emblem, describing the pink hue of pink concrete blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.pink_1.example: 桜の木の下でピンクのブロックを置く (Sakura no ki no shita de pinku no burokkku wo oku) - I placed a pink block under the cherry tree.
minnanocraft.token.magenta.desc: The term 赤紫 (akashi) merges 赤 (aka) 'red' and 紫 (murasaki) 'purple', mirroring the red‑purple hue of Minecraft's magenta wool blocks.
minnanocraft.token.magenta.example: 赤紫の羊毛で旗を作ろう！ (Akashi no youmou de hata wo tsukurou!) - Let's craft a banner using magenta wool.
minnanocraft.token.dark.desc: ダーク (daaku) is rendered in katakana as a gairaigo from English 'dark'. In Minecraft it prefixes items such as Dark Oak, denoting a darker shade.
minnanocraft.token.dark.example: ダークオークの木材で屋根を作ろう！ (Daaku Ooku no mokuzai de yane wo tsukurou!) - Let's build a roof using dark oak wood.
minnanocraft.token.oak.desc: オーク (ooku) is written in katakana as a loanword from English 'oak', designating the standard oak wood block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.oak.example: オークの板で家を建てよう！ (Ooku no ita de ie wo tatemashou!) - Let's build a house with oak planks.
minnanocraft.token.birch.desc: シラカバ (shirakaba) is rendered in katakana, originating from the native term 白樺 (shirokaba) – 白 (shiro) 'white' and 樺 (kaba) 'birch'. In Minecraft the birch tree’s pale bark matches this meaning.
minnanocraft.token.birch.example: シラカバの木で灯篭を作ろう！ (Shirakaba no ki de tourou wo tsukurou!) - Let's craft a lantern using birch wood.
minnanocraft.token.spruce.desc: トウヒ (touhi) is written in katakana, denoting the native Japanese word for 'spruce'. In Minecraft, spruce wood exhibits a grayish hue akin to real spruce trees.
minnanocraft.token.spruce.example: トウヒの木で船を作ろう！ (Touhi no ki de fune wo tsukurou!) - Let's build a boat using spruce wood.
minnanocraft.token.acacia.desc: The word アカシア (Akashia) is a gairaigo from English “acacia”. In Minecraft, acacia wood’s orange‑brown bark mirrors the real‑world acacia’s distinctive color, linking the name to its appearance.
minnanocraft.token.acacia.example: 私はアカシアの木を切って、家を建てます (Watashi wa Akashia no ki wo kitte, ie wo tatemasu) - I cut an acacia tree and build a house.
minnanocraft.token.pale.desc: ペール (Pēru) comes from the English “pale”. In Minecraft, “pale” can describe the faint coloration of certain blocks, such as the light‑colored quartz, matching the term’s meaning.
minnanocraft.token.pale.example: 洞窟の壁はペールな光で照らされている (Dookutsu no kabe wa Pēru na hikari de terasarete iru) - The cave walls are lit by a pale light.
minnanocraft.token.mangrove.desc: マングローブ (Manguroobu) derives from English “mangrove”. In Minecraft, the mangrove swamp biome features mangrove trees whose roots protrude from shallow water, mirroring the real ecosystem.
minnanocraft.token.mangrove.example: 私たちはマングローブの根を集めて、橋を作ります (Watashitachi wa Manguroobu no ne wo atsumete, hashi wo tsukurimasu) - We gather mangrove roots to build a bridge.
minnanocraft.token.jungle.desc: ジャングル (Janguru) is borrowed from English “jungle”. In Minecraft, the Jungle biome is dense with tall trees, vines, and cocoa beans, reflecting a tropical jungle environment.
minnanocraft.token.jungle.example: ジャングルでココア豆を探す (Janguru de kokoa mame wo sagasu) - Search for cocoa beans in the jungle.
minnanocraft.token.cherry.desc: サクラ (Sakura) is the native Japanese word 桜 (sakura) meaning “cherry tree”. In Minecraft, the cherry tree’s pink‑tinged leaves resemble real sakura blossoms, tying the term to its appearance.
minnanocraft.token.cherry.example: 春になるとサクラの木がピンクに染まる (Haruninaru to Sakura no ki ga pinku ni somaru) - When spring arrives, the cherry tree turns pink.
minnanocraft.token.bamboo.desc: The kanji 竹 (take) denotes bamboo, a tall flexible plant; in Minecraft bamboo sprouts quickly, is used as fuel, scaffolding, and panda food, mirroring the real plant's lightness and abundance.
minnanocraft.token.bamboo.example: 竹林でパンダが竹を食べる (Chikurin de panda ga take wo taberu) - Pandas eat bamboo in the bamboo forest.
minnanocraft.token.block.desc: ブロック (burokku) is a gairaigo from English 'block', referring to any solid cube in the game, highlighting the term's foreign origin.
minnanocraft.token.block.example: 新しいブロックを置いて家を建てよう (Atarashii burokku wo oite ie wo tatemashou) - Place a new block and build a house.
minnanocraft.token.block_1.desc: 俵 (tawara) means 'bale' or 'straw sack'; in Minecraft the hay bale block mirrors this meaning, linking the kanji to the stackable item.
minnanocraft.token.block_1.example: 俵の上に羊が寝ている (Tawara no ue ni hitsuji ga neteiru) - A sheep is sleeping on the bale.
minnanocraft.token.warped.desc: 歪んだ (yuganda) translates to 'warped' or 'twisted'; the warped wood block in the Nether appears twisted and bluish, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.warped.example: 歪んだ木はネザーで見つかる (Yuganda ki wa ne-za- de mitsukaru) - Warped wood is found in the Nether.
minnanocraft.token.crimson.desc: 真紅 (shinku) means 'deep red' or 'crimson'; the Crimson Forest biome features vivid red hues, directly echoing the kanji's meaning.
minnanocraft.token.crimson.example: 真紅の森で光る葉を集めよう (Shinku no mori de hikaru ha wo atsumeyou) - Gather the glowing leaves in the Crimson Forest.
minnanocraft.token.wood.desc: The character 木 (ki) denotes "tree" or "wood"; in Minecraft it labels all wooden blocks used for planks, sticks and crafting.
minnanocraft.token.wood.example: 私は木の板で家を建てる (Watashi wa ki no ita de ie wo tateru) - I build a house with wooden planks
minnanocraft.token.tuff.desc: Gyookaigan merges 凝 (gyoo, "to solidify"), 灰 (hai, "ash") and 岩 (gan, "rock"); it names the volcanic stone that appears as tuff in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.tuff.example: 洞窟の壁は凝灰岩でできている (Dookutsu no kabe wa gyookaigan de dekiteiru) - The cave walls are made of tuff
minnanocraft.token.bedrock.desc: Ganban combines 岩 (gan, "rock") and 盤 (ban, "plate"), referring to the unbreakable base layer in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.bedrock.example: 底層は岩盤で覆われている (Tekiso wa ganban de oowareteiru) - The bottom layer is covered by bedrock
minnanocraft.token.flint.desc: Hiuchi ishi merges 火 (hi, "fire"), 打 (uchi, "to strike") and 石 (ishi, "stone"); in Minecraft it creates sparks for lighting fires.
minnanocraft.token.flint.example: 火打石で火を起こす (Hiuchi ishi de hi wo okosu) - Light a fire with flint
minnanocraft.token.gravel.desc: Jari joins 砂 (suna, "sand") with 利 (ri, "advantage"), yet it denotes small stones used as gravel in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.gravel.example: 砂利が落ちて道が塞がれる (Jari ga ochite michi ga fusagareru) - Gravel falls and blocks the path
minnanocraft.token.sand.desc: The term 砂 (suna) means sand; the kanji denotes loose particles, mirroring the granular block that falls and can be smelted into glass in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.sand.example: 砂の上で砂時計を作ろう (Suna no ue de sunadokei wo tsukurou) - Let's craft an hourglass on the sand.
minnanocraft.token.basalt.desc: Genbugan (玄武岩) merges 玄 (gen, mysterious), 武 (bu, warrior) and 岩 (gan, rock); the name suggests a dark, sturdy stone, matching the basalt columns found in Nether fortresses.
minnanocraft.token.basalt.example: 玄武岩の柱で要塞を築く (Genbugan no hashira de yoosai wo kizuku) - Build a fortress with basalt pillars.
minnanocraft.token.granite.desc: Kakoogan (花崗岩) joins 花 (ka, flower) and 崗 (koo, ridge) with 岩 (gan, rock); the phrase hints at the speckled texture of granite, akin to the block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.granite.example: 花崗岩の壁で装飾的な塔を作る (Kakoogan no kabe de sooshokuteki na too wo tsukuru) - Build a decorative tower using granite walls.
minnanocraft.token.andesite.desc: Anzangan (安山岩) merges 安 (an, peaceful), 山 (zan, mountain) and 岩 (gan, rock); the term describes a calm mountain stone, echoing the neutral gray of andesite in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.andesite.example: 安山岩で道を平らにする (Anzangan de michi wo taira ni suru) - Flatten a path using andesite.
minnanocraft.token.diorite.desc: Senryokugan (閃緑岩) combines 閃 (sen, flash), 緑 (ryoku, green) and 岩 (gan, rock); the name implies a stone that flashes with green specks, matching the veined appearance of diorite in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.diorite.example: 閃緑岩の斑点で装飾的な床を作る (Senryokugan no hantēn de sooshokuteki na yuka wo tsukuru) - Craft a decorative floor with diorite speckles.
minnanocraft.token.deepslate.desc: The term 深層岩 (shinsougan) merges 深 (deep) + 層 (layer) + 岩 (rock), mirroring the rock that appears in deep underground layers, just like the Deepslate block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.deepslate.example: 深層岩の洞窟で鉱石を探す。 (Shinsougan no doukutsu de kousei wo sagasu.) - Search for ores in deepslate caves.
minnanocraft.token.deepslate_1.desc: 深層 (shinsou) translates to "deep layer", denoting the underground stratum where Deepslate appears.
minnanocraft.token.deepslate_1.example: 深層の地底で新しい資源が見つかる。 (Shinsou no chitei de atarashii shigen ga mitsukaru.) - New resources are found in the deep layer.
minnanocraft.token.stone.desc: 石 (ishi) is the standard kanji for "stone", representing the fundamental building block in the game.
minnanocraft.token.stone.example: 石で家を作る。 (Ishi de ie wo tsukuru.) - Build a house using stone.
minnanocraft.token.stone_1.desc: ストーン (sutoon) is written in katakana as a gairaigo from English "stone", typical for block names in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.stone_1.example: ストーンの壁は頑丈だ。 (Sutoon no kabe wa ganjou da.) - The stone wall is sturdy.
minnanocraft.token.cobblestone.desc: 丸石 (maruishi) merges 丸 (maru, "round") + 石 (ishi, "stone"), depicting the rounded stones used as cobblestone.
minnanocraft.token.cobblestone.example: 丸石で道を舗装する。 (Maruishi de michi wo hosou suru.) - Lay a path with cobblestone.
minnanocraft.token.blackstone.desc: ブラックストーン (burakku sutoon) is a katakana loanword mirroring the English "blackstone"; in Minecraft it denotes a dark stone from the Nether, matching the literal meaning "black stone".
minnanocraft.token.blackstone.example: ブラックストーンの塔を建てよう (Burakku sutoon no too wo tatemashoo) - Let's build a tower of blackstone
minnanocraft.token.chainmail.desc: チェーン (chēn) is a katakana gairaigo meaning "chain"; in Minecraft it names the chainmail armor, whose visual design resembles linked metal rings.
minnanocraft.token.chainmail.example: チェーンの鎧でモンスターと戦う (Chēn no yoroi de monsutaa to tatakau) - Fight monsters with chainmail armor
minnanocraft.token.charcoal.desc: 木炭 (もくたん, mokutan) merges 木 (tree, wood) and 炭 (charcoal); it denotes charcoal produced by burning wood, matching the Minecraft item.
minnanocraft.token.charcoal.example: 木炭で松明を作る (Mokutan de takuyaki wo tsukuru) - Craft torches with charcoal
minnanocraft.token.coal.desc: 石炭 (せきたん, sekitan) combines 石 (stone) and 炭 (charcoal); literally "stone charcoal", referring to the mineral coal mined in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.coal.example: 石炭を燃料に使う (Sekitan wo nenryoo ni tsukau) - Use coal as fuel
minnanocraft.token.iron.desc: 鉄 (てつ, tetsu) is a single kanji meaning "iron"; in Minecraft it represents the metal mined from ore and crafted into tools and armor.
minnanocraft.token.iron.example: 鉄のツルハシで岩を壊す (Tetsu no tsuruhashi de iwa wo kowasu) - Break rocks with an iron pickaxe
minnanocraft.token.iron_1.desc: アイアン (Aian) is a gairaigo from English “iron”, denoting the metal used for tools and armor in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.iron_1.example: アイアンのツルハシで岩を掘る (Aian no tsuruhashi de iwa wo horu) - Mine rocks with an iron pickaxe.
minnanocraft.token.iron_nugget.desc: 鉄 (tetsu) means “iron” and 塊 (kai) means “lump”; together 鉄塊 (tetsu kai) refers to the tiny iron mass in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.iron_nugget.example: 鉄塊を集めて金床でインゴットにする (Tetsu kai wo atsumete kinboo de ingotto ni suru) - Collect iron nuggets and smelt them into an ingot on a furnace.
minnanocraft.token.copper.desc: 銅 (dou) is the kanji for copper, the material for wires and blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.copper.example: 銅のブロックでレッドストーン回路を作る (Dou no burokku de reddosutoon kairo wo tsukuru) - Build a redstone circuit with copper blocks.
minnanocraft.token.copper_1.desc: カッパー (kappaa) is a gairaigo from English “copper”, used as the item name in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.copper_1.example: カッパーのツルハシで鉱石を採掘する (Kappaa no tsuruhashi de kooseki wo saikutsu suru) - Mine ore with a copper pickaxe.
minnanocraft.token.gold.desc: 金 (kin) means “gold” and also “money”; in Minecraft it denotes the precious yellow metal used for high‑value items.
minnanocraft.token.gold.example: 金のリンゴで一時的に飛行できる (Kin no ringo de ichijiteki ni hikoo dekiru) - Gain temporary flight with a golden apple.
minnanocraft.token.golden.desc: The kanji 金 (kin) means “gold”. In Minecraft it evokes the shiny golden look of items such as gold.
minnanocraft.token.golden.example: 金のツルハシで鉱石を掘る (Kin no tsuruhashi de kooseki wo horu) - Mine ore with a golden pickaxe.
minnanocraft.token.gold_nugget.desc: Gold nugget is 金塊 (kinkai), where 金 (kin) means “gold” and 塊 (kai) means “lump” or “block”. It denotes the tiny lump of gold used for smelting.
minnanocraft.token.gold_nugget.example: 金塊を作業台に置く (Kinkai wo sagyoodai ni oku) - Place the gold nugget on the crafting table.
minnanocraft.token.diamond.desc: Diamond is written ダイヤモンド (daiyamondo), a katakana loanword from English “diamond”. It designates the toughest material in the game.
minnanocraft.token.diamond.example: ダイヤモンドの防具は耐久性が高い (Daiyamondo no boogu wa taikyuusei ga takai) - Diamond armor has high durability.
minnanocraft.token.emerald.desc: Emerald appears as エメラルド (emerarudo), a katakana loanword from English “emerald”. It functions as the trade currency with villagers.
minnanocraft.token.emerald.example: エメラルドで交易する (Emerarudo de kooeki suru) - Trade with emeralds.
minnanocraft.token.netherite.desc: Netherite is written ネザライト (nezaraito), merging ネザー (Nezaa, “Nether”) with ライト (raito, “‑ite”). It denotes the strongest material crafted in the Nether.
minnanocraft.token.netherite.example: ネザライトのツルハシでほとんどのブロックを壊す (Nezaraito no tsuruhashi de hotondo no burokkku wo kowasu) - Break almost any block with a netherite pickaxe.
minnanocraft.token.lapis.desc: The term ラピス (rapisu) comes from Latin *lapis* ‘stone’, matching the deep blue gem that serves as a resource for enchantments and decoration in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.lapis.example: 洞窟でラピスを見つけたら、エンチャント台に置こう (Doukutsu de rapisu wo mitsuketara, enchanto-dai ni okou) - If you find lapis in a cave, place it on the enchantment table.
minnanocraft.token.lazuli.desc: ラズリ (razuri) is a loan from French *lazur* or Latin *lazulum*, denoting the vivid blue mineral that forms the Minecraft lapis lazuli block.
minnanocraft.token.lazuli.example: ラズリの鉱石を採掘して、染料に変えよう (Razuri no kouseki wo saikutsu shite, senryou ni kaeyou) - Mine lazuli ore and turn it into dye.
minnanocraft.token.quartz.desc: クォーツ (ku~o~tsu) comes from English *quartz*, naming the translucent crystal in the Nether that serves for building and redstone components.
minnanocraft.token.quartz.example: ネザーでクォーツを集めて、光る柱を作ろう (Neza- de ku~o~tsu wo atsumete, hikaru hashira wo tsukurou) - Gather quartz in the Nether and build glowing pillars.
minnanocraft.token.amethyst.desc: アメジスト (amejisuto) originates from Greek *amethystos* ‘not intoxicated’; in Minecraft it denotes the purple crystal in geodes, useful for respawn anchors.
minnanocraft.token.amethyst.example: 洞窟の奥でアメジストのブロックを見つけたら、音楽ブロックと組み合わせよう (Doukutsu no oku de amejisuto no buroku wo mitsuketara, ongaku-buroku to kumiawaseyou) - When you find amethyst blocks deep in a cave, combine them with note blocks.
minnanocraft.token.calcite.desc: 方解石 (houkaisei) is formed from 方 (hou, ‘direction/side’), 解 (kai, ‘to dissolve’), and 石 (seki, ‘stone’); it describes a stone that dissolves easily, matching the pale, fragile calcite block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.calcite.example: 山岳バイオームで方解石を採掘して、建築素材に使おう (Sangaku baio-mu de houkaisei wo saikutsu shite, kenchiku sozai ni tsukaou) - Mine calcite in the mountain biome and use it as building material.
minnanocraft.token.leather.desc: The term 革 (kawa) literally means leather, the hide of animals; in Minecraft it is harvested from cows and used to craft light armor.
minnanocraft.token.leather.example: 牛から 革 を 取って 防具 を 作ろう (Ushi kara kawa wo totte boogu wo tsukurou) - Gather leather from cows and craft armor.
minnanocraft.token.armor.desc: Yoroi (鎧) means full armor; in Minecraft it denotes the set of pieces that shields the player.
minnanocraft.token.armor.example: 全ての 鎧 を 装備すれば 敵の 攻撃 を 防げる (Subete no yoroi wo soobi sureba teki no koogeki wo fusegeru) - Equipping the full armor set protects against enemy attacks.
minnanocraft.token.armor_1.desc: Boogu (防具) merges 防 (boo, to defend) and 具 (gu, tool), meaning protective gear; in Minecraft it refers to any armor piece.
minnanocraft.token.armor_1.example: 防具 を 強化すれば 耐久度 が 上がる (Boogu wo kyooka sureba taikyuudo ga agaru) - Strengthening the armor raises its durability.
minnanocraft.token.helmet.desc: Herumetto (ヘルメット) is a gairaigo from English 'helmet', used in Minecraft to protect the head.
minnanocraft.token.helmet.example: ヘルメット を 装着すれば 頭 が 安全だ (Herumetto wo soochaku sureba atama ga anzen da) - With the helmet equipped, the head is safe.
minnanocraft.token.helmet_1.desc: Booshi (帽子) merges 帽 (boo, hat) and 子 (shi, suffix), meaning hat; in Minecraft it can serve as decorative headgear.
minnanocraft.token.helmet_1.example: 帽子 を 被って 冒険 に 出かけよう (Booshi wo kabutte booken ni dekakeyoo) - Put on the hat and set out on an adventure.
minnanocraft.token.helmet_2.desc: The word 甲羅 (koura) is formed by 甲 (kou, “armor/shell”) + 羅 (ra, “thin net/layer”), literally “armor net,” used for a turtle's shell; in Minecraft the shell helmet mimics a protective carapace for the head.
minnanocraft.token.helmet_2.example: 洞窟の奥で光る甲羅を見つけた (Doukutsu no oku de hikaru koura wo mitsuketa) - I found a shining shell deep in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.chestplate.desc: チェストプレート (chesuto pureeto) is a katakana gairaigo from English “chestplate,” denoting the torso armor that increases the player’s protection.
minnanocraft.token.chestplate.example: 敵の矢が当たらないようにチェストプレートを装備した (Teki no ya ga ataranai you ni chesuto pureeto wo soubi shita) - I equipped a chestplate so enemy arrows wouldn’t hit me.
minnanocraft.token.chestplate_1.desc: 上着 (uwagi) consists of 上 (ue, “above”) + 着 (ki, “to wear”), literally “upper garment”; in Minecraft it corresponds to a chestplate or tunic covering the torso.
minnanocraft.token.chestplate_1.example: 寒い夜は上着を着て洞窟に入った (Samui yoru wa uwagi wo kite doukutsu ni haitta) - On a cold night I put on the 上着 and entered the cave.
minnanocraft.token.leggings.desc: レギンス (reginsu) is a katakana loan from English “leggings,” the leg armor that offers agility and protection in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.leggings.example: 速く走るためにレギンスを装備した (Hayaku hashiru tame ni reginsu wo soubi shita) - I equipped leggings to run faster.
minnanocraft.token.leggings_1.desc: ズボン (zubon) is a katakana gairaigo derived from French “pantalon,” meaning “pants”; in Minecraft it refers to the basic leg armor.
minnanocraft.token.leggings_1.example: 新しいズボンで洞窟探検を始めた (Atarashii zubon de doukutsu tanken wo hajimeta) - I started cave exploring with the new ズボン.
minnanocraft.token.boots.desc: ブーツ (buutsu) is a katakana loan from English “boots”; in Minecraft it denotes the foot armor that shields the player’s feet, matching the literal meaning of footwear.
minnanocraft.token.boots.example: 私はダイヤのブーツを履いて洞窟を探検する (Watashi wa daiya no buutsu wo haite dookoo wo tanken suru) - I explore caves wearing diamond boots.
minnanocraft.token.foot.desc: 足 (ashi) means “foot” or “leg”; in Minecraft the player’s foot contacts blocks, enabling movement and jumping.
minnanocraft.token.foot.example: 足が濡れたので、石のブーツを作る (Ashi ga nureta node, ishi no buutsu wo tsukuru) - Since my feet got wet, I craft stone boots.
minnanocraft.token.nose.desc: 鼻 (hana) means “nose” or “snout”; in Minecraft it evokes the idea of sniffing, relevant for mob tracking or detection mechanisms.
minnanocraft.token.nose.example: 猪の鼻を使って、トラップを作る (Inoshishi no hana wo tsukatte, torappu wo tsukuru) - Using the pig's snout, I build a trap.
minnanocraft.token.to_sound.desc: 鳴らす (narasu) merges 鳴 (naru, “to sound”) with the causative suffix, meaning “to make a sound”; in Minecraft it is used to trigger sound-producing blocks such as note blocks.
minnanocraft.token.to_sound.example: レッドストーンの音符ブロックで音を鳴らす (Reddo sutoon no onpu burokku de oto wo narasu) - I make a sound with the redstone note block.
minnanocraft.token.detector.desc: ディテクター (ditekutaa) is a katakana loan from English “detector”, naming blocks that sense light, sound, or motion in redstone circuits.
minnanocraft.token.detector.example: 光ディテクターでモブの出現を感知する (Hikari ditekutaa de mobu no shutsugen wo kanchi suru) - I detect mob spawns with the light detector.
minnanocraft.token.detector_1.desc: The word ディテクター (Ditekutaa) is a gairaigo from English “detector”. In Minecraft it senses entities, matching the literal meaning of a device that detects.
minnanocraft.token.detector_1.example: ディテクターが近くのモブを感知した。 (Ditekutaa ga chikaku no mobu wo kanchi shita.) - The detector sensed nearby mobs.
minnanocraft.token.piston.desc: ピストン (Pisuton) is derived from the English “piston”, the moving component of an engine. In Minecraft it pushes blocks when powered, mirroring a real piston.
minnanocraft.token.piston.example: ピストンがレッドストーン信号で伸びた。 (Pisuton ga reddosutoon shingoo de nobita.) - The piston extended with a redstone signal.
minnanocraft.token.observer.desc: オブザーバー (Obuzaabaa) comes from English “observer”. It watches block updates and emits a redstone signal, acting like a visual sensor.
minnanocraft.token.observer.example: オブザーバーが隣のブロックが壊れると信号を出した。 (Obuzaabaa ga tonari no burokkuto ga kowareru to shingoo wo dashita.) - The observer emitted a signal when the neighboring block broke.
minnanocraft.token.repeater.desc: リピーター (Ripītaa) is taken from English “repeater”, a device that repeats or amplifies signals. In Minecraft it strengthens and delays redstone signals.
minnanocraft.token.repeater.example: リピーターで信号を二倍にした。 (Ripītaa de shingoo wo nibai ni shita.) - I used the repeater to double the signal.
minnanocraft.token.hopper.desc: ホッパー (Hoppaa) derives from English “hopper”. It acts as a funnel that moves items from one container to another, mirroring the concept of a hopper.
minnanocraft.token.hopper.example: ホッパーがチェストへアイテムを送った。 (Hoppaa ga chesuto e aitemu wo okutta.) - The hopper sent items to the chest.
minnanocraft.token.dropper.desc: ドロッパー (doroppaa) is a katakana loan from English “dropper”, reflecting its role of releasing items like a dripping faucet in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.dropper.example: ドロッパーからアイテムが降り注ぐ (Doroppaa kara aitemu ga furisosogu) - Items rain down from the dropper.
minnanocraft.token.dispenser.desc: ディスペンサー (disupensaa) is a katakana rendering of English “dispenser”, denoting its function of ejecting items outward.
minnanocraft.token.dispenser.example: ディスペンサーが矢を放つ (Disupensaa ga ya wo hanatsu) - The dispenser shoots arrows.
minnanocraft.token.comparator.desc: コンパレーター (konparētaa) is a katakana loan of English “comparator”, reflecting its ability to compare redstone signal strengths.
minnanocraft.token.comparator.example: コンパレーターが信号を比較する (Konparētaa ga shingoo wo hikaku suru) - The comparator compares signals.
minnanocraft.token.compass.desc: コンパス (konpasu) is a katakana adaptation of English “compass”, serving as a navigation tool toward the world spawn.
minnanocraft.token.compass.example: コンパスが北を指す (Konpasu ga kita wo sasu) - The compass points north.
minnanocraft.token.recovery.desc: リカバリー (rikabarī) is a katakana loan from English “recovery”, relating to the restoration of health or lost items in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.recovery.example: リカバリーで体力が回復する (Rikabarī de tairyoku ga kaifuku suru) - Recovery restores health.
minnanocraft.token.totem.desc: トーテム (tootemu) is a katakana loan from English "totem"; in Minecraft it is a block that can be placed as a resurrection altar, echoing the notion of a sacred object that preserves life.
minnanocraft.token.totem.example: トーテムを祭壇に置くと、死んでも復活できる。 (Tootemu wo saidan ni oku to, shinde mo fukkatsu dekiru.) - Placing the totem on the altar lets you resurrect after death.
minnanocraft.token.rod.desc: ロッド (roddo) is a katakana loan from English "rod"; in Minecraft it refers to the fishing rod, a long tool used to catch fish, matching the literal meaning of "rod".
minnanocraft.token.rod.example: 川でロッドを使ってサバイバル魚を釣る。 (Kawa de roddo wo tsukatte sabaibaru sakana wo tsuru.) - Use the rod in the river to catch survival fish.
minnanocraft.token.stick.desc: 棒 (boo) is a kanji meaning "stick" or "rod"; in Minecraft, sticks are crafted from wood and serve as the basic component for tools and weapons.
minnanocraft.token.stick.example: 木をクラフトして棒を作り、ツールの材料にする。 (Ki wo kurafuto shite boo wo tsukuri, tsuuru no zairyoo ni suru.) - Craft wood into sticks and use them as material for tools.
minnanocraft.token.shield.desc: 盾 (tate) means "shield"; in Minecraft the shield blocks arrows and melee attacks, mirroring its traditional defensive role.
minnanocraft.token.shield.example: 敵の矢が来たら、盾で防御する。 (Teki no ya ga kitara, tate de boogyo suru.) - When enemy arrows come, defend with the shield.
minnanocraft.token.bow.desc: 弓 (yumi) stands for "bow"; in Minecraft the bow lets players shoot arrows from afar, echoing the historic use of bows for hunting.
minnanocraft.token.bow.example: 弓で遠くのゾンビを狙い撃ちする。 (Yumi de tooku no zonbi wo nerai uchi suru.) - Use the bow to aim and shoot distant zombies.
minnanocraft.token.crossbow.desc: Crossbow (クロスボウ, kurosu bou) is a katakana loan from English; in Minecraft it functions as a ranged weapon resembling a medieval crossbow.
minnanocraft.token.crossbow.example: I shot a zombie with a crossbow. (Watashi wa kurosu bou de zonbi wo shageki shita.) - Eu atirei em um zumbi com a besta.
minnanocraft.token.trident.desc: Trident (トライデント, torai dento) is a katakana loan from English; in Minecraft it is a throwable weapon wielded by drowned mobs.
minnanocraft.token.trident.example: The drowned guard the ocean monument with a trident. (Oboreta mono wa torai dento de kaitei shinden wo mamoru.) - Os afogados defendem wo monumento oceânico com wo tridente.
minnanocraft.token.elytra.desc: Elytra (エリトラ, eritora) is a katakana rendering of the Greek word for "wings"; in Minecraft it grants the ability to glide through the air.
minnanocraft.token.elytra.example: I glided from the high mountain with Elytra. (Eritura de kouzan kara kakuu shita.) - Eu planar do alto da montanha usando a Elytra.
minnanocraft.token.fishing_rod.desc: Fishing rod (釣竿, tsurizao) consists of 釣 (tsuri, "to fish") and 竿 (zao, "rod"); in Minecraft it is used to catch fish and treasure from water.
minnanocraft.token.fishing_rod.example: I caught salmon with a fishing rod by the river. (Kawabe de tsurizao wo tsukatte sake wo tsutta.) - Eu usei a vara de pesca à beira do rio para pegar salmão.
minnanocraft.token.brush.desc: Brush (ブラシ, burashi) is a katakana loan from English; in Minecraft it is used to paint patterns onto blocks such as wool.
minnanocraft.token.brush.example: I painted a pattern on wool with a brush. (You mou no ue ni burashi de moyou wo kaita.) - Eu pintei um padrão na lã com a escova.
minnanocraft.token.spyglass.desc: The term 望遠鏡 (booenkyoo) merges 望 (boo, aspiration), 遠 (en, far) and 鏡 (kyoo, mirror); it literally means a mirror for far objects, matching the Spyglass function of viewing distant terrain in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.spyglass.example: 遠くの山を望遠鏡で観察する (Tooku no yama wo booenkyoo de kansatsu suru) - I observe the far mountains with the Spyglass.
minnanocraft.token.shears.desc: ハサミ (hasami) appears in katakana, a stylistic choice for tool names; the term denotes scissors, reflecting the Minecraft shears used to trim leaves and shear sheep.
minnanocraft.token.shears.example: 羊の毛をハサミで刈る (Hitsuji no ke wo hasami de karu) - I shear the sheep's wool with the shears.
minnanocraft.token.mace.desc: メイス (meisu) is a katakana loanword from English "mace", directly naming the heavy blunt weapon that deals impact damage in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.mace.example: 敵にメイスで強打する (Teki ni meisu de kyooda suru) - I strike the foe hard with the mace.
minnanocraft.token.pickaxe.desc: ツルハシ (tsuruhashi) in katakana merges ツル (tsuru, handle) and ハシ (hashi, shovel), literally “handle‑shovel”, which matches the pickaxe’s role of breaking stone in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.pickaxe.example: 岩をツルハシで掘る (Iwa wo tsuruhashi de horu) - I mine the stone with the pickaxe.
minnanocraft.token.shovel.desc: シャベル (shaberu) is a katakana loan from English "shovel", naming the digging tool that moves dirt, sand and snow in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.shovel.example: 砂をシャベルですくう (Suna wo shaberu de sukuu) - I scoop the sand with the shovel.
minnanocraft.token.hoe.desc: The term クワ (kuwa) appears in katakana, representing the native Japanese word for hoe; in Minecraft, the hoe tills dirt into farmland, mirroring its agricultural purpose.
minnanocraft.token.hoe.example: 農場を作るときはクワで土を耕す。 (Noojoo wo tsukuru toki wa kuwa de tsuchi wo koosu.) - Till the soil with a hoe when building a farm.
minnanocraft.token.axe.desc: 斧 (ono) consists of the knife radical 刂 and the tree element 木, denoting a cutting tool; in Minecraft, the axe chops logs and deals damage, echoing its real‑world role.
minnanocraft.token.axe.example: Gather timber quickly with an axe. (Ono de mokuzai wo atsumeru.) - Collect wood quickly using an axe.
minnanocraft.token.spear.desc: 槍 (yari) combines the tree radical 木 with a spearhead component, signifying a wooden pole with a sharp tip; in Minecraft, the spear attacks from range, echoing this design.
minnanocraft.token.spear.example: Launch a spear to strike mobs from afar. (Yari de mobu wo tooru.) - Use a spear to hit mobs from a distance.
minnanocraft.token.sword.desc: 剣 (ken) merges the knife radical 刂 with the blade component 刃, denoting a bladed weapon; in Minecraft, the sword deals melee damage, matching its linguistic meaning.
minnanocraft.token.sword.example: Swing the sword to defeat creepers. (Ken wo furui to kurīpaa wo taosu.) - Use the sword to defeat creepers.
minnanocraft.token.sandstone.desc: 砂岩 (suna iwa) combines 砂 (sand) and 岩 (rock), meaning "sand rock"; in Minecraft, sandstone is crafted from sand blocks, matching the literal translation.
minnanocraft.token.sandstone.example: Build a desert temple with sandstone. (Suna iwa de desert temple wo tatemasu.) - Construct a desert temple using sandstone.
minnanocraft.token.podzol.desc: Podozoru (ポドゾル) is a loan from the English scientific term for a dark, organic-rich soil; in Minecraft the block appears beneath spruce trees, mirroring its appearance as a shaded fertile ground.
minnanocraft.token.podzol.example: ポドゾルの上に松の木を植えると、暗い土が広がる。(Podozoru no ue ni matsu no ki wo ueru to, kurai tsuchi ga hirogaru.) - Plant a spruce on podzol and the dark soil spreads.
minnanocraft.token.dirt.desc: Tsuchi (土) means 'earth' or 'soil' in Japanese; in Minecraft the Dirt block is the basic soil used for farming and building.
minnanocraft.token.dirt.example: 土を掘って、農作物の畑を作ろう。(Tsuchi wo hotte, nousakubutsu no hatake wo tsukurou.) - Dig dirt to create a crop field.
minnanocraft.token.wool.desc: The term 羊毛 (youmou) merges 羊 'sheep' and 毛 'hair', literally 'sheep hair', matching the block obtained by shearing sheep in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.wool.example: 羊毛を集めて色を染めよう。 (Youmou wo atsumete iro wo someyou.) - Gather wool and dye it.
minnanocraft.token.clay.desc: 粘土 (nendo) combines 粘 'sticky' and 土 'earth', meaning sticky earth; in Minecraft the clay block is a wet, malleable material for bricks.
minnanocraft.token.clay.example: 川底の粘土を掘ってレンガを作ろう。 (Kawasoko no nendo wo hotte rengaa wo tsukurou.) - Dig the river‑bed clay and craft bricks.
minnanocraft.token.clump.desc: 塊 (katamari) translates to 'lump' or 'mass'; Minecraft ore veins form compact clusters, mirroring this meaning.
minnanocraft.token.clump.example: 石の塊を壊して鉱石を手に入れよう。 (Ishi no katamari wo kowashite kooseki wo te ni ireyoo.) - Break the stone clump to obtain ore.
minnanocraft.token.ore.desc: 鉱石 (kouseki) combines 鉱 'mineral' and 石 'stone', meaning 'mineral stone', directly describing the ore block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.ore.example: 洞窟で鉱石を見つけたら採掘しよう。 (Dookutsu de kouseki wo mitsuketara saikutsu shiyoo.) - When you find ore in a cave, mine it.
minnanocraft.token.dye.desc: 染料 (senryou) merges 染 'to dye' and 料 'substance', meaning 'dye material'; in Minecraft dyes are crafted from plants to color wool.
minnanocraft.token.dye.example: 花から染料を作って羊毛を染めよう。 (Hana kara senryou wo tsukutte youmou wo someyou.) - Craft dye from flowers and dye the wool.
minnanocraft.token.brick.desc: レンガ (renga) is a katakana loan from English "brick", denoting the baked‑clay block that visually resembles real bricks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.brick.example: レンガの壁を作って拠点を守ろう。 (Renga no kabe wo tsukutte kyoten wo mamorou.) - Build a wall of bricks to protect your base.
minnanocraft.token.mossy.desc: 苔む (koke-mu) merges 苔 (koke, "moss") with the verb suffix む (mu), indicating a moss‑covered state, matching the mossy blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.mossy.example: 苔むした階段は古代の遺跡を思わせる。 (Koke mushita kaidan wa kodai no iseki wo omowaseru.) - Mossy stairs evoke ancient ruins.
minnanocraft.token.stairs.desc: 階段 (kaidan) combines 階 (kai, "level") and 段 (dan, "step"), referring to the stair block that lets players ascend levels in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.stairs.example: 階段を上って山頂の要塞へ向かう。 (Kaidan wo nobotte sanchou no yoosai e mukau.) - Climb the stairs toward the mountaintop fortress.
minnanocraft.token.slab.desc: ハーフブロック (haafu burokku) is a katakana loan from English "half block", denoting the thin block used as a slab in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.slab.example: ハーフブロックで床を作り、光を調整しよう。 (Haafu burokku de yuka wo tsukuri, hikari wo choosei shiyoo.) - Build a floor with slabs to adjust lighting.
minnanocraft.token.pillar.desc: 柱 (hashira) means "pillar" or "column" and refers to vertical blocks that act as structural supports in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.pillar.example: 柱を並べて壮大な塔を建てよう。 (Hashira wo narabete soodaina too wo tateyoo.) - Line up pillars to build a grand tower.
minnanocraft.token.mosaic.desc: 細工 (saiku) merges 細 'fine' and 工 'craft', denoting detailed workmanship; in Minecraft, mosaic blocks are crafted by arranging colored tiles into intricate designs.
minnanocraft.token.mosaic.example: 壁に細工 (saiku) を貼って、家を飾ろう。 (Kabe ni saiku wo hatte, ie wo kazarou.) - Place mosaics on the wall to adorn the house.
minnanocraft.token.prismarine.desc: プリズマリン (purizumarin) is a gairaigo from English "prismarine", referring to the luminous ocean stone blocks.
minnanocraft.token.prismarine.example: 海底のプリズマリン (purizumarin) を採掘して、海底要塞を建てよう。 (Kaitei no purizumarin wo saikutsu shite, kaitei yoosai wo tatemashou.) - Mine prismarine from the ocean floor to build the ocean monument.
minnanocraft.token.terracotta.desc: テラコッタ (terakotta) comes from Italian "terracotta", meaning 'baked earth', matching the reddish baked‑clay blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.terracotta.example: 洞窟でテラコッタ (terakotta) を見つけて、装飾ブロックに使おう。 (Dookutsu de terakotta wo mitsukete, sooshoku burokkku ni tsukau.) - Find terracotta in caves and use it as a decorative block.
minnanocraft.token.banner.desc: 旗 (hata) translates to 'flag'; in Minecraft, banners are customizable flags used to mark locations or display heraldry.
minnanocraft.token.banner.example: 拠点に旗 (hata) を立てて、所有者を示そう。 (Kyoten ni hata wo tatete, shoyuusha wo shimesou.) - Place a banner at the outpost to show ownership.
minnanocraft.token.concrete.desc: コンクリート (konkurīto) is a katakana loan from English "concrete", mirroring the block's gray, solid appearance used for sturdy builds in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.concrete.example: 私はコンクリートで橋を作る (Watashi wa konkurīto de hashi wo tsukuru) - I build a bridge with concrete.
minnanocraft.token.nylium.desc: ナイリウム (nairiumu) is a katakana loan, derived from the fictional term "nylium" denoting the fertile substrate for Nether fungi in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.nylium.example: ナイリウムの上にシカク菌を植える (Nairiumu no ue ni shikaku kin wo ueru) - Plant warped fungi on nylium.
minnanocraft.token.planks.desc: 板材 (いたざい, itazai) combines 板 (ita, "board") and 材 (zai, "material"), indicating the block represents wooden board material.
minnanocraft.token.planks.example: 木の板材で家を建てる (Ki no itazai de ie wo tateru) - Build a house with wooden planks.
minnanocraft.token.purpur.desc: プルプァ (purupua) is a stylized katakana loan from "purpur", referring to the purple hue of the block in the Nether.
minnanocraft.token.purpur.example: プルプァの柱で塔を装飾する (Purupua no hashira de too wo sooshoku suru) - Decorate a tower with purpur pillars.
minnanocraft.token.netherrack.desc: ネザーラック (nezaa rakku) is a katakana loan from English "netherrack", the basic dark rock block of the Nether.
minnanocraft.token.netherrack.example: ネザーラックを掘って溶岩を見つける (Nezaa rakku wo hotte yoogan wo mitsukeru) - Mine netherrack to find lava.
minnanocraft.token.ingot.desc: インゴット (ingotto) is a katakana loan from English "ingot", denoting solid metal bars, matching the uniform shape of the item in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.ingot.example: 鍛冶台でインゴットを作った (Kandai de ingotto wo tsukutta) - I crafted ingots at the furnace.
minnanocraft.token.log.desc: 原木 (げんぼく, genboku) is composed of 原 ("origin, raw") and 木 ("tree, wood"), referring to the unprocessed log block obtained from trees.
minnanocraft.token.log.example: 原木を手に入れたら作業台で板に変えよう (Genboku wo te ni ireta ra sagyouda de ita ni kaeyou) - I harvested a log and turned it into planks.
minnanocraft.token.raw.desc: 原石 (げんせき, genshiki) combines 原 ("origin, raw") and 石 ("stone"), naming the unrefined ore block found underground.
minnanocraft.token.raw.example: 洞窟で原石を見つけた (Doukutsu de genshiki wo mitsuketa) - I discovered raw ore deep underground.
minnanocraft.token.raw_1.desc: 生 (なま, nama) means "raw, uncooked, fresh", applied to items like raw meat or vegetables in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.raw_1.example: 生の魚を焼く前にインベントリに入れた (Nama no sakana wo yaku mae ni inbentori ni ireta) - I stored raw fish before cooking it.
minnanocraft.token.wall.desc: 塀 (へい, hei) translates to "wall, fence", matching the Minecraft wall block used as a decorative barrier.
minnanocraft.token.wall.example: 家の周りに塀を建てた (Ie no mawari ni hei wo tateta) - I built a wall around my house.
minnanocraft.token.wall_1.desc: The term 壁 (kabe) literally means “wall”. In Minecraft, a Wall is the vertical block that defines space, matching the kanji’s meaning.
minnanocraft.token.wall_1.example: この壁 (kono kabe) に松明を取り付けよう。 - Let's attach a torch to this wall.
minnanocraft.token.scaffolding.desc: 足場 (ashiba) merges 足 (ashi, “foot”) and 場 (ba, “place”), meaning “place for the feet”. In Minecraft, Scaffolding gives a climbable platform, mirroring the kanji.
minnanocraft.token.scaffolding.example: 足場 (ashiba) を組んで高い塔へ登ろう。 - Build scaffolding to climb the tall tower.
minnanocraft.token.fragments.desc: 破片 (hahen) combines 破 (ha, “break”) and 片 (hen, “piece”), meaning “fragment”. In Minecraft, fragments are tiny pieces of materials such as glass or stone.
minnanocraft.token.fragments.example: ガラスの破片 (garasu no hahen) を集めてランタンを作ろう。 - Gather glass fragments to craft a lantern.
minnanocraft.token.sign.desc: 看板 (kanban) joins 看 (kan, “to look”) and 板 (ban, “board”), literally “looking board”. In Minecraft, a Sign displays text, acting as a board.
minnanocraft.token.sign.example: 看板 (kanban) に道案内を書こう。 - Write directions on the sign.
minnanocraft.token.portal.desc: ポータル (pootaru) is a katakana loanword from English “portal”. In Minecraft, a Portal creates a gateway between dimensions, matching the original meaning.
minnanocraft.token.portal.example: ポータル (pootaru) を作ってエンドへ行こう。 - Build a portal to reach the End.
minnanocraft.token.fence.desc: フェンス (Fensu) is a gairaigo from English “fence”. In Minecraft it denotes the wooden or stone fence block that blocks mob movement, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.fence.example: フェンスを設置して羊を守ろう (Fensu wo setchi shite hitsuji wo mamorou) - Place a fence to keep the sheep safe.
minnanocraft.token.gate.desc: ゲート (Gēto) is borrowed from English “gate”. In Minecraft it is the fence gate that can be toggled, serving as a controllable entrance.
minnanocraft.token.gate.example: ゲートを開けて村人を通す (Gēto wo akete murabito wo toosu) - Open the gate to let the villager through.
minnanocraft.token.grate.desc: 金網 (Kanawa) is composed of 金 (kin) “metal” and 網 (ami) “net”. The Minecraft grate block looks like a metal mesh, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.grate.example: 金網で鉄の格子を作る (Kanawa de tetsu no kooshi wo tsukuru) - Build an iron grate using the metal net.
minnanocraft.token.bars.desc: 格子 (Kooshi) consists of 格 (kaku) “framework” and 子 (shi) “small thing”, together meaning “lattice”. The iron bars in Minecraft act as a lattice.
minnanocraft.token.bars.example: 格子で窓を装飾する (Kooshi de mado wo sooshoku suru) - Decorate the window with bars.
minnanocraft.token.boat.desc: ボート (Booto) is a gairaigo from English “boat”. In Minecraft it is the boat item used to travel across water.
minnanocraft.token.boat.example: ボートで川を下る (Booto de kawa wo kudaru) - Travel down the river by boat.
minnanocraft.token.raft.desc: イカダ (ikada) is the native term for a floating platform of logs; the "Raft" item mirrors this concept, letting players cross water bodies.
minnanocraft.token.raft.example: イカダで川を渡ろう (Ikada de kawa wo watarou) - Let's cross the river using a raft.
minnanocraft.token.bundle.desc: バンドル (bandoru) is a katakana loan from English "bundle"; in Minecraft it serves as a compact inventory slot for multiple items.
minnanocraft.token.bundle.example: バンドルを作って資源をまとめよう (Bandoru wo tsukutte shigen wo matomeyou) - Create a bundle to consolidate resources.
minnanocraft.token.bed.desc: ベッド (beddo) is a katakana transcription of English "bed"; in Minecraft it lets players sleep to skip night and set spawn points.
minnanocraft.token.bed.example: ベッドで夜を過ごすと寝返りができる (Beddo de yoru wo sugosu to negaeri ga dekiru) - Sleeping in a bed lets you rest through the night.
minnanocraft.token.conduit.desc: コンジット (konjitto) is a katakana loan from English "conduit"; in Minecraft it creates an underwater beacon granting breathing and night vision.
minnanocraft.token.conduit.example: コンジットを海底に設置すれば水中呼吸が可能になる (Konjitto wo kaitei ni setchi sureba suichuu kokyuu ga kanou ni naru) - Placing a conduit on the ocean floor enables underwater breathing.
minnanocraft.token.froglight.desc: フロッグライト (furogguraito) is a katakana rendering of English "froglight"; it is a luminous block dropped by frogs, ideal for lighting dark spaces.
minnanocraft.token.froglight.example: フロッグライトで洞窟を照らそう (Furogguraito de doukutsu wo terasou) - Light up the cave with froglight.
minnanocraft.token.candle.desc: ろうそく (roosoku) is a native Japanese term meaning candle; in Minecraft it refers to the candle block that emits light and can be lit with flint and steel.
minnanocraft.token.candle.example: ろうそくが灯ると、暗闇が和らぐ (roosoku ga tomoru to, kurayami ga yawaragu) - When the candle lights up, the darkness eases.
minnanocraft.token.door.desc: ドア (doa) is a katakana loanword from English "door"; it denotes the block that can be opened or closed to link rooms or block mob movement.
minnanocraft.token.door.example: ドアが閉まると、モブが入れない (doa ga shimaru to, mobu ga hairenai) - When the door closes, mobs cannot enter.
minnanocraft.token.trapdoor.desc: トラップドア (torappu doa) merges the loanwords "trap" and "door" in katakana; it acts as a floor panel that opens downward when triggered.
minnanocraft.token.trapdoor.example: トラップドアが開くと、敵が落ちる (torappu doa ga aku to, teki ga ochiru) - When the trapdoor opens, enemies fall.
minnanocraft.token.trap.desc: トラップ (torappu) is a katakana loanword from English "trap"; it refers to mechanisms that capture or harm entities.
minnanocraft.token.trap.example: トラップが作動すると、プレイヤーにダメージ (torappu ga sadoo suru to, pureiyaa ni dameiji) - When the trap activates, it damages the player.
minnanocraft.token.arrow.desc: 矢 (や, ya) is a kanji meaning "arrow"; in Minecraft it denotes the projectile launched from bows or dispensers.
minnanocraft.token.arrow.example: 矢が命中すると、敵が倒れる (ya ga meichuu suru to, teki ga taoreru) - When the arrow hits, the enemy falls.
minnanocraft.token.torch.desc: Torch (taimatsu) merges 松 (matsu, pine) and 明 (mei, bright), mirroring the Minecraft torch crafted from pine wood that emits light when lit.
minnanocraft.token.torch.example: 松明 (taimatsu) を灯して洞窟を照らす。 (Matsuka (taimatsu) wo tomoshite doukutsu wo terasu.) - Light a torch to illuminate the cave.
minnanocraft.token.torch_1.desc: Torch (toochi) is a gairaigo from English "torch", representing the basic light source in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.torch_1.example: トーチ (toochi) を右クリックして光源にする。 (Toochi wo migi klikku shite koogen ni suru.) - Right‑click the torch to make it a light source.
minnanocraft.token.bulb.desc: Bulb (denkyuu) combines 電 (den, electricity) and 球 (kyuu, sphere), describing a spherical light source powered by electricity in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.bulb.example: 電球 (denkyuu) はレッドストーン回路で光る。 (Denkyuu wa reddosutoon kairo de hikaru.) - The bulb glows when powered by a redstone circuit.
minnanocraft.token.lamp.desc: Lamp (ranpu) is a gairaigo from English "lamp", referring to the block that offers steady illumination in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.lamp.example: ランプ (ranpu) を設置して夜を明るくする。 (Ranpu wo setchi shite yoru wo akaruku suru.) - Place a lamp to brighten the night.
minnanocraft.token.key.desc: Key (kagi) literally means "key", the item employed to unlock doors and chests in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.key.example: 鍵 (kagi) でドアを開ける。 (Kagi de doa wo akeru.) - Use the key to open the door.
minnanocraft.token.eye.desc: The kanji 目 (me) literally means “eye”; in Minecraft, eyes appear in items such as the Eye of Ender that guides to the portal.
minnanocraft.token.eye.example: エンダーの目で要塞を探す (Endaa no me de yoosai wo sagasu) - Search for the fortress with the Eye of Ender.
minnanocraft.token.eye_1.desc: アイ (ai) is the katakana transcription of “eye”, used for items that keep the English name in the game.
minnanocraft.token.eye_1.example: アイを投げてエンダーの位置を探す (Ai wo nage te Endaa no ichi wo sagasu) - Throw the Eye to locate the Ender.
minnanocraft.token.bucket.desc: バケツ (baketsu) comes from the English “bucket”, rendered in katakana to denote the container that carries water or lava.
minnanocraft.token.bucket.example: バケツで水を汲んで農場に持って行く (Baketsu de mizu wo kunde noojoo ni motte iku) - Fill the bucket with water and take it to the farm.
minnanocraft.token.mineral.desc: 鉱物 (koomotsu) combines 鉱 (koo) “ore” and 物 (butsu) “thing”, referring to resources like iron or gold extracted in the game.
minnanocraft.token.mineral.example: 洞窟で鉱物を採掘して装備を作る (Dookutsu de koomotsu wo saikutsu shite soobi wo tsukuru) - Mine minerals in caves to craft gear.
minnanocraft.token.crystal.desc: クリスタル (kurisutaru) is the katakana transcription of “crystal”, used for the block that emits light and powers the beacon.
minnanocraft.token.crystal.example: クリスタルを集めてビーコンを起動する (Kurisutaru wo atsumete bīkon wo kidoo suru) - Gather crystals to activate the beacon.
minnanocraft.token.statue.desc: 像 (zou) translates to "image" or "statue"; the kanji denotes a sculpted form that can be placed as decoration in the world.
minnanocraft.token.statue.example: 像の前に立つと、夜になると光る (zou no mae ni tatsu to, yoru ni naru to hikaru) - When you stand before the statue, it glows at night.
minnanocraft.token.filled_map.desc: 地図 (chizu) merges 地 (chi) "earth" and 図 (zu) "drawing, diagram"; it mirrors the map that displays the terrain's layout.
minnanocraft.token.filled_map.example: 新しい地図を広げて、洞窟の入口を探す (atarashii chizu wo hirogete, doukutsu no iriguchi wo sagasu) - Open the newly crafted map and search for the cave entrance.
minnanocraft.token.ball.desc: ボール (booru) is a gairaigo from English "ball", rendered in katakana to denote a round object used in mini‑games.
minnanocraft.token.ball.example: ボールを投げて、敵の塔を壊す (booru wo nagete, teki no tou wo kowasu) - Throw the ball to break the enemy's tower.
minnanocraft.token.ball_1.desc: 玉 (tama) means "ball, sphere, gem"; the kanji suggests round items such as snowballs or ender pearls.
minnanocraft.token.ball_1.example: 玉を集めて、エンドポータルを起動させる (tama wo atsumete, endo pootaru wo kidoo saseru) - Gather balls to activate the End portal.
minnanocraft.token.note.desc: 音符 (onpu) merges 音 (on) "sound" and 符 (fu) "symbol"; it denotes the musical note that plays when placed in a jukebox.
minnanocraft.token.note.example: 音符を右クリックして、レッドストーンで音楽を流す (onpu wo migi klikku shite, reddosutoon de ongaku wo nagasu) - Right‑click the note and use redstone to play music.
minnanocraft.token.book.desc: The kanji 本 (hon) means "book" or "origin"; in Minecraft, the Book item stores written text, mirroring its role as a compiled source of information.
minnanocraft.token.book.example: I crafted a book to record enchantments (Watashi wa hon wo tsukutte enchanto wo kiroku shita.) - Eu criei um livro para registrar encantamentos.
minnanocraft.token.bookshelf.desc: Bookshelf (本棚, hondana) merges 本 (hon, "book") + 棚 (dana, "shelf"); the block stores books, matching its literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.bookshelf.example: Placing a book on the bookshelf activates redstone (Hondana ni hon wo oku to, redstone ga hikaru.) - Colocar um livro na estante ativa wo redstone.
minnanocraft.token.shelf.desc: Shelf (棚, tana) means "shelf"; within the mod it acts as a surface for item organization, akin to in‑game houses.
minnanocraft.token.shelf.example: I arranged items on the shelf (Tana ni aitemu wo narabete seiri shita.) - Eu alinhei itens na prateleira.
minnanocraft.token.minecart.desc: Minecart (トロッコ, torokko) is a katakana loan from English "trolley"; in Minecraft it runs on rails, echoing a mining cart.
minnanocraft.token.minecart.example: I rode the minecart to haul ores (Torokko ni notte kouseki wo hakunda.) - Eu viajei no carrinho para transportar minérios.
minnanocraft.token.powder.desc: Powder (パウダー, paudaa) is a katakana loan from English "powder"; in Minecraft it is used for gunpowder and bone meal, matching its granular nature.
minnanocraft.token.powder.example: I crafted gunpowder using powder (Paudaa wo tsukatte kayaku wo tsukutta.) - Eu criei pólvora usando pó.
minnanocraft.token.powder_1.desc: 粉 (fun) translates to 'powder', denoting fine particles that match the granular nature of the Minecraft powder item.
minnanocraft.token.powder_1.example: 粉を集めて火山の洞窟に撒くと、光が拡散する。 (fun wo atsumete kazan no doukutsu ni maku to, hikari ga kakusan suru.) - Spread the powder in the volcanic cave and the light diffuses.
minnanocraft.token.dust.desc: ダスト (dasuto) is a katakana loanword from English 'dust', denoting fine particles such as redstone dust in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.dust.example: 赤石のダストを回路に置くと、信号が流れる。 (akaseki no dasuto wo kairo ni oku to, shingou ga nagareru.) - Placing redstone dust on the circuit lets the signal flow.
minnanocraft.token.shroomlight.desc: シュルームライト (shuruumu raito) is a katakana loan of 'shroomlight', describing the mushroom‑derived luminous block.
minnanocraft.token.shroomlight.example: 洞窟の天井にシュルームライトを吊るすと、暗闇が和らぐ。 (doukutsu no tenjou ni shuruumu raito wo tsurusuto, kurayami ga yawaragu.) - Hanging a shroomlight from the cave ceiling eases the darkness.
minnanocraft.token.glow.desc: 輝く (kagayaku) means 'to shine', matching blocks that emit light in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.glow.example: この石は夜になると輝く。 (kono ishi wa yoru ni naru to kagayaku.) - This stone shines at night.
minnanocraft.token.glow_1.desc: ヒカリ (hikari) is the native term '光' rendered in katakana, denoting light or brightness in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.glow_1.example: ヒカリが差し込むと、草が揺れる。 (hikari ga sashikomu to, kusa ga yureru.) - When light streams in, the grass sways.
minnanocraft.token.glow_2.desc: Gurou (グロウ) is a katakana loan from English 'glow', denoting illumination; in Minecraft it labels items that emit light, such as glowstone.
minnanocraft.token.glow_2.example: 光るグロウストーンを掘って、洞窟を照らそう (Hikaru Gurou Sutoon wo hotte, doukutsu wo terasou) - Mine the glowing glowstone to light the cave.
minnanocraft.token.blue_orchid.desc: Hisui Ran (ヒスイラン) mixes hisui ('jade') with ran ('orchid', 蘭); the blue orchid’s hue resembles jade, fitting the name.
minnanocraft.token.blue_orchid.example: ヒスイランを植えて、庭を彩ろう (Hisui Ran wo uete, niwa wo irodorou) - Plant the blue orchid to decorate the garden.
minnanocraft.token.egg.desc: Tamago (卵) means 'egg', the basic reproductive unit; in Minecraft it serves as a projectile and a source for chickens.
minnanocraft.token.egg.example: 卵を投げて、クリーパーを驚かせよう (Tamago wo nagete, kuriipaa wo odorokaseyou) - Throw an egg to startle a creeper.
minnanocraft.token.cactus.desc: Saboten (サボテン) is a katakana loan from Spanish 'cactus', denoting the spiny desert plant; in Minecraft it damages entities on touch.
minnanocraft.token.cactus.example: サボテンの近くで作業すると、体力が減る (Saboten no chikaku de sagyou suru to, tai ryoku ga heru) - Working near a cactus reduces health.
minnanocraft.token.hay.desc: Hoshikusa (干草) merges 干 ('dry') and 草 ('grass'), meaning 'dry grass'; in Minecraft hay bales are dried grass used for fuel.
minnanocraft.token.hay.example: 干草ブロックでかまどを燃やす (Hoshikusa burokku de kamado wo moyasu) - Burn a furnace with a hay block.
minnanocraft.token.wheat.desc: 小麦 (komugi) merges 小 (small) and 麦 (cereal), mirroring the low‑lying crop that grows in Minecraft fields, harvested for bread and food.
minnanocraft.token.wheat.example: 小麦畑で朝日に小麦を収穫する。 (Komugi hatake de asahi ni komugi wo shuukaku suru) - Harvest wheat in the field at sunrise.
minnanocraft.token.seeds.desc: 種 (tane) is a single kanji meaning “seed”, the fundamental item for planting wheat, pumpkin, and melon in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.seeds.example: 種を植えて農場を作ろう。 (Tane wo uete noojoo wo tsukurou) - Plant seeds to build a farm.
minnanocraft.token.pumpkin.desc: カボチャ (kabocha) is rendered in katakana, marking it as a gairaigo from Portuguese “caboche”, denoting the orange vegetable used for lanterns in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.pumpkin.example: カボチャを切ってランタンを作ろう。 (Kabocha wo kitte rantan wo tsukurou) - Cut the pumpkin to craft a lantern.
minnanocraft.token.pumpkin_1.desc: パンプキン (panpukin) is katakana transliteration of the English “pumpkin”, employed as an alternate name in the mod.
minnanocraft.token.pumpkin_1.example: パンプキンを祭壇に置く。 (Panpukin wo saitan ni oku) - Place the pumpkin on the altar.
minnanocraft.token.melon.desc: スイカ (suika) is written in katakana, though it is a native term derived from Chinese 西瓜, representing the melon that grows in Minecraft melon blocks.
minnanocraft.token.melon.example: スイカを収穫して渇きを癒す。 (Suika wo shuukaku shite kawaki wo iyasu) - Harvest the melon to quench thirst.
minnanocraft.token.sapling.desc: The Japanese term 苗木 (naegi) merges 苗 (na) “seedling” and 木 (ki) “tree”. In Minecraft, a sapling is the early growth stage of a tree, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.sapling.example: この苗木を植えて、森を作ろう！ (Kono naegi wo uete, mori wo tsukurou!) - Plant this sapling and build a forest!
minnanocraft.token.sprouts.desc: スプラウト (supurauto) is a gairaigo from English “sprout”. In Minecraft, sprouts appear when seeds grow, directly matching the borrowed word.
minnanocraft.token.sprouts.example: スプラウトが出たら、すぐに収穫しよう！ (Supurauto ga detara, sugu ni shuukaku shiyou!) - When sprouts appear, harvest them right away!
minnanocraft.token.bud.desc: 芽 (me) translates to “bud” or “sprout”. In Minecraft, a bud is the first growth phase of fungi or coral, embodying nascent development.
minnanocraft.token.bud.example: この芽を育てて、巨大なキノコにしよう！ (Kono me wo sodate te, kyodaina kinoko ni shiyou!) - Grow this bud into a massive mushroom!
minnanocraft.token.root.desc: 根 (ne) means “root”. In Minecraft, roots indicate a tree’s nutrient source, directly matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.root.example: 根が見えるときは、土壌が肥えている証拠だ。 (Ne ga mieru toki wa, dojoo ga koete iru shooko da.) - Visible roots signal fertile soil.
minnanocraft.token.echo.desc: 残響 (zankyou) merges 残 (zan) “remaining” and 響 (kyou) “resonance”. In Minecraft, echoing caves produce lingering sounds, matching the literal sense.
minnanocraft.token.echo.example: 洞窟で残響が鳴り続けると、危険が近い。 (Dookutsu de zankyou ga nari tsuzukeru to, kiken ga chikai.) - If echoes continue in a cave, danger is near.
minnanocraft.token.button.desc: ボタン (Botan) is a katakana loan from English “button”, used for the small pressable object that activates redstone, matching the literal meaning of a button.
minnanocraft.token.button.example: 木のボタンを押してドアを開けよう。 (Ki no botan wo oshite doa wo akeyou.) - Press the wooden button to open the door.
minnanocraft.token.pressure_plate.desc: 感圧板 (kan'atsuban) combines 感 (kan, sense) + 圧 (atsu, pressure) + 板 (ban, plate), literally “plate that senses pressure”, matching Minecraft’s pressure plate.
minnanocraft.token.pressure_plate.exampl: 感圧板に足を乗せてトラップを作ろう。 (Kan'atsuban ni ashi wo nosete torappu wo tsukurou.) - Step on the pressure plate to create a trap.
minnanocraft.token.campfire.desc: 焚き火 (takibi) combines 焚 (ta, burn) + 火 (hi, fire), literally “burning fire”, which matches the block that emits flames and cooks food.
minnanocraft.token.campfire.example: 夜に焚き火を囲んで食事をしよう。 (Yoru ni takibi wo kakonde shokuji wo shiyou.) - Gather around the campfire at night to eat.
minnanocraft.token.composter.desc: コンポスター (Komposutaa) is a katakana loan from English “composter”, denoting the block that turns waste into fertilizer, mirroring composting.
minnanocraft.token.composter.example: 作物の残りをコンポスターに入れて肥料を作ろう。 (Sakumotsu no nokori wo komposutaa ni irete hiryoo wo tsukurou.) - Put crop leftovers into the composter to make fertilizer.
minnanocraft.token.anvil.desc: 金床 (kanatoko) merges 金 (kin, metal) + 床 (toko, bench), literally “metal bench”, describing the anvil’s shape used for forging.
minnanocraft.token.anvil.example: 金床で鉄のツルハシを修理しよう。 (Kanatoko de tetsu no tsuruhashi wo shuuri shiyou.) - Repair the iron pickaxe on the anvil.
minnanocraft.token.cauldron.desc: The term 大釜 (daigama) merges 大 'big' and 釜 'iron kettle', mirroring the Minecraft cauldron that holds water for brewing.
minnanocraft.token.cauldron.example: 大釜に水を注いで、ポーションを作ろう。 (Daigama ni mizu wo sosoide, pooshon wo tsukurou.) - Fill the cauldron with water and brew potions.
minnanocraft.token.nest.desc: The character 巣 (su) denotes 'nest' or 'beehive', matching the Minecraft block that houses bees.
minnanocraft.token.nest.example: 巣の近くでミツバチを観察しよう。 (Su no chikaku de mitsubachi wo kansatsu shiyou.) - Observe the bees near the nest.
minnanocraft.token.barrel.desc: The kanji 樽 (taru) means 'barrel', reflecting the Minecraft container for fluids and storage.
minnanocraft.token.barrel.example: 樽に水を入れて、遠くの農場へ運ぼう。 (Taru ni mizu wo irete, tooku no noojoo e hakobou.) - Fill the barrel with water and carry it to the distant farm.
minnanocraft.token.chest.desc: チェスト (chesuto) is a katakana loanword from English 'chest', denoting the storage container in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.chest.example: チェストにダイヤを入れて、洞窟の入口に置こう。 (Chesuto ni daiya wo irete, dookutsu no iriguchi ni okou.) - Place diamonds in the chest and set it at the cave entrance.
minnanocraft.token.shulker_box.desc: シュルカーボックス (shurukaa bokkusu) is a katakana transliteration of 'Shulker Box', a portable storage that retains contents when broken.
minnanocraft.token.shulker_box.example: シュルカーボックスを持って、遠征に出よう。 (Shurukaa bokkusu wo motte, ensei ni deyoo.) - Take the Shulker Box on the expedition.
minnanocraft.token.shulker.desc: シュルカー (Shurukaa) is a direct loan from English “shulker”, naming the mob that retreats into a hard shell; the term mirrors its function as a portable container in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.shulker.example: 私の拠点にシュルカーが潜んでいる (Watashi no kyooten ni Shurukaa ga hisonde iru) - A shulker is lurking in my base.
minnanocraft.token.grindstone.desc: 砥石 (といし, toishi) merges 砥 “sharpening stone” and 石 “stone”, literally “sharpening stone”; in Minecraft it is used to repair and disenchant tools.
minnanocraft.token.grindstone.example: 砥石で剣を研いだ (Toishi de ken wo toita) - I sharpened my sword on the grindstone.
minnanocraft.token.flower_pot.desc: 植木鉢 (うえきばち, uekibachi) combines 植 “to plant”, 木 “tree”, and 鉢 “pot”, literally “plant pot”; in Minecraft it holds flowers and saplings.
minnanocraft.token.flower_pot.example: 庭に植木鉢を置いた (Niwa ni uekibachi wo oita) - I placed a flower pot in the garden.
minnanocraft.token.pottery.desc: 壺 (つぼ, tsubo) translates to “jar” or “pot”; in Minecraft the pottery block serves as a container, matching the original meaning.
minnanocraft.token.pottery.example: 壺に水を入れた (Tsubo ni mizu wo ireta) - I filled the pot with water.
minnanocraft.token.jukebox.desc: ジュークボックス (juukubokkusu) is a katakana loan from English “jukebox”, the block that plays records in Minecraft, preserving the original device idea.
minnanocraft.token.jukebox.example: ジュークボックスで音楽を流す (Juukubokkusu de ongaku wo nagasu) - Play music on the jukebox.
minnanocraft.token.beehive.desc: The Japanese term 養蜂箱 (youhoubako) literally means “bee‑raising box”, matching the Minecraft beehive that houses and breeds bees.
minnanocraft.token.beehive.example: 養蜂箱を設置して、ミツバチを育てよう (Youhoubako wo setchi shite, mitsubachi wo sodateyou) - Place the beehive and raise the bees
minnanocraft.token.beacon.desc: ビーコン (bīkon) is a katakana transcription of the English “beacon”, a signal tower, which aligns with its function in Minecraft as a light‑emitting beacon.
minnanocraft.token.beacon.example: ビーコンを起動して、遠くの拠点を照らそう (Bīkon wo kidoo shite, tooku no kyoten wo terasou) - Activate the beacon to illuminate the distant base
minnanocraft.token.lever.desc: レバー (rebaa) transcribes the English “lever”, a device that changes a mechanism’s state, matching its Minecraft use.
minnanocraft.token.lever.example: レバーを引いてドアを開けよう (Rebaa wo hiite doa wo akeyou) - Pull the lever to open the door
minnanocraft.token.chain.desc: 鎖 (kusari) translates to “chain”, and the Minecraft chain block behaves like a real chain, linking items vertically.
minnanocraft.token.chain.example: 鎖で天井から吊るしたランタンを支えよう (Kusari de tenjoo kara tsurusita rantan wo sasaeyou) - Support the lantern hanging from the ceiling with a chain
minnanocraft.token.chain_1.desc: チェーン (chēn) is the katakana transcription of “chain”, offering the alternative translation “cadeia”. It denotes the same Minecraft block.
minnanocraft.token.chain_1.example: チェーンを使って高い場所へ上がろう (Chēn wo tsukatte takai basho e agarou) - Use the chain to climb to a high place
minnanocraft.token.clock.desc: 時計 (tokei) combines the kanji 時 (ji) "time" and 計 (kei) "to count", literally "to count time". In Minecraft, the clock shows the day‑night cycle, acting as a time indicator.
minnanocraft.token.clock.example: 時計が刻む音で洞窟が明るくなる (Tokei ga kizamu oto de doukutsu ga akaruku naru) - The clock's ticking brightens the cave.
minnanocraft.token.bone.desc: 骨 (hone) means "bone", representing the rigid tissue of skeletons. In Minecraft, bones drop from skeletons and are used to craft items or feed wolves.
minnanocraft.token.bone.example: 犬が骨を噛むと喜ぶ (Inu ga hone wo kamu to yorokobu) - The dog rejoices when chewing a bone.
minnanocraft.token.bone_meal.desc: 骨粉 (kotsufun) merges bone (骨, hone) and powder (粉, fun), meaning "bone powder". In Minecraft, bone meal functions as a fertilizer that speeds plant growth, matching the concept of a stimulating powder.
minnanocraft.token.bone_meal.example: 骨粉で作物が一瞬で芽吹く (Kotsufun de sakumotsu ga isshun de mebuku) - Crops sprout instantly with bone meal.
minnanocraft.token.sponge.desc: スポンジ (suponji) is written in katakana, marking it as a gairaigo from English "sponge". In Minecraft, the sponge absorbs water, mirroring the porous material that retains liquids.
minnanocraft.token.sponge.example: スポンジで水を吸い取る (Suponji de mizu wo suitoru) - The sponge absorbs water.
minnanocraft.token.ice.desc: The kanji 氷 (koori) merges the water radical 氵 with the ice radical 冫, literally meaning frozen water. In Minecraft, ice appears as a clear, slippery block that melts when exposed to heat.
minnanocraft.token.ice.example: 氷の上に水を流すと滑りやすい道になる。 (Koori no ue ni mizu wo nagasu to suberiyasui michi ni naru.) - If you pour water over ice, it becomes a slippery path.
minnanocraft.token.packed_ice.desc: 氷塊 (hyookai) combines 氷 (koori, ice) and 塊 (katamari, chunk, mass). It denotes the dense ice block that remains solid under most conditions in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.packed_ice.example: 氷塊は冷凍された洞窟の壁を作るのに最適だ。 (Hyookai wa reifukareta dookutsu no kabe wo tsukuru no ni saiteki da.) - Packed ice is perfect for building walls in frozen caves.
minnanocraft.token.packed.desc: 固めた (katameta) is the past form of 固める (katameru), meaning to harden or pack. In Minecraft, "packed" describes items that have been compressed, such as packed sand.
minnanocraft.token.packed.example: 土を固めたら、圧縮ブロックができる。 (Tsuchi wo katametara, assaku burokkku ga dekiru.) - If you harden the soil, you can make a compressed block.
minnanocraft.token.snow.desc: 雪 (yuki) means snow, the falling crystals of ice. In Minecraft, snow blankets the landscape, can be harvested as a block, and slows movement.
minnanocraft.token.snow.example: 雪が降ると、屋根に白い層ができる。 (Yuki ga furu to, yane ni shiroi soo ga dekiru.) - When snow falls, a white layer forms on roofs.
minnanocraft.token.snow_1.desc: スノウ (sunoo) is rendered in katakana, marking it as a gairaigo (loanword) from English "snow". It keeps the original pronunciation while naming the snow block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.snow_1.example: スノウは寒いバイオームで自然に生成される。 (Sunoo wa samui baioomu de shizen ni seisei sareru.) - Snow naturally generates in cold biomes.
minnanocraft.token.snowball.desc: 雪玉 (yukidama) combines 雪 'snow' and 玉 'ball', precisely naming the snow sphere thrown in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.snowball.example: 雪玉でクリーパーを撃退しよう！ (Yukidama de kurīpaa wo gekitai shiyoo!) - Use a snowball to fend off a creeper!
minnanocraft.token.golem.desc: ゴーレム (gooremu) is a gairaigo from English 'golem', referring to stone or iron guardians in villages.
minnanocraft.token.golem.example: ゴーレムと一緒に鉱石を運ぼう。 (Gooremu to issho ni kooseki wo hakoboo.) - Transport ores together with the golem.
minnanocraft.token.husk.desc: ハスク (hasuku) is a loanword from 'husk', denoting the desert zombie that resists sunlight.
minnanocraft.token.husk.example: ハスクと戦うと砂が舞う。 (Hasuku to tatakau to suna ga mau.) - Fighting a husk stirs up sand.
minnanocraft.token.ghast.desc: ガスト (gasuto) derives from 'ghast', naming the floating Nether mob that shoots explosive fireballs.
minnanocraft.token.ghast.example: ガストが暗闇でうなる。 (Gasuto ga kurayami de unaru.) - The ghast roars in the darkness.
minnanocraft.token.phantom.desc: ファントム (fantomu) comes from 'phantom', referring to the flying mob that attacks players who stay asleep too long.
minnanocraft.token.phantom.example: ファントムの羽根で翼を作ろう。 (Fantomu no hane de tsubasa wo tsukuroo.) - Craft wings using phantom feathers.
minnanocraft.token.piglin.desc: Piglin (ピグリン, pigurin) uses katakana as a gairaigo of "piglin", matching its pig-like Nether creature.
minnanocraft.token.piglin.example: Piglin stalks the bastion. (Pigurin ga basuchon wo meguru.) - Piglin circula a fortaleza.
minnanocraft.token.hoglin.desc: Hoglin (ホグリン, hogurin) is a katakana transcription of "hoglin", highlighting its massive hog form.
minnanocraft.token.hoglin.example: Hoglin charges across the crimson forest. (Hogurin ga akai mori wo tsukamu.) - wo hoglin avança pela floresta carmesim.
minnanocraft.token.zoglin.desc: Zoglin (ゾグリン, zogurin) is a katakana loan of "zoglin", the undead variant of the hoglin.
minnanocraft.token.zoglin.example: Zoglin roams the ruined portal. (Zogurin ga hakai sareta pootaru wo meguru.) - wo zoglin vagueia pela porta arruinada.
minnanocraft.token.warden.desc: Warden (ウォーデン, wooden) is rendered in katakana from "warden", fitting its function as a deep‑cave guardian.
minnanocraft.token.warden.example: Warden senses every footstep. (Wooden wa subete no ashioto wo kanjiru.) - wo warden sente cada passo.
minnanocraft.token.vex.desc: Vex (ヴェックス, vekksu) employs katakana with ヴ to capture the foreign "v" sound, mirroring its pesky nature.
minnanocraft.token.vex.example: Vex darts around the witch's tower. (Vekksu ga majo no too wo mawaru.) - wo vex circula a torre da bruxa.
minnanocraft.token.guardian.desc: ガーディアン (Gaadian) is a direct loan from English “guardian”. The katakana spelling signals a transliteration, matching its role as the ocean‑realm protector.
minnanocraft.token.guardian.example: 海底神殿でガーディアンが見張りをしている (Kaitei shinden de Gaadian ga mihari wo shiteiru) - In the ocean monument, the Guardian watches.
minnanocraft.token.enderman.desc: エンドマン (Endoman) merges エンド (Endo, “end”) and マン (Man). The loanword conveys the tall, teleporting creature that haunts the End dimension.
minnanocraft.token.enderman.example: エンドマンがブロックを持ち上げた (Endoman ga burokku wo mochiageta) - The Enderman lifted a block.
minnanocraft.token.endermite.desc: エンダーマイト (Endomaito) combines エンダー (Endaa, “ender”) with マイト (Maito, “mite”). The loanword highlights its tiny, pest‑like nature near End portals.
minnanocraft.token.endermite.example: エンダーマイトがスポーンした (Endomaito ga supoon shita) - An Endermite spawned.
minnanocraft.token.creeper.desc: クリーパー (Kurīpaa) is a katakana loan from English “creeper”. The name captures the mob’s sneaky approach and explosive behavior.
minnanocraft.token.creeper.example: クリーパーが近づいてきた (Kurīpaa ga chikadzuite kita) - A Creeper came close.
minnanocraft.token.silverfish.desc: シルバーフィッシュ (Shirubaa fisshu) directly borrows the English “silverfish”. The katakana spelling denotes a foreign term for the tiny stone‑dwelling bug.
minnanocraft.token.silverfish.example: シルバーフィッシュが石ブロックから出た (Shirubaa fisshu ga ishi burokku kara deta) - A Silverfish emerged from a stone block.
minnanocraft.token.breeze.desc: ブリーズ (buriizu) is a gairaigo from English “breeze”, matching the swift, wind‑like movement of the Nether Breeze mob.
minnanocraft.token.breeze.example: ブリーズが洞窟を駆け抜けた。 (Buriizu ga doukutsu wo kakenuketa.) - The Breeze raced through the cavern.
minnanocraft.token.blaze.desc: ブレイズ (bureizu) is borrowed from English “blaze”, describing the fiery creature that shoots fireballs.
minnanocraft.token.blaze.example: ブレイズの火が洞窟を照らす。 (Bureizu no hi ga doukutsu wo terasu.) - The Blaze’s fire illuminates the cavern.
minnanocraft.token.wither.desc: ウィザー (uiyaa) derives from English “wither”, fitting the boss that causes decay.
minnanocraft.token.wither.example: ウィザーが近くのブロックを腐らせた。 (Uiyaa ga chikaku no burokkku wo kusurashita.) - The Wither corrupted nearby blocks.
minnanocraft.token.spider.desc: グモ (gumo) is a katakana rendering of the native word “kumo” (spider), referring to the crawling mob.
minnanocraft.token.spider.example: グモが天井から降りてきた。 (Gumo ga tenjou kara oritekita.) - A spider descended from the ceiling.
minnanocraft.token.spider_1.desc: クモ (kumo) is the katakana form of “kumo”, the Japanese word for spider, used for the same mob.
minnanocraft.token.spider_1.example: クモがプレイヤーを待ち伏せした。 (Kumo ga pureiyaa wo machibuse shita.) - A spider ambushed the player.
minnanocraft.token.skeleton.desc: スケルトン (sukeruton) is a gairaigo from English “skeleton”, matching the mob’s bony frame and ranged attack.
minnanocraft.token.skeleton.example: 闇の洞窟でスケルトンが弓で狙う (Yami no doukutsu de sukeruton ga yumi de nerau) - In the dark cave, a skeleton aims with its bow.
minnanocraft.token.zombie.desc: ゾンビ (zonbi) is borrowed from English “zombie”, describing the undead mob that hunts players after dark.
minnanocraft.token.zombie.example: 夜になるとゾンビが村を襲う (Yoru ni naru to zonbi ga mura wo osou) - At night, zombies raid the village.
minnanocraft.token.tadpole.desc: オタマジャクシ (otamajakushi) is a native Japanese word for tadpole, literally “small bowl”, referencing its rounded larval shape.
minnanocraft.token.tadpole.example: 池でオタマジャクシが泳いでいる (Ike de otamajakushi ga oyoide iru) - In the pond, tadpoles are swimming.
minnanocraft.token.drowned.desc: ドラウンド (doraundo) comes from English “drowned”, naming the underwater zombie that attacks with tridents.
minnanocraft.token.drowned.example: 海底でドラウンドが剣を振る (Kaitei de doraundo ga ken wo furu) - In the ocean depths, the drowned swings its sword.
minnanocraft.token.strider.desc: ストライダー (sutoraida) is borrowed from English “strider”, a mob that walks on lava, matching its literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.strider.example: 溶岩の上をストライダーが歩く (Yoogan no ue wo sutoraida ga aruku) - The strider walks across the lava.
minnanocraft.token.parched.desc: The term パーチド (Paachido) is a loan from English “parched”, denoting extreme dryness; in Minecraft, “parched” blocks show cracked textures that resemble dried earth.
minnanocraft.token.parched.example: In the arid desert, digging パーチド (Paachido) soil intensifies thirst. (Kawaita sabaku de Paachido no tsuchi wo horu to, kawaki ga masu.) - In the dry desert, digging parched soil increases thirst.
minnanocraft.token.witch.desc: ウィッチ (Uicchi) is a gairaigo from English “witch”, a sorceress; in Minecraft, witches brew potions and cast harmful effects on players.
minnanocraft.token.witch.example: In the dark forest, ウィッチ (Uicchi) brews a lingering potion. (Yoru no mori de Uicchi ga pooshon wo tsukutte iru.) - In the night forest, the witch is making a potion.
minnanocraft.token.ravager.desc: ラヴェジャー (Ravejaa) comes from English “ravager”, meaning a destroyer; in Minecraft, the Ravager is a massive hostile mob that tramples blocks and assaults villages.
minnanocraft.token.ravager.example: A lone ラヴェジャー (Ravejaa) charges through the fields, flattening everything. (Ravejaa ga hatake wo tsukamu, subete wo hakai suru.) - A solitary Ravager rushes across the fields, flattening everything.
minnanocraft.token.evoker.desc: エヴォーカー (Evookaa) is borrowed from English “evoker”, one who summons; in Minecraft, the Evoker summons vexes and wields an enchanted staff.
minnanocraft.token.evoker.example: Deep in the woodland temple, エヴォーカー (Evookaa) summons a swarm of vexes. (Mori no doojoo de Evookaa ga Vekkusu no shuudan wo yobi dasu.) - Inside the forest temple, the evoker calls forth a swarm of vexes.
