minnanocraft.token.pillager.desc: ピリジャー (Pirijaa) originates from English “pillager”, a raider; in Minecraft, Pillagers are illagers that assault villages with crossbows.
minnanocraft.token.pillager.example: A group of ピリジャー (Pirijaa) patrols the outskirts, searching for loot. (Pirijaa no ichidan ga shuuhen wo patrouiru, takaramono wo sagasu.) - A squad of pillagers patrols the perimeter, looking for treasure.
minnanocraft.token.villager.desc: The word 村人 (murabito) merges 村 (village) and 人 (person), matching the NPC that lives in villages, trades items, and follows daily routines.
minnanocraft.token.villager.example: 村人が作物を交換してくれる (Mura bito ga sakumotsu wo kookan shite kureru) - The villager trades crops.
minnanocraft.token.player.desc: プレイヤー (pureiyaa) is a katakana gairaigo from English 'player', referring to the human controlling the character in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.player.example: プレイヤーは洞窟で鉱石を採掘する (Pureiyaa wa dookutsu de kooseki wo saikutsu suru) - The player mines ores in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.friend.desc: 友 (tomo) translates to 'friend', representing a companion who can join you in building and exploring in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.friend.example: 友と一緒に城を建てよう (Tomo to issho ni shiro wo tateyoo) - Let's build a castle with a friend.
minnanocraft.token.vindicator.desc: ヴィンディケーター (vindikētaa) is a katakana loan from English 'vindicator', reflecting its role as an illager that attacks villages.
minnanocraft.token.vindicator.example: ヴィンディケーターがゾンビを倒す (Vindikētaa ga zonbi wo taosu) - The Vindicator defeats zombies.
minnanocraft.token.trader.desc: 商人 (shoonin) merges 商 (trade) and 人 (person), fitting the NPC that offers trades for emeralds and other goods.
minnanocraft.token.trader.example: 商人がエメラルドと交換する (Shoonin ga emerarudo to kookan suru) - The trader exchanges emeralds.
minnanocraft.token.allay.desc: アレイ (Arei) is a gairaigo from "allay" (to soothe); the Minecraft mob gathers items for the player, embodying the notion of easing the burden.
minnanocraft.token.allay.example: In the forest I discovered a glowing chest with an Allay (Arei) - I found a glowing chest with an Allay in the forest
minnanocraft.token.bee.desc: ミツバチ (Mitsubachi) combines 蜜 (mitsu, honey) and 蜂 (hachi, bee); in Minecraft they produce honey and pollinate, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.bee.example: In the flower field the bees (Mitsubachi) gather honey - Bees gather honey in the flower field
minnanocraft.token.dolphin.desc: イルカ (Iruka) is a katakana rendering of the native term for dolphin; in Minecraft they lead players to underwater treasure, echoing their helpful nature.
minnanocraft.token.dolphin.example: Deep underwater the dolphin (Iruka) led me to a glowing gem - The dolphin guided me to a shining gem below sea level
minnanocraft.token.nautilus.desc: オウムガイ (Oumugai) comes from 烏 (ou, crow) + 貝 (gai, shell), "crow shell"; the nautilus block resembles a spiral shell, matching the etymology.
minnanocraft.token.nautilus.example: In the oceanic temple I discovered a nautilus shell (Oumugai) - I found a nautilus shell in the submerged temple
minnanocraft.token.stray.desc: ストレイ (Sutorei) is a gairaigo from "stray" (wanderer); the Stray skeleton roams snowy biomes, embodying the notion of being lost.
minnanocraft.token.stray.example: On the frozen plain a Stray (Sutorei) howls from afar - A wandering skeleton cries out on the icy field
minnanocraft.token.sniffer.desc: スニッファー (Suniffaa) is a gairaigo from English “sniffer”, matching its ability to sniff buried blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.sniffer.example: スニッファーが土の下の化石を嗅ぎ分けた。 (Suniffaa ga tsuchi no shita no kaseki wo kagikaketa.) - The Sniffer sniffed out the fossil beneath the soil.
minnanocraft.token.squid.desc: イカ (Ika) is the katakana spelling of the native word for squid, and its in‑game behavior of swimming and shooting ink mirrors the real animal.
minnanocraft.token.squid.example: イカが水中でインクを放出した。 (Ika ga suichuu de inku wo hooshutsu shita.) - The squid released ink underwater.
minnanocraft.token.turtle.desc: カメ (Kame) is the katakana representation of the native term for turtle, and its slow movement and egg‑laying in Minecraft echo the real creature.
minnanocraft.token.turtle.example: カメが砂浜に卵を産んだ。 (Kame ga sunahama ni tamago wo unda.) - The turtle laid eggs on the beach.
minnanocraft.token.armadillo.desc: アルマジロ (Arumajiro) is a gairaigo from “armadillo”, and its rolling defense in Minecraft mirrors the creature’s protective shell.
minnanocraft.token.armadillo.example: アルマジロが危険を感じて丸くなった。 (Arumajiro ga kiken wo kanjite maruku natta.) - The armadillo curled up when it sensed danger.
minnanocraft.token.fox.desc: キツネ (Kitsune) is the katakana spelling of the native word for fox, and its sneaky behavior in Minecraft reflects the cunning nature of real foxes.
minnanocraft.token.fox.example: キツネがプレイヤーの食料を盗んだ。 (Kitsune ga pureiyaa no shokuryoo wo nusunda.) - The fox stole the player's food.
minnanocraft.token.cow.desc: ウシ (Ushi) is the native term for bovine; rendered in katakana for game stylization. In Minecraft the cow yields leather and milk, mirroring a domesticated cattle.
minnanocraft.token.cow.example: ウシが草原で草を食べている (Ushi ga soogen de kusa wo tabete iru) - The cow grazes on the plain.
minnanocraft.token.mooshroom.desc: ムーシュルーム (Muushuruumu) is a gairaigo from English 'Mooshroom', blending 'mushroom' and 'cow'. In Minecraft it appears as a red cow with mushrooms, yielding milk and mushrooms when sheared.
minnanocraft.token.mooshroom.example: ムーシュルームを見つけたら、ハサミで刈り取ろう (Muushuruumu wo mitsuketara, hasami de karitoroo) - When you find a Mooshroom, shear it.
minnanocraft.token.bat.desc: コウモリ (Koomori) is the katakana rendering of the native term 蝙蝠, composed of 蝙 (bat) and 蝠 (wing). In Minecraft they spawn in dark caves, matching their nocturnal nature.
minnanocraft.token.bat.example: 洞窟でコウモリが飛び回っている (Dookutsu de koomori ga tobimawatte iru) - Bats flutter through the cavern.
minnanocraft.token.parrot.desc: オウム (oomu) is the katakana form of the native term 鸚鵡, composed of the kanjis 鸚 and 鵡, both meaning 'parrot'. In Minecraft they mimic player sounds, echoing real parrots' vocal mimicry.
minnanocraft.token.parrot.example: オウムがプレイヤーの声を真似した (oomu ga pureiyaa no koe wo mane shita) - The parrot mimicked the player's voice.
minnanocraft.token.cat.desc: ネコ (neko) is written in katakana as a stylized loanword; the native kanji 猫 (neko) merges the animal radical 犭 with 子 ('child'), echoing the companionable cat that follows and can be tamed in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.cat.example: ネコが私のベッドの上で丸くなる (Neko ga watashi no beddo no ue de maruku naru) - The cat curls up on my bed.
minnanocraft.token.sheep.desc: ヒツジ (hitsuji) appears in katakana, though the native kanji is 羊 (hitsuji) meaning 'sheep', linking to the wool block obtained by shearing the animal in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.sheep.example: ヒツジの毛を刈ってウールを作る (Hitsuji no ke wo katte uuru wo tsukuru) - I shear the sheep's wool to make wool.
minnanocraft.token.goat.desc: ヤギ (yagi) is katakana for the native term 山羊 (yagi), literally 'mountain sheep', fitting the goat that spawns on cliffs and can be ridden in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.goat.example: ヤギが崖の上で草を食べている (Yagi ga gake no ue de kusa wo tabete iru) - The goat grazes on the cliff.
minnanocraft.token.wolf.desc: オオカミ (ookami) written in katakana corresponds to the kanji 狼 (ookami) meaning 'wolf', matching the hostile mob that can become a loyal companion when tamed in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.wolf.example: オオカミが夜に遠吠えしている (ookami ga yoru ni tooboe shite iru) - The wolf howls at night.
minnanocraft.token.polar_bear.desc: シロクマ (shirokuma) in katakana reflects the kanji 白熊 (shirokuma), literally 'white bear', appropriate for the icy‑biome mob that damages players on contact in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.polar_bear.example: シロクマが氷の上で歩いている (Shirokuma ga koori no ue de aruite iru) - The polar bear walks on the ice.
minnanocraft.token.panda.desc: パンダ (panda) is a katakana loanword, mirroring its foreign origin; in Minecraft, pandas spawn in bamboo jungles and interact by rolling and eating bamboo.
minnanocraft.token.panda.example: バンブーの森でパンダを見つけよう！ (Banbuu no mori de panda wo mitsukeyou!) - Let's find pandas in the bamboo forest!
minnanocraft.token.frog.desc: カエル (kaeru) is rendered in katakana despite the native kanji 蛙; in Minecraft, frogs spawn in swamps and can be harvested for potion ingredients.
minnanocraft.token.frog.example: 沼地でカエルを捕まえて！ (Numachi de kaeru wo tsukamaete!) - Capture frogs in the swamp!
minnanocraft.token.pufferfish.desc: フグ (fugu) is a katakana representation of the poisonous fish 河豚; in Minecraft, pufferfish puff up when hurt and can be cooked for food.
minnanocraft.token.pufferfish.example: 海でフグを見つけて料理しよう！ (Umi de fugu wo mitsukete ryoori shiyoo!) - Find pufferfish in the ocean and cook them!
minnanocraft.token.angler.desc: 釣り人 (tsuribito) merges the kanjis 釣 (to fish) and 人 (person); in Minecraft, the angler mob wields a fishing rod and attacks players near water at night.
minnanocraft.token.angler.example: 夜の湖で釣り人と戦おう！ (Yoru no mizuumi de tsuribito to tatakaou!) - Fight the angler at the night lake!
minnanocraft.token.axolotl.desc: ウーパールーパー (uupaaruupaa) is a katakana loan from the English "axolotl"; in Minecraft, axolotls inhabit water blocks and can be bred for rare drops.
minnanocraft.token.axolotl.example: 水槽でウーパールーパーを育てよう！ (Suisoo de uupaaruupaa wo sodateyoo!) - Raise axolotls in the aquarium!
minnanocraft.token.salmon.desc: The kanji 鮭 (sake) merges 魚 (fish) with a phonetic component denoting the species; in Minecraft, salmon is a raw fish obtainable from rivers and oceans, matching its real‑world environment.
minnanocraft.token.salmon.example: 川で鮭 (sake) を捕まえた。 (Kawa de sake wo tsukamaeta.) - I caught a salmon in the river.
minnanocraft.token.salmon_1.desc: サケ (sake) is rendered in katakana, indicating a gairaigo (loanword); it denotes the same fish as 鮭 and serves the identical role in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.salmon_1.example: 川でサケ (sake) を捕まえた。 (Kawa de sake wo tsukamaeta.) - I caught a salmon in the river.
minnanocraft.token.cod.desc: The kanji 鱈 (tara) merges 魚 (fish) with 替 as a phonetic element; in Minecraft, cod is a cold‑water fish that can be cooked for sustenance.
minnanocraft.token.cod.example: 海で鱈 (tara) を見つけた。 (Umi de tara wo mitsuketa.) - I found cod in the sea.
minnanocraft.token.cod_1.desc: タラ (tara) in katakana signals a loanword; it denotes the same fish as 鱈, serving as a marine food source in the game.
minnanocraft.token.cod_1.example: 海でタラ (tara) を見つけた。 (Umi de tara wo mitsuketa.) - I found cod in the sea.
minnanocraft.token.tropical_fish.desc: 熱帯魚 (nettai-gyo) merges 熱 (heat), 帯 (zone) and 魚 (fish), meaning ‘fish of warm zones’; in Minecraft, tropical fish appear in warm biomes with vivid colors.
minnanocraft.token.tropical_fish.example: 熱帯魚 (nettai-gyo) を水槽に入れた。 (Nettai-gyo wo suiso ku ni iれta.) - I placed the tropical fish in the aquarium.
minnanocraft.token.horse.desc: The kanji 馬 (uma) means ‘horse’; in Minecraft the horse is a rideable mob that provides fast travel and can jump over terrain, echoing its historic function as a transport animal.
minnanocraft.token.horse.example: 馬に乗って広大な平原を探索しよう。 (Uma ni notte koodaina heigen wo tansaku shiyoo.) - Let's explore the vast plains riding a horse.
minnanocraft.token.horse_1.desc: ホース (hoosu) is a katakana loan from English ‘horse’; in Minecraft it refers to the same rideable animal, with the spelling emphasizing its foreign origin.
minnanocraft.token.horse_1.example: ホースに乗って山を越えよう。 (Hoosu ni notte yama wo koeyoo.) - Ride the horse and cross the mountain.
minnanocraft.token.horse_2.desc: ウマ (uma) is the native word ‘uma’ rendered in katakana; in Minecraft it still denotes the horse, with the katakana form chosen for stylistic simplicity.
minnanocraft.token.horse_2.example: ウマと一緒に鉱山へ潜ろう。 (Uma to issho ni koozan e mogoroo.) - Let's descend into the mine together with the horse.
minnanocraft.token.donkey.desc: ロバ (roba) is a katakana loan from Portuguese ‘burro’; in Minecraft the donkey can transport items, mirroring its historical role as a pack animal.
minnanocraft.token.donkey.example: ロバに荷物を乗せて遠くへ行こう。 (Roba ni nimotsu wo nosete tooku e ikoo.) - Load the donkey with supplies and travel far.
minnanocraft.token.mule.desc: ラバ (raba) originates from Portuguese ‘mula’ and is written in katakana; in Minecraft the mule inherits traits from both horse and donkey, allowing it to carry a larger inventory.
minnanocraft.token.mule.example: ラバは荷物をたくさん運べる。 (Raba wa nimotsu wo takusan hakoberu.) - The mule can carry many items.
minnanocraft.token.llama.desc: Rama (ラマ) is a loan from Spanish 'llama'; in Minecraft it appears as a pack animal that can be ridden and carry supplies.
minnanocraft.token.llama.example: Rama ni notte yama e ikou! (Rama ni notte yama e ikou!) - Let's ride the llama to the mountain.
minnanocraft.token.camel.desc: Rakuda (ラクダ) is a loanword for camel; in Minecraft it serves as a desert mount, echoing its heat‑tolerant nature.
minnanocraft.token.camel.example: Rakuda de sabaku wo oudan shiyou! (Rakuda de sabaku wo oudan shiyou!) - Let's cross the desert on a camel.
minnanocraft.token.pig.desc: Buta (豚) employs the kanji for pig; in Minecraft the pig yields porkchop and can be ridden with a carrot on a stick.
minnanocraft.token.pig.example: Buta wo oikakete niku wo te ni ireyoo! (Buta wo oikakete niku wo te ni ireyoo!) - Chase the pig to get meat.
minnanocraft.token.pig_1.desc: Buta (ブタ) is katakana, a gairaigo for 'pig', denoting the Minecraft animal that drops pork.
minnanocraft.token.pig_1.example: Buta ga mori no naka de hashitte iru. (Buta ga mori no naka de hashitte iru.) - The pig is running in the forest.
minnanocraft.token.chicken.desc: Niwa tori (鶏) is the kanji for chicken; in Minecraft the chicken lays eggs, drops feathers and meat.
minnanocraft.token.chicken.example: Niwa tori ga tamago wo unda! (Niwa tori ga tamago wo unda!) - The chicken laid an egg!
minnanocraft.token.chicken_1.desc: Niwatori (ニワトリ) is written in katakana, a stylistic choice in Minecraft; the term combines niwa (garden) + tori (bird), mirroring the farmed bird in the game.
minnanocraft.token.chicken_1.example: ニワトリが卵を産むと、農場が活気づく。 (Niwatori ga tamago wo umu to, noojoo ga kakki dzuku.) - When the chicken lays an egg, the farm comes alive.
minnanocraft.token.chicken_2.desc: Tori (鳥) is the kanji meaning 'bird'; in Minecraft, the chicken is a bird-type mob, reinforcing the link between the character and egg‑laying mechanics.
minnanocraft.token.chicken_2.example: 鳥の羽根で作った矢は、遠くまで飛ぶ。 (Tori no hane de tsukutta ya wa, tooku made tobu.) - Arrows made from bird feathers fly far.
minnanocraft.token.rabbit.desc: Usagi (兎) is the kanji for 'rabbit'; in Minecraft, the rabbit hops swiftly, can be tamed, and provides meat when killed.
minnanocraft.token.rabbit.example: 兎は草原で速く跳ね回る。 (Usagi wa soogen de hayaku hanemawaru.) - The rabbit hops quickly across the meadow.
minnanocraft.token.rabbit_1.desc: Usagi (ウサギ) is written in katakana as a stylistic choice; it denotes the same animal as 兎, appearing as fur and food items in the game.
minnanocraft.token.rabbit_1.example: ウサギの毛皮で作った服は、寒さに強い。 (Usagi no kefu de tsukutta fuku wa, samusa ni tsuyoi.) - Clothing made from rabbit fur resists cold.
minnanocraft.token.slime.desc: Suraimu (スライム) is a katakana loanword from English 'slime'; in Minecraft, the slime is a gelatinous mob that bounces and drops experience when killed.
minnanocraft.token.slime.example: スライムは地下で跳ねながら、経験値を落とす。 (Suraimu wa chika de hanenagara, keikenchi wo otosu.) - The slime bounces underground, dropping experience points.
minnanocraft.token.feather.desc: 羽根 (hane) combines the kanji 羽 (feather) and 根 (root), literally meaning 'feather'. In Minecraft, feathers drop from chickens and are used to craft arrows.
minnanocraft.token.feather.example: 鶏が羽根 (hane) を落とすと、矢の材料になる。 (Niwa ga hane wo otosu to, ya no zairyoo ni naru.) - When a chicken drops a feather, it becomes material for arrows.
minnanocraft.token.moss.desc: 苔 (koke) is a single kanji meaning 'moss'. In Minecraft, the moss block spreads over stone, forming green, hidden areas.
minnanocraft.token.moss.example: 苔 (koke) が石に広がると、隠し通路が作れる。 (Koke ga ishi ni hirogaru to, kakushi tsuuro ga tsukureru.) - When moss spreads over stone, hidden passages can be created.
minnanocraft.token.petals.desc: 花びら (hanabira) combines 花 (hana, 'flower') with びら, a reading of 枚 (mai, flat‑object counter), meaning 'flower petal'. In Minecraft, petals are harvested from flowers for dyes.
minnanocraft.token.petals.example: 花びら (hanabira) を集めて染料を作ろう。 (Hanabira wo atsumete senryoo wo tsukuroo.) - Gather petals to craft dye.
minnanocraft.token.lily.desc: スイレン (suiren) is written in katakana, marking it as a loanword from Chinese 水蓮 ('water lily'). In Minecraft, lily pads float on water and can be stepped on.
minnanocraft.token.lily.example: スイレン (suiren) の葉は水面に浮かび、プレイヤーが踏める。 (Suiren no ha wa suimen ni ukabi, pureiyaa ga fumeru.) - Lily pads float on the water surface, letting the player step on them.
minnanocraft.token.leaves.desc: 葉 (ha) is a single kanji meaning 'leaf'. In Minecraft, leaves drop from trees, can be gathered, and act as fertilizer for soil.
minnanocraft.token.leaves.example: 葉 (ha) が落ちると、土に肥料を与える。 (Ha ga ochiru to, tsuchi ni hiryoo wo ataeru.) - When leaves fall, they fertilize the soil.
minnanocraft.token.coral.desc: サンゴ (sango) is a katakana loan from Portuguese "coral"; in Minecraft it designates the colorful marine blocks that mimic real coral reefs.
minnanocraft.token.coral.example: 海底でサンゴを育てよう (Kaitei de sango wo sodateyou) - Grow coral on the ocean floor.
minnanocraft.token.fan.desc: ウチワ (uchiwa) is the katakana rendering of the native word for a hand fan; in the mod the fan creates airflow that moves particles.
minnanocraft.token.fan.example: ウチワで炎を消す (Uchiwa de honoo wo kesu) - Use the fan to extinguish fire.
minnanocraft.token.tube.desc: クダ (kuda) is a katakana loan of "tube"; in Minecraft tubes convey items or fluids, matching the notion of a conduit.
minnanocraft.token.tube.example: クダで水を流す (Kuda de mizu wo nagasu) - Channel water through the tube.
minnanocraft.token.brain.desc: ノウ (nou) is the katakana form of "brain"; in Minecraft the Brain Coral block looks like a brain, matching its name.
minnanocraft.token.brain.example: ノウサンゴを観察する (Nou sango wo kansatsu suru) - Observe the brain coral.
minnanocraft.token.horn.desc: シカツノ (shikatuno) merges シカ (shika, "deer") and ツノ (tsuno, "horn"); it denotes a deer antler used as a horn in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.horn.example: シカツノで音を鳴らす (Shikatuno de oto wo narasu) - Blow the horn to make a sound.
minnanocraft.token.horn_1.desc: The word 角笛 (kakutei) merges 角 (kaku, “horn”) and 笛 (fue, “whistle”), matching the goat horn that emits a sound in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.horn_1.example: 山の頂で角笛を吹くと、羊が集まる。 (Yama no itadaki de kakutei wo fuku to, hitsuji ga atsumaru.) - When you blow the horn atop the mountain, sheep gather.
minnanocraft.token.flame.desc: 炎 (honoo) translates to “flame”, directly describing the fire that appears when blocks burn in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.flame.example: 洞窟の壁に炎が揺らめく。 (Doukutsu no kabe ni honoo ga yurameku.) - Flames flicker on the cave wall.
minnanocraft.token.fire_1.desc: ミレポラ (Mirepora) is rendered in katakana as a gairaigo from “Millepora”, the fire coral genus, representing the luminous coral block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.fire_1.example: 海底でミレポラを見つけると、光が広がる。 (Kaitei de Mirepora wo mitsukeru to, hikari ga hirogaru.) - Finding a fire coral underwater spreads light.
minnanocraft.token.fireproof.desc: 耐火 (taika) combines 耐 (tai, “to endure”) and 火 (ka, “fire”), naming the fire‑resistance effect that shields players in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.fireproof.example: 耐火の鎧を装備すれば、溶岩に入っても安全だ。 (Taika no yoroi wo soubi sureba, yougan ni haitte mo anzen da.) - Wearing fire‑proof armor keeps you safe even in lava.
minnanocraft.token.water.desc: 水 (mizu) translates to “water”, denoting the fluid that fills rivers, lakes, and oceans in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.water.example: 川の水は常に流れ続ける。 (Kawa no mizu wa tsune ni nagare tsuzukeru.) - The river water keeps flowing forever.
minnanocraft.token.underwater.desc: 水中 (suichuu) merges 水 'water' and 中 'inside', literally meaning being inside water, matching the player’s state when swimming in water blocks.
minnanocraft.token.underwater.example: 潜って水中の洞窟へ向かう (mogutte suichuu no doukutsu e mukau) - Dive and head towards the underwater cave.
minnanocraft.token.bubble.desc: 気泡 (kifuu) combines 気 'air/energy' and 泡 'bubble', referring to the bubbles that appear when breathing underwater.
minnanocraft.token.bubble.example: 気泡が上昇し、光を反射する (kifuu ga joushou shi, hikari wo hansha suru) - Bubbles rise and reflect light.
minnanocraft.token.bubble_1.desc: ミズタマ (mizutama) is written in katakana, a stylized loanword evoking 'mizu' (water) and 'tama' (sphere), used for small water spheres in the mod.
minnanocraft.token.bubble_1.example: ミズタマが水面に跳ね返る (mizutama ga suimen ni hanekaeru) - Mizutama bounce on the water surface.
minnanocraft.token.glazed.desc: 彩釉 (saiyuu) merges 彩 'color' and 釉 'glaze', describing blocks with a colored vitreous finish, like glazed tiles in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.glazed.example: 彩釉のタイルが光を受けて輝く (saiyuu no tairu ga hikari wo ukete kagayaku) - Glazed tiles shine as they catch the light.
minnanocraft.token.harness.desc: ハーネス (haanesu) is a katakana gairaigo from English 'harness', indicating equipment that secures animals to the player.
minnanocraft.token.harness.example: ハーネスを装着した馬が速く走る (haanesu wo souchaku shita uma ga hayaku hashiru) - A horse wearing a harness runs fast.
minnanocraft.token.saddle.desc: The term 鞍 (ara) merges 馬 (uma, horse) with the radical 卩, denoting a seat, mirroring the item that lets players ride horses and other mobs in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.saddle.example: 馬に鞍を装着したら、速く走れる。 (Uma ni ara wo soochaku shitara, hayaku hashireru.) - When you equip a saddle on a horse, it runs faster.
minnanocraft.token.nether.desc: ネザー (Nezaa) is a katakana transcription of the English 'Nether', naming the fiery dimension in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.nether.example: ネザーへポータルを作ったら、危険が待っている。 (Nezaa e pootaru wo tsukuttara, kiken ga matte iru.) - When you build a portal to the Nether, danger awaits.
minnanocraft.token.star.desc: 星 (hoshi) means 'star', matching the item that emits light when placed or used in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.star.example: 夜に星を投げると、光が広がる。 (Yoru ni hoshi wo nageru to, hikari ga hirogaru.) - Throwing a star at night spreads light.
minnanocraft.token.star_1.desc: スター (sutaa) is a katakana rendering of 'star', referring to the luminous item in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.star_1.example: スカイライトの近くでスターを使うと、光が増える。 (Sukairaito no chikaku de sutaa wo tsukau to, hikari ga fueru.) - Using the star near a skylight boosts the light level.
minnanocraft.token.honey.desc: ハチミツ (hachimitsu) is written in katakana but derives from the native term 蜂蜜, where 蜂 (hachi) means 'bee' and 蜜 (mitsu) means 'nectar', describing the honey produced by bees in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.honey.example: ハチミツのブロックを壊すと、粘着性の液体が出る。 (Hachimitsu no buroku wo kowasu to, nenchakusei no ekitai ga deru.) - Breaking a honey block releases a sticky liquid.
minnanocraft.token.honeycomb.desc: ハニカム (hanikamu) is a katakana loan from English "honeycomb", mirroring the hexagonal cells used for beehives in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.honeycomb.example: ハニカムのブロックを置いて、ミツバチの巣を作ろう (Hanikamu no burokku wo oite, mitsubachi no su wo tsukurou) - Place a honeycomb block to build a beehive.
minnanocraft.token.head.desc: 頭 (atama) employs the kanji 頁 meaning "head" or "surface", denoting the upper part of the body; in Minecraft, the "head" block replicates a player or mob's head.
minnanocraft.token.head.example: 頭のブロックを壁に貼って、装飾しよう (Atama no burokku wo kabe ni hatte, sooshoku shiyou) - Attach a head block to a wall for decoration.
minnanocraft.token.head_1.desc: ヘッド (heddo) is a katakana loan from English "head", referring to the head block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.head_1.example: ヘッドブロックでモブの頭を展示しよう (Heddo burokku de mobu no atama wo tenji shiyou) - Display a mob's head using a head block.
minnanocraft.token.skull.desc: 頭蓋骨 (zugaikotsu) merges 頭 (atama, "head"), 蓋 (gai, "cover"), and 骨 (kotsu, "bone"), describing the bone covering the brain; in Minecraft, the "skull" block depicts this bone.
minnanocraft.token.skull.example: 頭蓋骨を地面に置いて、ゾンビを驚かせよう (Zugaikotsu wo jimen ni oite, zonbi wo odorokaseyou) - Place a skull on the ground to scare zombies.
minnanocraft.token.skull_1.desc: 骸骨 (gaikotsu) joins 骸 (gai, "skeleton") and 骨 (kotsu, "bone"), referring to a complete skeleton; in Minecraft, the "skull_1" block displays a skeleton skull.
minnanocraft.token.skull_1.example: 骸骨の頭を壁に貼って、暗い洞窟を飾ろう (Gaikotsu no atama wo kabe ni hatte, kurai dookutsu wo kazarou) - Hang a skeleton skull on a wall to adorn a dark cave.
minnanocraft.token.coarse.desc: The adjective 粗い (arai) means "rough" or "infertile"; in Minecraft, the "coarse dirt" block has a gritty texture and prevents crops from growing, mirroring the meaning.
minnanocraft.token.coarse.example: この粗い土は作物を育てにくい。(Kono arai tsuchi wa sakumotsu wo sodate nikui.) - This coarse dirt makes it hard to grow crops.
minnanocraft.token.grass.desc: 草 (kusa) means "grass"; in Minecraft, the grass block covers dirt and spreads, representing typical vegetation.
minnanocraft.token.grass.example: 草ブロックの上に立つと、風の音が聞こえる。(Kusa burokku no ue ni tatsu to, kaze no oto ga kikoeru.) - Standing on a grass block, you can hear the sound of wind.
minnanocraft.token.soul_soil.desc: ソウルソイル (Souru Soiru) is a katakana loan of "Soul Soil"; in the game, this soil appears in soul biomes and allows spectral creatures to respawn, reflecting its name.
minnanocraft.token.soul_soil.example: ソウルソイルの上で、魂の炎が揺らめく。(Souru Soiru no ue de, tamashii no honoo ga yureruku.) - Above the Soul Soil, the souls' flames flicker.
minnanocraft.token.carpet.desc: カーペット (Kaapetto) is a katakana loan of "carpet"; in Minecraft, it functions as a decorative floor block, just like a carpet.
minnanocraft.token.carpet.example: カーペットを敷いて、部屋を暖かくした。(Kaapetto wo shiite, heya wo atatakaku shita.) - I laid a carpet to warm the room.
minnanocraft.token.bottle.desc: 瓶 (bin) combines the radicals 皿 (plate) and 匕 (spoon) to form "bottle"; in Minecraft, the bottle stores water or potions, reflecting its function as a container.
minnanocraft.token.bottle.example: 瓶に入れた水は、遠くの拠点へ持ち運べる。(Bin ni ireta mizu wa, tooku no kyoten e mochihakoberu.) - Water in a bottle can be carried to distant bases.
minnanocraft.token.ocelot.desc: Yamaneko (ヤマネコ) is rendered in katakana, a stylistic choice in Minecraft. It combines 山 (yama, “mountain”) and 猫 (neko, “cat”), literally “mountain cat”. This matches the wild feline that spawns in jungles, resembling a small mountain cat.
minnanocraft.token.ocelot.example: ヤマネコがジャングルで潜んでいる (Yamaneko ga janguru de hisonde iru) - The ocelot is lurking in the jungle.
minnanocraft.token.lectern.desc: Shokken-dai (書見台) merges 書 (sho, “writing/book”), 見 (ken, “to see”), and 台 (dai, “stand”). It denotes a stand for viewing books, precisely the lectern’s role of holding and displaying books for reading.
minnanocraft.token.lectern.example: 書見台に本を置くと光が当たる (Shokken-dai ni hon wo oku to hikari ga ataru) - Placing a book on the lectern makes light shine.
minnanocraft.token.name_tag.desc: Nafuda (名札) combines 名 (na, “name”) and 札 (fuda, “tag”). It directly describes the item used to assign names to entities in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.name_tag.example: 名札で狼に「影」(Kage)と名付けた (Nafuda de ookami ni “Kage” to nadzuketa) - I named the wolf “Shadow” with a name tag.
minnanocraft.token.ladder.desc: Hashigo (はしご) is presented in hiragana, a native Japanese term meaning “ladder”. In Minecraft it enables vertical movement between blocks.
minnanocraft.token.ladder.example: はしごで塔の上まで登った (Hashigo de too no ue made nobotta) - I climbed to the top of the tower using the ladder.
minnanocraft.token.shard.desc: Kakera (欠片) merges 欠 (kaku, “lack”) with 片 (hen, “piece”), meaning “fragment”. In Minecraft shards represent tiny pieces of resources such as netherite or prismarine.
minnanocraft.token.shard.example: 欠片を集めて新しい道具を作る (Kakera wo atsumete atarashii doogu wo tsukuru) - Collecting shards to craft new tools.
minnanocraft.token.dragon.desc: ドラゴン (doragon) is a katakana loanword mirroring the English “dragon”, a mythical beast. In Minecraft, the Ender Dragon embodies this massive creature, soaring above the End portal and serving as the final boss.
minnanocraft.token.dragon.example: ドラゴンが空を舞う (doragon ga sora wo mau) - The dragon soars through the sky
minnanocraft.token.ender.desc: エンダー (endaa) is a katakana gairaigo meaning “ender”, a term for the End dimension in games. In Minecraft, Ender blocks and items reference this far‑off realm.
minnanocraft.token.ender.example: エンダーのポータルを開く (endaa no pootaru wo hiraku) - Open the End portal
minnanocraft.token.pearl.desc: パール (paaru) is a katakana transcription of the English “pearl”. In Minecraft, the Ender Pearl is dropped by the Ender Dragon and lets players teleport across distances.
minnanocraft.token.pearl.example: パールでテレポートする (paaru de terepooto suru) - Teleport using the pearl
minnanocraft.token.tear.desc: 涙 (namida) merges the water radical 氵 (sanzui) with the eye kanji 目 (me), denoting a drop from the eye. In Minecraft, the Ghast Tear mirrors this meaning as a rare drop from Ghasts.
minnanocraft.token.tear.example: 涙が地面に落ちる (namida ga jimen ni ochiru) - Tears fall onto the ground
minnanocraft.token.spawn_egg.desc: スポーンエッグ (supoon eggu) blends the English words “spawn” and “egg” into katakana, signifying an item that creates entities. In Minecraft, a Spawn Egg lets players summon mobs instantly.
minnanocraft.token.spawn_egg.example: スポーンエッグでゾンビを呼び出す (supoon eggu de zonbi wo yobi dasu) - Summon a zombie with the spawn egg
minnanocraft.token.monster.desc: モンスター (monsutaa) is a katakana loan from English 'monster'. In Minecraft it denotes hostile mobs that attack the player, matching the original meaning of a frightening creature.
minnanocraft.token.monster.example: モンスターが洞窟から現れた！ (Monsutaa ga dookoo kara arawareta!) - Monsters emerged from the cave!
minnanocraft.token.spawner.desc: スポナー (supoonaa) is a katakana loan of 'spawner'. The block creates mobs, aligning with the notion of a monster generator.
minnanocraft.token.spawner.example: スポナーが夜になるとモンスターを召喚する。 (Supoonaa ga yoru ni naru to monsutaa wo shookan suru.) - The spawner summons monsters at night.
minnanocraft.token.target.desc: 的 (まと, mato) uses the kanji 的 meaning 'target' or 'mark'. In Minecraft the target block records projectile hits, matching the idea of a point of aim.
minnanocraft.token.target.example: 的に矢を当てた！ (Mato ni ya wo ateta!) - Hit the arrow on the target.
minnanocraft.token.rocket.desc: ロケット (roketto) is a katakana loan of 'rocket'. In the game the firework rocket lifts the player, evoking vertical flight.
minnanocraft.token.rocket.example: ロケットで空へ飛び立った。 (Roketto de sora e tobitatta.) - I launched into the sky with a rocket.
minnanocraft.token.firework.desc: 花火 (はなび, hanabi) combines 花 'flower' and 火 'fire', suggesting colorful bursts like fire‑flowers. In Minecraft the item produces bright explosions.
minnanocraft.token.firework.example: 花火が夜空に咲いた。 (Hanabi ga yoru sora ni saita.) - Fireworks bloomed in the night sky.
minnanocraft.token.bell.desc: 鐘 (kane) merges 金 (metal) and 中 (center), denoting a metal object that sounds from its core; in Minecraft the bell is a metal block that rings when triggered by players or mobs.
minnanocraft.token.bell.example: 鐘が鳴ると、村人が集まる。 (Kane ga naru to, murabito ga atsumaru.) - When the bell rings, villagers gather.
minnanocraft.token.paper.desc: 紙 (kami) historically merges 糸 (thread) and 帛 (silk), denoting a fiber material; in Minecraft paper is crafted from sugarcane and used for maps and books.
minnanocraft.token.paper.example: 紙で地図を作ると、冒険が楽になる。 (Kami de chizu wo tsukuru to, booken ga raku ni naru.) - Making a map with paper makes adventure easier.
minnanocraft.token.stem.desc: 幹 (miki) merges 木 (tree) and 干 (dry), denoting the main trunk; in Minecraft the stem is the basic log block of trees.
minnanocraft.token.stem.example: 幹を切って木材を集めよう。 (Miki wo kitte mokuzai wo atsumeyoo.) - Cut the stem to gather wood.
minnanocraft.token.stem_1.desc: 柄 (gara) combines 木 (tree) and 手 (hand), signifying a wooden handle; in Minecraft the handle connects the tool head to the player.
minnanocraft.token.stem_1.example: 木の柄でピッケルを作ると、採掘が速くなる。 (Ki no gara de pikkeru wo tsukuru to, saikutsu ga hayaku naru.) - Crafting a pickaxe with a wooden handle speeds up mining.
minnanocraft.token.stem_2.desc: 茎 (kuki) merges 艹 (grass) and 干 (dry), denoting a plant stalk; in Minecraft melon and pumpkin stems grow from seeds.
minnanocraft.token.stem_2.example: 茎が成長すると、メロンが収穫できる。 (Kuki ga seichoo suru to, meron ga shuukaku dekiru.) - When the stem matures, the melon can be harvested.
minnanocraft.token.wart.desc: Wooto (ウォート) is a gairaigo from English “wart”, referring to the red, bump‑like plant that grows on soul sand in the Nether, mirroring the texture of real warts.
minnanocraft.token.wart.example: Gather Wooto (ウォート) in the Nether to brew potions.
minnanocraft.token.hyphae.desc: Kinshi (菌糸) merges kin (fungus) and shi (thread), literally “fungus thread”, matching the block Hyphae that looks like a network of fungal filaments in the game.
minnanocraft.token.hyphae.example: Locate Kinshi (菌糸) in caves and mine the hyphae block.
minnanocraft.token.knowledge.desc: Chie (知恵) combines chi (knowledge) and e (blessing), literally “blessed knowledge”; the Knowledge Book in Minecraft stores recipes that unlock new crafting options, embodying this concept.
minnanocraft.token.knowledge.example: Use a Chie (知恵) book at the enchantment table to learn new recipes.
minnanocraft.token.muddy.desc: Dorodarake (泥だらけ) merges doro (mud) with the suffix -darake, meaning “covered in mud”; blocks such as muddy mangrove roots acquire this description when waterlogged.
minnanocraft.token.muddy.example: Locate Dorodarake (泥だらけ) roots by the river and mine them.
minnanocraft.token.mud.desc: Doro (泥) translates to “mud”; Minecraft’s Mud block can be crafted and later dried into clay, mirroring the real‑world conversion.
minnanocraft.token.mud.example: Collect Doro (泥) to craft mud blocks and dry them into clay.
minnanocraft.token.resin.desc: The term 樹脂 (jushi) merges 樹 (tree) and 脂 (fat/oil), meaning “tree oil”; in Minecraft resin drops from logs, mirroring its botanical source.
minnanocraft.token.resin.example: 樹脂が滴る木を見つけた (Jushi ga shizuru ki wo mitsuketa) - I found a tree dripping resin.
minnanocraft.token.mourner.desc: 哀悼者 (aitoosha) combines 哀 (sorrow) + 悼 (mourn) + 者 (person), “one who mourns”; in Minecraft the Mourner wanders near graves, embodying grief.
minnanocraft.token.mourner.example: 哀悼者が墓のそばで黙って立っている (Aitoosha ga haka no soba de damatte tatteiru) - The mourner stands silently beside the tomb.
minnanocraft.token.plenty.desc: 富 (fu) translates to “wealth” or “plenty”; in Minecraft the Plenty token marks chests overflowing with loot, echoing abundance.
minnanocraft.token.plenty.example: 富の宝箱を開けたらダイヤが山ほど出た (Fu no takarabako wo aketara daiya ga yama hodo deta) - Opening the chest of plenty yielded a mountain of diamonds.
minnanocraft.token.enchanted.desc: エンチャント (enchanto) is a katakana gairaigo from English “enchant”; in Minecraft it labels items that possess magical effects, such as enchanted gear.
minnanocraft.token.enchanted.example: エンチャントされた剣でドラゴンを倒した (Enchanto sareta ken de doragon wo taoshita) - I slayed the dragon with an enchanted sword.
minnanocraft.token.cracked.desc: The term ひび割 (hibi-wari) merges ひび (crack sound) and 割 (split), meaning “cracked”; in Minecraft cracked blocks show visible fissures, matching the word.
minnanocraft.token.cracked.example: ひび割れた石ブロックを修復した (Hibiwareta ishi burokku wo shuufuku shita) - I repaired the cracked stone block.
minnanocraft.token.damaged.desc: The word 壊れかけ (kowarekake) merges 壊 (kowasu, “to break”) with かけ (kake, “partial”), meaning partially broken. In Minecraft, items such as a damaged anvil show cracks that reflect this condition.
minnanocraft.token.damaged.example: 壊れかけの金床を修理しよう (Kowarekake no kinshoo wo shuuri shiyoo) - Let's repair the damaged anvil.
minnanocraft.token.dried.desc: 乾燥 (kansoo) combines 乾 (kan, “dry”) and 燥 (soo, “dryness”), meaning “drying”. In Minecraft, the dried kelp block is a fuel source and looks desiccated.
minnanocraft.token.dried.example: 乾燥した海藻ブロックを燃料に使える (Kansoo shita kaisoo burokku wo nenryoo ni tsukaeru) - You can use the dried kelp block as fuel.
minnanocraft.token.polished.desc: 磨かれた (migakareta) comes from 磨 (migaku, “to polish”) plus the passive suffix かれた, meaning “polished”. In Minecraft, Polished Deepslate reflects light because of its smooth surface.
minnanocraft.token.polished.example: 磨かれた深層岩は光を反射する (Migakareta shinsoogan wa hikari wo hansha suru) - The Polished Deepslate reflects light.
minnanocraft.token.oxidized.desc: 酸化 (sanka) merges 酸 (san, “acid”) with 化 (ka, “change”), meaning “oxidation”. In Minecraft, oxidized copper turns a green hue.
minnanocraft.token.oxidized.example: 酸化した銅ブロックは緑色に変わる (Sanka shita doo burokku wa midori-iro ni kawaru) - The oxidized copper block turns green.
minnanocraft.token.exposed.desc: 風化 (fuuka) combines 風 (fuu, “wind”) with 化 (ka, “change”), meaning “weathering”. In Minecraft, exposed copper is the initial weathered stage, still retaining some sheen.
minnanocraft.token.exposed.example: 風化した銅はまだ光沢がある (Fuuka shita doo wa mada kootaku ga aru) - The exposed copper still has a sheen.
minnanocraft.token.waxed.desc: 錆止め (sabi tome) merges 錆 (sabi) ‘rust’ and 止め (tome) ‘stop’, describing blocks that prevent oxidation, matching waxed blocks that stay rust‑free in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.waxed.example: この錆止めのブロックは雨でも錆びない。 (Kono sabitome no burokkku wa ame demo sabinai.) - This waxed block doesn't rust even in rain.
minnanocraft.token.weathered.desc: 錆びた (sabita) consists of 錆び (sabi) ‘rust’ plus the past suffix た, meaning ‘rusted’; in Minecraft, weathered copper shows the green patina of oxidation.
minnanocraft.token.weathered.example: 錆びた銅の階段は時間とともに色が変わる。 (Sabita dou no kaidan wa jikan to tomo ni iro ga kawaru.) - Weathered copper stairs change color over time.
minnanocraft.token.stripped.desc: を剥いだ (wo hakuida) uses 剥く (haku) ‘to peel’ with the past form いだ, meaning ‘peeled’; stripped logs in Minecraft have their bark removed, exposing a smooth core.
minnanocraft.token.stripped.example: 木を剥いだ後、表面は滑らかになる。 (Ki wo hakuida ato, hyomen wa nameraka ni naru.) - After stripping the wood, the surface becomes smooth.
minnanocraft.token.infested.desc: 虫食い (mushikui) combines 虫 (mushi) ‘insect’ and 食い (kui) ‘eating’, literally ‘eaten by insects’; infested blocks hide silverfish that emerge when mined.
minnanocraft.token.infested.example: 虫食いの石は銀魚が潜んでいる。 (Mushikui no ishi wa gin'gyo ga hisonde iru.) - Infested stone hides silverfish.
minnanocraft.token.tipped.desc: 効能 (kounou) merges 効 (kou) ‘effect’ and 能 (nou) ‘ability’, denoting a potion’s effect; tipped arrows carry this ‘efficacy’ in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.tipped.example: 効能のある矢は敵に特別な効果を与える。 (Kounou no aru ya wa teki ni tokubetsu na kouka wo ataeru.) - Tipped arrows give enemies a special effect.
minnanocraft.token.primary.desc: The kanji 主 (shu) means 'primary' or 'master'. In Minecraft, the "primary" item acts as the central component of a mechanism, mirroring this meaning.
minnanocraft.token.primary.example: この装置の主 (shu) はレッドストーンです。 (kono souchi no shu wa redstone desu.) - The primary component of this device is redstone.
minnanocraft.token.ignition.desc: Ignition is expressed by 着火 (chakuka), where 着 (chaku) means 'to set' and 火 (ka) means 'fire', denoting the start of combustion. In Minecraft, "ignition" refers to using flint and steel to start fire.
minnanocraft.token.ignition.example: 火打石で着火 (chakuka) できる。 (hiuchishou de chakuka dekiru.) - You can ignite with flint and steel.
minnanocraft.token.propagule.desc: Propagule is written 零余子 (rei yoko), combining 零 (rei, 'zero/remaining'), 余 (yo, 'excess'), and 子 (shi, 'seed'), meaning a leftover seed. In Minecraft, a "propagule" is the item that sprouts a tree when placed.
minnanocraft.token.propagule.example: 零余子 (rei yoko) を植えると木が育つ。 (rei yoko wo ueru to ki ga sodatsu.) - Planting a propagule grows a tree.
minnanocraft.token.quill.desc: Quill is expressed as 羽根ペン (hane pen), where 羽根 (hane) means 'feather' and ペン (pen) is a gairaigo from English 'pen'. In Minecraft, a "quill" is used to write in enchanted books.
minnanocraft.token.quill.example: 羽根ペン (hane pen) で本に書く。 (hane pen de hon ni kaku.) - Write in a book with a quill.
minnanocraft.token.peculiar.desc: Peculiar is written 奇妙 (kimyou), merging 奇 (ki, 'odd') and 妙 (myou, 'mysterious'), yielding 'odd' or 'strange'. In Minecraft, a "peculiar" effect may denote unusual status or oddly shaped blocks.
minnanocraft.token.peculiar.example: 奇妙な光が洞窟に漂う。 (kimyou na hikari ga doukutsu ni tadayou.) - A peculiar light drifts through the cave.
minnanocraft.token.common.desc: "ありふれた" (arifureta) translates to "common"; it comes from あり (to exist) + ふれる (to spread), reflecting items that are plentiful, such as stone blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.common.example: このブロックはありふれた石です。 (Kono burokkku wa arifureta ishi desu.) - This block is a common stone.
minnanocraft.token.thick.desc: 濃厚 (noukou) merges 濃 (dense) and 厚 (thick), describing a highly concentrated substance; in Minecraft it can describe a potion or slime block with a strong effect.
minnanocraft.token.thick.example: 濃厚なスープは体力を回復させる。 (Noukou na suupu wa tai-ryoku wo kaifuku saseru.) - The thick soup restores health.
minnanocraft.token.creaking.desc: クリーキング (kuriikingu) is a katakana loanword from English "creaking", describing the squeaking sound of wooden doors or stairs in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.creaking.example: ドアがクリーキングと鳴る。 (Doa ga kuriikingu to naru.) - The door creaks.
minnanocraft.token.heartbreak.desc: 傷心 (shoushin) merges 傷 (wound) and 心 (heart), meaning "heartbreak"; in Minecraft it can be felt when valuable items are lost.
minnanocraft.token.heartbreak.example: 宝箱が空で、傷心になる。 (Houkou ga kara de, shoushin ni naru.) - The chest is empty, causing heartbreak.
minnanocraft.token.stand.desc: 立て (tate) derives from the kanji 立 (to stand) and denotes the act of placing or supporting; in Minecraft it applies to blocks that act as stands, such as torch placements.
minnanocraft.token.stand.example: 松明を立てて光を得よう。 (Shoumei wo tatete hikari wo eyou.) - Place the torch to get light.
minnanocraft.token.pane.desc: 板 (ita) translates to "board"; a Minecraft pane is a thin board‑like glass piece, matching the literal sense.
minnanocraft.token.pane.example: ガラスの板をドアの横に置く。 (Garasu no ita wo doa no yoko ni oku.) - Place the glass pane next to the door.
minnanocraft.token.glass.desc: ガラス (garasu) is a katakana loanword from English "glass", denoting the transparent block that reflects light.
minnanocraft.token.glass.example: ガラスのブロックが太陽の光を反射する。 (Garasu no burokku ga taiyou no hikari wo hansha suru.) - The glass block reflects sunlight.
minnanocraft.token.stained.desc: 色付き (irotsuki) merges 色 (iro, "color") and 付 (tsuku, "attach"), meaning "colored", fitting the stained‑glass mechanic.
minnanocraft.token.stained.example: 色付きガラスは洞窟を彩る。 (Irotsuki garasu wa doukutsu wo irodoru.) - Stained glass decorates the cave.
minnanocraft.token.pattern.desc: 模様 (moyou) combines 模 (mo, "model") and 様 (you, "appearance"), denoting a decorative design, matching chiseled or patterned blocks.
minnanocraft.token.pattern.example: 模様のブロックは建築に個性を与える。 (Moyou no bukku wa kenchiku ni kosei wo ataeru.) - Patterned blocks give personality to builds.
minnanocraft.token.powered.desc: パワード (pawaado) is a katakana loan from English "powered", describing blocks that receive redstone energy.
minnanocraft.token.powered.example: レッドストーンでパワードされたドアが開く。 (Reddo sutoon de pawaado sareta doa ga aku.) - The door powered by redstone opens.
minnanocraft.token.attached.desc: The kanji 付 (tsu) means 'to attach' or 'to affix', mirroring how torches or signs are fixed to surfaces in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.attached.example: 松明が壁に付いている。 (Shoomei ga kabe ni tsuite iru.) - The torch is attached to the wall.
minnanocraft.token.activator.desc: アクティベーター (akutibētaa) is a gairaigo from English 'activator', referring to the rail that powers Redstone mechanisms.
minnanocraft.token.activator.example: レッドストーンのアクティベーターがレールを作動させる。 (Reddo sutoon no akutibētaa ga rēru wo sadoo saseru.) - The Redstone activator powers the rail.
minnanocraft.token.sticky.desc: 粘着 (nenchaku) merges 粘 (nen, 'sticky') and 着 (chaku, 'to attach'), describing pistons that cling to blocks.
minnanocraft.token.sticky.example: 粘着ピストンがブロックを引き寄せる。 (Nenchaku piston ga burokkku wo hikiyoseru.) - The sticky piston pulls the block.
minnanocraft.token.dry.desc: 枯れ (kare) means 'withered' or 'dry', fitting for blocks such as dried cactus or dead wood in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.dry.example: 枯れたサボテンは乾いている。 (Kareta saboten wa kawaite iru.) - The dried cactus is dry.
minnanocraft.token.suspicious.desc: 怪しげな (ayashigena) derives from 怪 (kai, 'mysterious') plus the adjective suffix, denoting something suspicious, like suspicious sand that uncovers loot.
minnanocraft.token.suspicious.example: 怪しげな砂は宝を隠す。 (Ayashigena suna wa takara wo kakusu.) - Suspicious sand hides treasure.
minnanocraft.token.spectral.desc: 光 (hikari) means 'light'. In Minecraft, spectral blocks emit a glow akin to light sources, mirroring the literal meaning. The term also appears as スペクトル (supekutoru), a gairaigo for 'spectral'.
minnanocraft.token.spectral.example: 光のスペクトルが洞窟を照らす (Hikari no supekutoru ga doukutsu wo terasu) - The spectral light illuminates the cave.
minnanocraft.token.smooth.desc: 滑らかな (namerakana) combines 滑 (suberu, 'to slip') with the adjective suffix らかな, meaning 'smooth'. In Minecraft, smooth blocks lower friction, allowing carts and entities to glide more easily.
minnanocraft.token.smooth.example: 滑らかなレールでトロッコが速く走る (Namerakana reeru de torokko ga hayaku hashiru) - The smooth rails let the minecart run fast.
minnanocraft.token.sweet.desc: スイート (suiito) is a katakana loanword from English 'sweet', describing sweet items. In Minecraft, sweet blocks lure bees and serve as ingredients in recipes.
minnanocraft.token.sweet.example: スイートブロックが蜂を引き寄せる (Suiito burokku ga hachi wo hikiyoseru) - The sweet block attracts bees.
minnanocraft.token.wet.desc: 濡 (nure) means 'wet', composed of the water radical 氵 and the element 湿. In Minecraft, wet blocks create slippery surfaces that affect movement.
minnanocraft.token.wet.example: 濡れた石が滑りやすい (Nureta ishi ga suberiyasui) - The wet stone is slippery.
minnanocraft.token.cut.desc: 切り込み入り (kirikomi-iri) combines 切 (kiru, 'to cut') + 込み (komi, 'insertion') + 入り (iri, 'entry'), indicating a block with cut grooves. In Minecraft, cut stones have sharp edges useful for decoration or tools.
minnanocraft.token.cut.example: 切り込み入りの石が剣の装飾になる (Kirikomi-iri no ishi ga ken no soushoku ni naru) - The cut stone becomes a sword decoration.
minnanocraft.token.cut_1.desc: The kanji 研 (ken) means "to sharpen"; it suggests a polished blade that can cut blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.cut_1.example: 研がれた石の刃で木を切る (Togareta ishi no ha de ki wo kiru) - I cut wood with a polished stone blade.
minnanocraft.token.slice.desc: 薄 (usu) means "thin" and 切り (kiri) derives from 切る "to cut"; together 薄切り (usugiri) denotes thin slices, like sliced meat or cake in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.slice.example: 薄切りのパンを食べると満腹度が上がる (Usugiri no pan wo taberu to manpuku-do ga agaru) - Eating thin slices of bread raises hunger.
minnanocraft.token.brewer.desc: 醸 (jou) means "to brew", 造 (zou) "to make" and 家 (ka) denotes a person; 醸造家 (jouzouka) is the potion maker, akin to the brewer in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.brewer.example: 醸造家はポーションを作る (Jouzouka wa po-shon wo tsukuru) - The brewer crafts potions.
minnanocraft.token.dead.desc: 死 (shi) means "death"; the past form 死んだ (shinda) describes something that has died, like dead mobs that drop loot.
minnanocraft.token.dead.example: 死んだゾンビはドロップを残す (Shinda zonbi wa doroppu wo nokosu) - A dead zombie leaves a drop.
minnanocraft.token.shelter.desc: 木 (ki) means "tree" and 陰 (kage) "shade"; 木陰 (kokage) refers to the shade of a tree, serving as shelter from sunlight and hostile mobs.
minnanocraft.token.shelter.example: 木陰で夜を過ごすとモブが近づかない (Kokage de yoru wo sugosu to mobu ga chikazukanai) - Spending night in the tree's shade keeps mobs away.
minnanocraft.token.flow.desc: Uzumaki combines 渦 (vortex) and 巻き (coil), describing the swirling motion of water or redstone currents that coil like a spiral in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.flow.example: Uzumaki no suiryuu ga dookutsu wo mitasu. (Uzumaki no suiryuu ga dookutsu wo mitasu.) - The spiral water flow fills the cave.
minnanocraft.token.whirlwind.desc: Senpuu merges 旋 (rotation) and 風 (wind), referring to a particle whirlwind or fast‑circulating wind around a block, akin to a tornado in the game.
minnanocraft.token.whirlwind.example: Senpuu ga sabaku no too wo fukitobasu. (Senpuu ga sabaku no too wo fukitobasu.) - The whirlwind blows away the desert tower.
minnanocraft.token.trial.desc: Shiren combines 試 (test) and 練 (training), indicating a challenge or trial the player must overcome, like the trial chambers in adventure structures.
minnanocraft.token.trial.example: Shiren no saidan de yuusha wa shiren wo ukeru. (Shiren no saidan de yuusha wa shiren wo ukeru.) - The hero undergoes the trial at the trial altar.
minnanocraft.token.danger.desc: Kyooi merges 脅 (threat) and 威 (might), used to denote imminent danger, such as a Creeper that explodes when near.
minnanocraft.token.danger.example: Kyooi no kurīpaa ga chikazuku. (Kyooi no kurīpaa ga chikazuku.) - The threatening creeper approaches.
minnanocraft.token.gap.desc: Ma means space or interval, applicable to the gap between blocks or the narrow corridor the player must cross.
minnanocraft.token.gap.example: Dookutsu no ma ni hikari ga sasu. (Dookutsu no ma ni hikari ga sasu.) - Light shines through the gap in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.gilded.desc: きらめく (kirameku) means 'to sparkle', matching the shimmering appearance of gilded blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.gilded.example: 洞窟の奥で金の装飾がきらめく (Doukutsu no oku de kin no sooshoku ga kirameku) - Deep in the cave, the gilded decorations sparkle.
minnanocraft.token.explorer.desc: 探検家 (tankenka) combines 探 (search) + 検 (investigate) + 家 (person), describing a person who searches and investigates new territories, akin to a player exploring maps in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.explorer.example: 探検家は新しいバイオームを探検する (Tankenka wa atarashii baioomu wo tanken suru) - The explorer surveys a new biome.
minnanocraft.token.howl.desc: 遠吠え (toobooe) merges 遠 (far) and 吠 (howl), indicating a howl that carries over distance, like wolves' cries at night in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.howl.example: 夜になると狼が遠吠えする (Yoru ni naru to ookami ga toobooe suru) - When night falls, wolves howl.
minnanocraft.token.globe.desc: 地球 (chikyuu) combines 地 (earth) and 球 (sphere), literally 'earth sphere', reflecting the globe item representing the planet in the game.
minnanocraft.token.globe.example: 地図を広げると地球が見える (Chizu wo hirogeru to chikyuu ga mieru) - When you unfold the map, the globe appears.
minnanocraft.token.happy.desc: ハッピー (happī) is a loanword from English 'happy' written in katakana, used to denote a cheerful state, like the happiness effect in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.happy.example: ハッピーな村人がプレイヤーに笑う (Happī na murabito ga pureiyaa ni warau) - A happy villager smiles at the player.
minnanocraft.token.ominous.desc: Fukitsu na (不吉な) merges 不 (not) with 吉 (auspicious), meaning "not auspicious"; in Minecraft, dark biomes or ominous structures convey a threatening vibe.
minnanocraft.token.ominous.example: 不吉な洞窟は危険だ (Fukitsu na doukutsu wa kiken da) - The ominous cave is dangerous.
minnanocraft.token.miner.desc: Koufu (鉱夫) combines 鉱 (ore) and 夫 (man), literally "ore man", denoting the worker who mines blocks.
minnanocraft.token.miner.example: 鉱夫は石炭を掘る (Koufu wa sekitan wo horu) - The miner extracts coal.
minnanocraft.token.elder.desc: Erudaa (エルダー) is katakana for the English loanword "elder", naming the mob that guards villages in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.elder.example: エルダーが村を守る (Erudaa ga mura wo mamoru) - The elder guards the village.
minnanocraft.token.cooked.desc: Yaki (焼き) comes from the kanji 焼 (to grill) plus the nominalizer き, indicating something grilled; in Minecraft, cooked foods restore more hunger.
minnanocraft.token.cooked.example: 焼き魚は美味しい (Yaki sakana wa oishii) - Grilled fish is tasty.
minnanocraft.token.popped.desc: Yaita (焼いた) is the past tense of yaku (焼く, to roast); it denotes something that has been cooked, e.g., popped corn.
minnanocraft.token.popped.example: 焼いたトウモロコシはポップコーンだ (Yaita toumorokoshi wa poppukoon da) - Popped corn is roasted corn.
minnanocraft.token.reinforced.desc: 強化 (kyooka) merges 強 (kyoo, strength) and 化 (ka, change), denoting increased durability; in Minecraft, reinforced blocks have higher resistance to explosions.
minnanocraft.token.reinforced.example: この壁は強化されたので、爆発に耐える。 (kono kabe wa kyooka sareta node, bakuhatsu ni taeru.) - This wall is reinforced and withstands explosions.
minnanocraft.token.hanging.desc: 吊り (tsuri) comes from 吊 (tsuru, to hang), referring to suspended objects; in Minecraft, hanging lanterns or chains follow this idea.
minnanocraft.token.hanging.example: 天井から吊りのランタンが揺れている。 (tenjoo kara tsuri no rankan ga yurete iru.) - A hanging lantern sways from the ceiling.
minnanocraft.token.hanging_1.desc: 垂れ (tare) employs the kanji 垂 (sui/tare, to droop), signifying something that hangs or drips; in Minecraft, vines or draped strings are labeled this way.
minnanocraft.token.hanging_1.example: 壁に垂れのツタが付いている。 (kabe ni tare no tsuta ga tsuite iru.) - A hanging vine clings to the wall.
minnanocraft.token.flowering.desc: 開花 (kaika) joins 開 (kai, to open) and 花 (ka, flower), meaning to bloom; in Minecraft, flowering stages give blocks vivid colors.
minnanocraft.token.flowering.example: 春になると森は開花し、色とりどりになる。 (haru ni naru to mori wa kaika shi, irodoridori ni naru.) - In spring the forest flowers, becoming multicolored.
minnanocraft.token.flower_1.desc: フラワー (furawaa) is a katakana loanword for "flower", applied to decorative block names; in Minecraft, flower blocks are labeled this way.
minnanocraft.token.flower_1.example: 庭にフラワーのブロックを置いた。 (niwa ni furawaa no burokkku wo oita.) - I placed a flower block in the garden.
minnanocraft.token.flower.desc: 花 (hana) means "flower"; in Minecraft flowers are colorful blocks harvested for dyes.
minnanocraft.token.flower.example: 花畑で羊が草を食べる (Hanabatake de hitsuji ga kusa wo taberu) - Sheep graze on the flower field
minnanocraft.token.archer.desc: 射手 (ite) combines 射 (sha, "to shoot") and 手 (te, "hand"); it denotes a player using a bow to fire arrows.
minnanocraft.token.archer.example: 射手は遠くのゾンビを狙う (Ite wa tooku no zonbi wo nerau) - The archer aims at a distant zombie
minnanocraft.token.big.desc: 大 (oo) denotes largeness; structures such as massive trees are referred to as "big" in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.big.example: 大きな木の下で木材を集める (ookina ki no shita de mokuzai wo atsumeru) - Gather wood under the big tree
minnanocraft.token.tall.desc: 背の高い (se no takai) merges 背 (se, "back") and 高い (takai, "high"); it describes tall structures like towers or trees.
minnanocraft.token.tall.example: 背の高い塔から遠くを見る (Se no takai too kara tooku wo miru) - From the tall tower, view the distant horizon
minnanocraft.token.medium.desc: 中 (chuu) means "medium"; items such as medium-sized chests are labeled as "medium" in the game.
minnanocraft.token.medium.example: 中サイズのチェストに資源を入れる (Chuu saizu no chesuto ni shigen wo ireru) - Place resources in the medium chest
minnanocraft.token.small.desc: 小 (shou) means "small"; the kanji denotes something tiny, mirroring small-sized blocks or items in Minecraft, such as a compact block that occupies less space.
minnanocraft.token.small.example: 小さな箱を開けてみよう (chiisana hako wo akete miyou) - Let's open this small chest.
minnanocraft.token.short.desc: 背の低い (se no hikui) combines 背 (se, "back/height") and 低い (hikui, "low") to describe short height, as seen in low mobs or structures in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.short.example: 背の低い樹木の下で休む (se no hikui juumoku no shita de yasumu) - Rest under the short trees.
minnanocraft.token.soul_sand.desc: ソウルサンド (souru sando) is a katakana loanword for "Soul Sand"; in Minecraft the block slows movement, echoing trapped souls on its surface.
minnanocraft.token.soul_sand.example: ソウルサンドの上を歩くと遅くなる (souru sando no ue wo aruku to osoku naru) - Walking on Soul Sand slows you down.
minnanocraft.token.soul.desc: 魂 (tamashii) means "soul"; in Minecraft souls appear as glowing particles in the Nether and fuel soul fire.
minnanocraft.token.soul.example: 魂が光る洞窟を探検する (tamashii ga hikaru doukutsu wo tanken suru) - Explore the cave where souls glow.
minnanocraft.token.heart.desc: 心 (kokoro) means "heart" or "spirit"; in Minecraft the heart icon denotes the player's health bar.
minnanocraft.token.heart.example: 心が高鳴ると体力が回復する (kokoro ga takanaru to tairyoku ga kaifuku suru) - When the heart races, health regenerates.
minnanocraft.token.heart_1.desc: The kanji 心 (shin/kokoro) means 'heart' or 'mind' and 臓 (zoo) means 'internal organ'; together 心臓 (shinzoo) literally means 'heart organ', which in Minecraft is the health icon that restores the health bar.
minnanocraft.token.heart_1.example: 心臓 (shinzoo) が満タンになると、体力が回復する。 (Shinzoo ga mantan ni naru to, tairyoku ga kaifuku suru.) - When the heart is full, health regenerates.
minnanocraft.token.prize.desc: 宝 (taka) means 'treasure' and 物 (mono) means 'thing'; 宝物 (takaramono) literally means 'treasure thing', mirroring the rarity and value of a prize in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.prize.example: 宝物 (takaramono) を見つけたら、すぐにインベントリに入れよう。 (Takaramono wo mitsuketara, sugu ni inbentori ni ireyoo.) - When you find a prize, put it in your inventory right away.
minnanocraft.token.scute.desc: ウロコ (uroko) is written in katakana, a stylized loan of 鱗 (uroko) meaning 'scale'; in Minecraft, the scute is dropped by turtles and used to craft a durable shell.
minnanocraft.token.scute.example: ウロコ (uroko) を集めて、亀の甲羅を作ろう。 (Uroko wo atsumete, kame no koora wo tsukuroo.) - Gather scutes and craft a turtle shell.
minnanocraft.token.breath.desc: ブレス (buresu) is a katakana gairaigo from the English 'breath'; in Minecraft it denotes the air supply while underwater, shown as bubble icons.
minnanocraft.token.breath.example: ブレス (buresu) が切れる前に、空気ブロックへ戻ろう。 (Buresu ga kireru mae ni, kuuki burokku e modoroo.) - Return to an air block before your breath runs out.
minnanocraft.token.painting.desc: 絵 (e) means 'picture' and 画 (ga) means 'drawing'; 絵画 (kaiga) translates to 'painting', which in Minecraft are decorative frames that can be hung on walls.
minnanocraft.token.painting.example: 絵画 (kaiga) を壁に掛けて、拠点を彩ろう。 (Kaiga wo kabe ni kakete, kyoten wo irodoroo.) - Hang a painting on the wall to decorate your base.
minnanocraft.token.item_frame.desc: The term 額縁 (gakubuchi) merges 額 'frame' and 縁 'edge', mirroring the block that frames items for display.
minnanocraft.token.item_frame.example: Place an item frame (gakubuchi) on the wall to showcase your map. (Kabe ni gakubuchi wo setchi shite mappu wo kazarou.) - Place an item frame on the wall to showcase your map.
minnanocraft.token.cave.desc: 洞窟 (doukutsu) combines 洞 'hole' and 窟 'cavern', denoting the underground area where ores are found.
minnanocraft.token.cave.example: Explore the cave (doukutsu) to find diamonds. (Doukutsu de housei wo sagasou.) - Explore the cave to find diamonds.
minnanocraft.token.path.desc: 道 (michi) translates to 'path', matching the block that forms walkways.
minnanocraft.token.path.example: Lay a path (michi) to connect your base to the village. (Michi wo tsukutte base to mura wo musubu.) - Lay a path to connect your base to the village.
minnanocraft.token.tile.desc: タイル (tairu) is a gairaigo from English 'tile', referring to the decorative block used for flooring.
minnanocraft.token.tile.example: Build a tiled floor (tairu) in your house. (Tairu de ie no yuka wo tsukuru.) - Build a tiled floor in your house.
minnanocraft.token.tiles.desc: タイル (tairu) remains unchanged for plural; the sentence context conveys multiple tiles.
minnanocraft.token.tiles.example: Place many tiles (tairu) to create a mosaic. (Takusan no tairu de mosaiku wo tsukuru.) - Place many tiles to create a mosaic.
minnanocraft.token.jack_o_lantern.desc: Jack o'Lantern (Jacku wo Rantan) is a direct loan from English, naming the carved pumpkin that provides light in Minecraft, echoing the Western Halloween lantern tradition.
minnanocraft.token.jack_o_lantern.exampl: 夜の森でジャック・オ・ランタンを置くと、モンスターが遠ざかる。 (Yoru no mori de Jacku wo Rantan wo oku to, monsutaa ga toozakaru.) - Placing a Jack o'Lantern in the night forest keeps monsters at bay.
minnanocraft.token.lantern.desc: Lantern (Rantan) is a loan from English 'lantern', denoting the hanging light source that can be attached to blocks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.lantern.example: 洞窟の天井にランタンを吊るすと、暗闇が消える。 (Dookutsu no tenjoo ni Rantan wo tsurusuto, kurayami ga kieru.) - Hanging a lantern from the cave ceiling dispels the darkness.
minnanocraft.token.magma.desc: Magma (Maguma) originates from English 'magma', referring to the glowing liquid inside magma blocks that inflict damage on contact in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.magma.example: 溶岩の上にマグマブロックを置くと、熱で周囲が焼ける。 (Yoogan no ue ni Maguma burokku wo oku to, netsu de shuui ga yakeru.) - Placing a magma block over lava burns the surroundings with heat.
minnanocraft.token.ink.desc: Ink (Sumi) corresponds to the native word '墨' (sumi), black pigment for writing; in Minecraft, ink harvested from squids is used to color items.
minnanocraft.token.ink.example: インクを使って羊毛を黒く染めよう。 (Inku wo tsukatte yoomoo wo kuroku someyoo.) - Let's use ink to dye wool black.
minnanocraft.token.sac.desc: Sac (Ika) is the Japanese term for 'squid', rendered in katakana for stylistic effect; in Minecraft, the ink sac is obtained from this creature.
minnanocraft.token.sac.example: 海底でイカを捕まえてインクを集めよう。 (Kaitei de Ika wo tsukamaete Inku wo atsumeyoo.) - Catch squids underwater to gather ink.
minnanocraft.token.end.desc: エンド (endo) is a gairaigo from English “end”, naming the final dimension that marks the conclusion of the Minecraft world.
minnanocraft.token.end.example: エンドへのポータルを見つけた (Endo e no pootaru wo mitsuketa) - I found the portal to the End.
minnanocraft.token.end_stone.desc: エンドストーン (endosutoon) combines エンド (endo) and ストーン (sutoon, “stone”), both loanwords, referring to the rocky block that makes up the End island.
minnanocraft.token.end_stone.example: エンドストーンで橋を作った (Endosutoon de hashi wo tsukutta) - I built a bridge with End Stone.
minnanocraft.token.fern.desc: シダ (shida) is written in katakana despite being a native word for fern. In Minecraft it represents the plant that grows in shaded areas.
minnanocraft.token.fern.example: シダが生えている洞窟を探検した (Shida ga haete iru dookutsu wo tanken shita) - I explored a cave where ferns grow.
minnanocraft.token.dripleaf.desc: ドリップリーフ (Dorippuriifu) is a katakana loan from English “drip leaf”. In Minecraft the block drips water and acts as a descending platform, matching the literal “leaf that drips”.
minnanocraft.token.dripleaf.example: When you jump on a dripleaf, water drips down. (Dorippuriifu no ue de janpu suru to, mizu ga shitari ochiru.) - When you jump on a dripleaf, water drips down.
minnanocraft.token.sunflower.desc: ヒマワリ (Himawari) appears in katakana for stylistic reasons. The native term means “sunflower”, literally “sun” + “flower”. In Minecraft the tall plant tracks the sun, mirroring its name.
minnanocraft.token.sunflower.example: The sunflower grows toward the sun. (Himawari wa taiyoo ni mukatte seichoo suru.) - The sunflower grows toward the sun.
minnanocraft.token.rose.desc: バラ (Bara) is presented in katakana; the native spelling is 薔薇. It denotes the rose, an ornamental flower. In Minecraft the red rose is a decorative and trade item, echoing its aesthetic value.
minnanocraft.token.rose.example: Villagers smile when you bring a rose. (Bara wo te ni ireru to, murabito ga yorokobu.) - Villagers smile when you bring a rose.
minnanocraft.token.rose_1.desc: ローズ (Roozu) is a katakana loan from English “rose”. In Minecraft the “rose” block depicts the red flower, preserving the foreign origin.
minnanocraft.token.rose_1.example: Planting a rose colors the garden. (Roozu wo ueru to, niwa ga irodorareru.) - Planting a rose colors the garden.
minnanocraft.token.lily_of_the_valley.de: スズラン (Suzuran) appears in katakana; the kanji 鈴蘭 merges 鈴 (suzu, “bell”) and 蘭 (ran, “orchid”). The name suggests a delicate, bell‑shaped flower, matching the small white Minecraft lily that thrives in shady biomes.
minnanocraft.token.lily_of_the_valley.ex: Lily of the valley blooms quietly in forest shadows. (Suzuran wa mori no kage de shizuka ni saku.) - Lily of the valley blooms quietly in forest shadows.
minnanocraft.token.cornflower.desc: Yagurumagiku (ヤグルマギク) is written in katakana as a stylized loan for "cornflower"; in Minecraft it yields the blue dye used in crafting.
minnanocraft.token.cornflower.example: 畑でヤグルマギクを摘んで青い染料を作ろう。 (Hatake de Yagurumagiku wo tsunde aoi senryou wo tsukurou.) - Gather cornflowers in the field to make blue dye.
minnanocraft.token.tulip.desc: Chuurippu (チューリップ) is a katakana loan from Dutch "tulip", echoing its trade history; in Minecraft it provides pink dye.
minnanocraft.token.tulip.example: 庭にチューリップを植えて、ピンク染料を集めよう。 (Niwa ni Chuurippu wo uete, pinku senryou wo atsumeyou.) - Plant tulips in the garden to gather pink dye.
minnanocraft.token.dandelion.desc: Tanpopo (タンポポ) is rendered in katakana as a stylized native term for "dandelion"; in Minecraft it drops yellow dye.
minnanocraft.token.dandelion.example: 平原でタンポポを壊すと黄色の染料が手に入る。 (Heigen de Tanpopo wo kowasu to kiiro no senryou ga te ni hairu.) - Breaking dandelions on the plains yields yellow dye.
minnanocraft.token.wildflowers.desc: Nohana (野花) uses the kanji 野 "wild, field" and 花 "flower" to mean "wildflowers"; in Minecraft it appears as a colorful decorative block.
minnanocraft.token.wildflowers.example: 野花の上に座って、星空を眺めよう。 (Nohana no ue ni suwatte, hoshizora wo nagameyou.) - Sit atop the wildflowers and gaze at the starry sky.
minnanocraft.token.poppy.desc: Popī (ポピー) is a katakana loan from English "poppy"; in Minecraft it yields red dye for potions and banners.
minnanocraft.token.poppy.example: 洞窟の入口にポピーが咲いている。 (Doukutsu no iriguchi ni Popī ga saiteiru.) - Poppies bloom at the cave entrance.
minnanocraft.token.azalea.desc: Japanese ツツジ (tsutsuji) in katakana denotes the azalea shrub; in Minecraft it appears as a pink‑colored plant block.
minnanocraft.token.azalea.example: 庭にツツジを植えて、ピンクの花を楽しもう (Niwa ni tsutsuji wo uete, pinku no hana wo tanoshimou) - Plant tsutsuji in the garden to enjoy its pink blossoms.
minnanocraft.token.kelp.desc: コンブ (konbu) in katakana is a loanword for the seaweed; Minecraft kelp grows underwater as a green block.
minnanocraft.token.kelp.example: 海底でコンブを収穫して、食料にしよう (Kaitei de konbu wo shuukaku shite, shokuryou ni shiyou) - Harvest konbu at the ocean floor for food.
minnanocraft.token.kelp_1.desc: 昆布 (konbu) combines 昆 (kon, “descendant/insect”) and 布 (fu, “cloth”); the compound denotes kelp, represented as an underwater block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.kelp_1.example: 海の底で昆布を見つけたら、すぐに採取しよう (Umi no soko de konbu wo mitsuketara, sugu ni saishuu shiyou) - When you spot konbu at the ocean floor, harvest it right away.
minnanocraft.token.milk.desc: ミルク (miruku) in katakana is a gairaigo from English “milk”; Minecraft milk is obtained from cows and stored in buckets.
minnanocraft.token.milk.example: 牛からミルクを絞って、バケツに入れよう (Ushi kara miruku wo shitte, baketsu ni ireyoo) - Milk the cow and fill a bucket with miruku.
minnanocraft.token.lava.desc: 溶岩 (yougan) merges 溶 (you, “to melt”) and 岩 (gan, “rock”); it literally means molten rock, matching Minecraft’s glowing lava.
minnanocraft.token.lava.example: 溶岩の流れに近づくと、装備が焼ける (Yougan no nagare ni chikazuku to, soubi ga yakeru) - Getting close to a yougan stream burns your gear.
minnanocraft.token.sugar.desc: 砂糖 (satou) merges 砂 'sand' and 糖 'sugar', mirroring the granular appearance of the Minecraft item, essential for crafting cakes.
minnanocraft.token.sugar.example: 私は蜂の巣から砂糖を集めてケーキを作った (Watashi wa hachinosu kara satou wo atsumete keeki wo tsukutta) - I gathered sugar from a beehive and baked a cake.
minnanocraft.token.sugar_cane.desc: サトウキビ (satōkibi) is written in katakana as a gairaigo from English 'sugarcane'; in Minecraft it appears as tall stalks that yield sugar when processed.
minnanocraft.token.sugar_cane.example: 川辺でサトウキビを収穫し、砂糖に変換した (Kawabe de satōkibi wo shuukaku shi, satou ni henkan shita) - I harvested sugar cane by the river and turned it into sugar.
minnanocraft.token.chorus.desc: コーラス (kōrasu) uses katakana as a gairaigo of 'chorus'; the End chorus fruit in Minecraft lets players teleport, echoing the idea of a repeated refrain.
minnanocraft.token.chorus.example: エンドの島でコーラスの果実を食べて瞬間移動した (Endo no shima de kōrasu no kajitsu wo tabete shunkan idou shita) - I ate the chorus fruit on the End island and instantly teleported.
minnanocraft.token.plant.desc: つる (tsuru) in hiragana means 'vine', matching the climbing vines that cling to walls in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.plant.example: 洞窟の壁に付いたつるを切ってアイテムを得た (Doukutsu no kabe ni tsuita tsuru wo kitte aitemu wo eta) - I cut the vine attached to the cave wall and obtained an item.
minnanocraft.token.plant_1.desc: プラント (puranto) is katakana for the English 'plant'; in Minecraft it denotes generic plant blocks used in farming.
minnanocraft.token.plant_1.example: 農場でプラントを植えて小麦を収穫した (Noujou de puranto wo uete komugi wo shuukaku shita) - I planted a plant on the farm and harvested wheat.
minnanocraft.token.berries.desc: ベリー (Berī) is a loanword from English "berry"; in Minecraft it refers to the small red fruits that can be harvested and eaten.
minnanocraft.token.berries.example: 森で甘いベリーを集めよう！ (Mori de amai Berī wo atsumeyou!) - Let's gather sweet berries in the forest!
minnanocraft.token.fruit.desc: フルーツ (Furuutsu) is borrowed from English "fruit"; it denotes edible fruits in the game, such as melon or pumpkin, that restore hunger.
minnanocraft.token.fruit.example: 農場でフルーツを育てて、食料を確保しよう。 (Noojoo de Furuutsu wo sodate, shokuryoo wo kakuhoo shiyoo.) - Grow fruit on the farm to secure food.
minnanocraft.token.apple.desc: リンゴ (Ringo) is a loanword from English "apple"; in Minecraft it restores health when eaten, matching the fruit's nourishing reputation.
minnanocraft.token.apple.example: 木から落ちたリンゴを拾って、体力を回復しよう。 (Ki kara ochita Ringo wo hirotte, tairyoku wo kaifuku shiyoo.) - Pick up the apple that fell from the tree and restore health.
minnanocraft.token.carrot.desc: ニンジン (Ninjin) comes from the kanji 人参 (person + root); in Minecraft it is an orange root used for potions and animal breeding.
minnanocraft.token.carrot.example: 畑でニンジンを育てて、ウサギを繁殖させよう。 (Hatake de Ninjin wo sodate, Usagi wo hanshoku saseyoo.) - Grow carrots in the farm and breed rabbits.
minnanocraft.token.potato.desc: ジャガイモ (Jagaimo) is borrowed from Dutch "aardappel"; the traditional kanji 馬鈴薯 (horse + bell + tuber) mirrors its round shape, serving as a staple food in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.potato.example: ジャガイモ畑で作物を収穫し、食料にしよう。 (Jagaimo hatake de sakumotsu wo shuukaku shi, shokuryoo ni shiyoo.) - Harvest potatoes in the field and turn them into food.
minnanocraft.token.beetroot.desc: ビートルート (Bītoruuto) is a loan from English 'beetroot', naming the red root that can be farmed and harvested in Minecraft, mirroring its vivid color and round shape.
minnanocraft.token.beetroot.example: ビートルートを植えて、赤い収穫を楽しもう！ (Bītoruuto wo uete, akai shuuka wo tanoshimou!) - Plant beetroots and enjoy the red harvest!
minnanocraft.token.baked_potato.desc: ベイクドポテト (Beikudo Poteto) comes from English 'baked potato', referring to the cooked potato that appears in Minecraft when a raw potato is baked, turning brownish‑gold.
minnanocraft.token.baked_potato.example: ベイクドポテトを作って、暖かい食事を取ろう。 (Beikudo Poteto wo tsukutte, atatakai shokuji wo torou.) - Make a baked potato and enjoy a warm meal.
minnanocraft.token.pickle.desc: ピクルス (Pikurusu) is a loan from English 'pickle', naming the preserved cucumber obtainable in Minecraft by converting cucumbers into pickle blocks.
minnanocraft.token.pickle.example: ピクルスを食べて、長時間の探検に備えよう。 (Pikurusu wo tabete, choojikan no tanken ni sonaeyou.) - Eat pickles to ready yourself for long expeditions.
minnanocraft.token.bread.desc: パン (Pan) originates from Portuguese 'pão', showing its historical borrowing; in Minecraft it denotes the staple food crafted from wheat.
minnanocraft.token.bread.example: パンを焼いて、満腹度を回復しよう。 (Pan wo yaite, manpukudo wo kaifuku shiyou.) - Bake bread and restore hunger.
minnanocraft.token.cake.desc: ケーキ (Kēki) comes from English 'cake', naming the decorative cake that can be placed as a block with multiple slices in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.cake.example: ケーキを作って、誕生日パーティーを開催しよう。 (Kēki wo tsukutte, tanjoobi paatī wo kaisai shiyou.) - Make a cake and host a birthday party.
minnanocraft.token.pie.desc: パイ (pai) is a katakana gairaigo from English "pie"; in Minecraft it resembles a golden‑crusted pie, matching its round shape and filling.
minnanocraft.token.pie.example: I baked a pie in the cave (Doukutsu de pai wo yaita) - I baked a pie in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.stew.desc: シチュー (shichuu) is a katakana loan from English "stew"; in Minecraft it serves as a slow‑healing food, analogous to a cooked stew.
minnanocraft.token.stew.example: I cooked stew in the pot (Nabe de shichuu wo tsukutta) - I cooked stew in the pot.
minnanocraft.token.soup.desc: スープ (suupu) is a katakana gairaigo from English "soup"; in Minecraft it instantly restores hunger, like a hot broth.
minnanocraft.token.soup.example: I drank soup at camp (Kyanpu de suupu wo nonda) - I drank soup at camp.
minnanocraft.token.beef.desc: 牛 (ushi) is a kanji meaning "cow"; in Minecraft the beef item comes from killing cows, reflecting the original meaning.
minnanocraft.token.beef.example: I hunted a cow and got beef (Ushi wo karitte bīfu wo eta) - I hunted a cow and got beef.
minnanocraft.token.beef_1.desc: ステーキ (sutēki) is a katakana loan from English "steak"; in Minecraft it denotes a grilled steak, a premium meat item.
minnanocraft.token.beef_1.example: I grilled steak at the furnace (Kandai de sutēki wo yaita) - I grilled steak at the furnace.
minnanocraft.token.cooked_beef.desc: Sutēki (ステーキ) is a gairaigo from English “steak”, denoting the cooked beef item that restores hunger.
minnanocraft.token.cooked_beef.example: 私はステーキを焼いて、満腹になった。 (Watashi wa sutēki wo yaite, manpuku ni natta.) - I cooked a steak and became full.
minnanocraft.token.seafloor.desc: Kaitei (海底) combines 海 (umi, “sea”) and 底 (tei, “bottom”), referring to the ocean floor where players find sand and marine resources.
minnanocraft.token.seafloor.example: 潜水艦は海底に沈んだ宝箱を探す。 (Sensuikan wa kaitei ni shizunda takarabako wo sagasu.) - The submarine searches for the sunken chest on the seafloor.
minnanocraft.token.sea.desc: Kaiyoo (海洋) joins 海 (umi, “sea”) and 洋 (yoo, “ocean”), denoting the expansive water biome in Minecraft inhabited by fish and dolphins.
minnanocraft.token.sea.example: 私たちは海洋でイルカと泳いだ。 (Watashitachi wa kaiyoo de iruka to oyoida.) - We swam with dolphins in the sea.
minnanocraft.token.sea_1.desc: Shī (シー) is a gairaigo from English “sea”, employed as a stylized label for minor marine zones or sea‑related items in the mod.
minnanocraft.token.sea_1.example: シーの旗が港に掲げられた。 (Shī no hata ga minato ni kakerareta.) - The sea flag was raised at the harbor.
minnanocraft.token.shell.desc: Kara (殻) means “shell” or “husk”, describing the collectible item found on beaches that can serve as decorative material.
minnanocraft.token.shell.example: 海岸で殻を集めて、装飾に使う。 (Kaigan de kara wo atsumete, sooshoku ni tsukau.) - We gather shells on the shore and use them for decoration.
minnanocraft.token.roots.desc: 根 (ne) translates to "root"; in Minecraft, roots are a block that spreads from logs, mirroring how real roots anchor trees.
minnanocraft.token.roots.example: 根が土に伸びて、木を支えている。 (Ne ga tsuchi ni nobite, ki wo sasaete iru.) - The roots extend into the soil, supporting the tree.
minnanocraft.token.rooted.desc: 根付いた (nezuita) merges 根 (ne, root) and 付く (tsuku, to attach) in past form, meaning "has taken root"; in Minecraft, it can refer to blocks or entities that are immobile, like a rooted plant.
minnanocraft.token.rooted.example: この木は根付いたので、壊せない。 (Kono ki wa nezuita node, kowasenai.) - This tree is rooted and cannot be broken.
minnanocraft.token.gunpowder.desc: 火薬 (kayaku) combines 火 (ka, fire) and 薬 (yaku, chemical), literally "fire medicine"; in Minecraft it is the component for TNT and fireworks, reflecting its explosive nature.
minnanocraft.token.gunpowder.example: 火薬を使ってTNTを作ろう。 (Kayaku wo tsukatte TNT wo tsukurou.) - Use gunpowder to craft TNT.
minnanocraft.token.command.desc: コマンド (komando) is a katakana loanword from English "command"; in Minecraft it denotes textual instructions that manipulate the world, e.g., /give or /tp.
minnanocraft.token.command.example: コマンドで天井を作れ。 (Komando de tenjoo wo tsukure.) - Build a ceiling with a command.
minnanocraft.token.furnace.desc: かまど (kamado) is written in hiragana, derived from the kanji 竃 meaning "furnace" or "stove"; in Minecraft, the Furnace block smelts ores, mirroring its historic cooking role.
minnanocraft.token.furnace.example: かまどで鉄鉱石を溶かす。 (Kamado de tetsukooseki wo tokasu.) - Smelt iron ore in the furnace.
minnanocraft.token.blast_furnace.desc: The term 溶鉱炉 (youkouro) merges 溶 (to melt), 鉱 (ore) and 炉 (furnace), mirroring the block that smelts ores at high heat in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.blast_furnace.example: Youkouro de tetsukouseki wo seiren suru (Refine iron ore in the blast furnace) - Thematic phrase
minnanocraft.token.smoker.desc: The word 燻製器 (kunseiki) combines 燻 (to smoke), 製 (to make) and 器 (device), describing the block that cooks food with smoke.
minnanocraft.token.smoker.example: Kunseiki de butaniku wo kunsei ni suru (Smoke pork in the smoker) - Thematic phrase
minnanocraft.token.rail.desc: レール (rēru) is a katakana loan from English "rail", denoting the tracks that guide minecarts.
minnanocraft.token.rail.example: Rēru wo shite torokko wo hashiraseyou (Lay rails and run a minecart) - Thematic phrase
minnanocraft.token.structure.desc: ストラクチャー (sutoraakyaa) is a katakana loan of "structure", referring to pre‑generated or player‑built constructions.
minnanocraft.token.structure.example: Sutoraakyaa wo seisei shite kyoten wo tsukurou (Generate a structure to build a base) - Thematic phrase
minnanocraft.token.tnt.desc: TNT retains its international abbreviation, written in katakana as TNT in Japanese, denoting a high‑power explosive.
minnanocraft.token.tnt.example: TNT wo setchi shite doukutsu wo hori susumeru (Place TNT to tunnel through the cave) - Thematic phrase
minnanocraft.token.test.desc: テスト (tesuto) is a katakana loan from English “test”, used in Minecraft for test worlds or blocks, reflecting its experimental purpose.
minnanocraft.token.test.example: テストワールドで新しいブロックを試す (Tesuto waarudo de atarashii burokk wo tamesu) - Test the new block in the test world.
