minnanocraft.token.cube.desc: キューブ (kyuubu) is a katakana loan from English “cube”, denoting the cubic shape of standard Minecraft blocks.
minnanocraft.token.cube.example: キューブの形をした鉱石ブロックを採掘した (Kyuubu no katachi wo shita kooseki burokk wo saikutsu shita) - Mined an ore block shaped like a cube.
minnanocraft.token.cream.desc: クリーム (kurīmu) is a katakana loan from English “cream”, referring to the creamy ingredient used in food recipes in the game.
minnanocraft.token.cream.example: クリームを使って甘いケーキを作った (Kurīmu wo tsukatte amai kēki wo tsukutta) - Made a sweet cake using cream.
minnanocraft.token.void.desc: ヴォイド (voido) is a katakana loan from English “void”, representing the empty space beneath the Minecraft world where falling is lethal.
minnanocraft.token.void.example: ヴォイドに落ちるとすぐに死んでしまう (Voido ni ochiru to sugu ni shinde shimau) - Falling into the void kills you instantly.
minnanocraft.token.void_1.desc: 奈落 (naraku) combines 奈 (na, phonetic) and 落 (raku, “fall”), meaning “abyss” or “hell”, used in Minecraft to denote deep void regions.
minnanocraft.token.void_1.example: 奈落の底から光が漏れ出した (Naraku no soko kara hikari ga more dashita) - Light leaked from the bottom of the abyss.
minnanocraft.token.blank_paper.desc: The Japanese word 白紙 (hakushi) is formed by 白 (white) + 紙 (paper). In Minecraft a blank paper item is the empty canvas for books, mirroring the literal “white paper”.
minnanocraft.token.blank_paper.example: 白紙の本に新しい冒険を書き込む (Hakushi no hon ni atarashii bouken wo kakikomu) - Write a new adventure in the blank book.
minnanocraft.token.instance.desc: インスタンス (insutansu) is a gairaigo from English “instance”, rendered in katakana as a technical loanword. In Minecraft each spawned entity represents an instance of its class.
minnanocraft.token.instance.example: インスタンスを生成してモブを呼び出す (Insutansu wo seisei shite mobu wo yobi dasu) - Create an instance to summon a mob.
minnanocraft.token.membrane.desc: 皮膜 (himaku) combines 皮 (skin) and 膜 (membrane). In Minecraft a slime-like membrane block behaves as a flexible barrier that blocks water flow.
minnanocraft.token.membrane.example: 皮膜のように粘着したブロックは水を通さない (Himaku no you ni nenchaku shita buroku wa mizu wo toosanai) - A block that sticks like a membrane does not let water pass.
minnanocraft.token.dripstone.desc: 鍾乳石 (shounyuuseki) is made of 鍾 (bell), 乳 (milk), and 石 (stone), historically describing stalactites that look like milk dripping from a bell. In Minecraft the Pointed Dripstone mimics these hanging stone formations.
minnanocraft.token.dripstone.example: 鍾乳石が洞窟の天井から垂れ下がる (Shounyuuseki ga doukutsu no tenjou kara tare sagaru) - The dripstone hangs from the cave ceiling.
minnanocraft.token.burn.desc: 炎 (honoo) directly translates to “flame”. In Minecraft fire spreads and burns blocks and mobs, matching the straightforward meaning.
minnanocraft.token.burn.example: 炎が燃えると周囲のブロックが焦げる (Honoo ga moeru to shuui no buroku ga kogeru) - When the flame burns, surrounding blocks char.
minnanocraft.token.animal.desc: 動物 (doobutsu) merges 動 "move" and 物 "thing", denoting entities that move in the game, e.g., cows and wolves.
minnanocraft.token.animal.example: 動物が草原で草を食べている (Doobutsu ga soogen de kusa wo tabete iru) - The animals are grazing on the plain.
minnanocraft.token.lightning_rod.desc: 避雷針 (hiraishin) consists of 避 "avoid", 雷 "thunder", and 針 "needle", indicating a device that draws and channels lightning.
minnanocraft.token.lightning_rod.example: 雷が避雷針に落ちた (Kaminari ga hiraishin ni ochita) - The lightning struck the lightning rod.
minnanocraft.token.skin.desc: 皮 (kawa) means "hide" or "skin", referring to leather armor or the player's visual layer.
minnanocraft.token.skin.example: 皮で作った防具は耐久性が低い (Kawa de tsukutta boogu wa taikyuusei ga hikui) - Leather armor has low durability.
minnanocraft.token.frame.desc: フレーム (fureemu) is a gairaigo from English "frame", denoting the item that holds paintings and maps.
minnanocraft.token.frame.example: 壁にフレームを置いて絵を飾る (Kabe ni fureemu wo oite e wo kazaru) - Place a frame on the wall to hang a picture.
minnanocraft.token.fire_charge.desc: ファイヤーチャージ (faiyaa chaaji) is a katakana loan of "fire charge", an incendiary projectile in the game.
minnanocraft.token.fire_charge.example: ファイヤーチャージを投げてクリーパーを燃やす (Faiyaa chaaji wo nagete kurīpaa wo moyasu) - Throw a fire charge to burn the creeper.
minnanocraft.token.petrified.desc: 石化 (sekika) combines 石 'stone' and 化 'to change', mirroring the wood block that becomes stone in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.petrified.example: 石化した木の板を使って橋を作ろう。 (Sekika shita ki no ita wo tsukatte hashi wo tsukurou.) - Let's build a bridge using petrified wood planks.
minnanocraft.token.epidermis.desc: 表皮 (hyouhi) joins 表 'surface' and 皮 'skin', describing the outer layer that covers blocks such as grass in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.epidermis.example: 表皮のように緑の層が覆う草ブロック。 (Hyouhi no you ni midori no sou ga oou kusa burokk.) - A grass block covered by a green layer like an epidermis.
minnanocraft.token.bark.desc: 樹皮 (juuhii) merges 樹 'tree' and 皮 'bark', referring to the bark block added in recent Minecraft updates.
minnanocraft.token.bark.example: 樹皮のブロックで家を装飾しよう。 (Juuhii no burokk de ie wo soushoku shiyou.) - Let's decorate the house with bark blocks.
minnanocraft.token.bowl.desc: ボウル (booru) is a katakana loan from English 'bowl', representing the container for soups and potions in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.bowl.example: ボウルにスープを入れて暖まろう。 (Booru ni suupu wo irete atatamarou.) - Put soup in the bowl to warm up.
minnanocraft.token.sensor.desc: センサー (sensaa) is a katakana loan of 'sensor', denoting the block that detects entities or block changes in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.sensor.example: センサーが近くのモブを感知した。 (Sensaa ga chikaku no mobu wo kanchi shita.) - The sensor detected a nearby mob.
minnanocraft.token.vault.desc: 宝物庫 (takaramono ko) combines 宝 “treasure”, 物 “thing” and 庫 “storehouse”, mirroring the vault that stores valuable items in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.vault.example: 冒険者は宝物庫へ宝を入れた (Bouken-sha wa takaramono ko e takara wo ireta) - The adventurer placed treasure into the vault.
minnanocraft.token.bush.desc: 茂み (shigemi) employs 茂 “dense vegetation” plus the suffix み, denoting a thicket, just like the bush block found in Minecraft biomes.
minnanocraft.token.bush.example: 森の中で茂みを切り倒した (Mori no naka de shigemi wo kiritaoshita) - I cut down the bush in the forest.
minnanocraft.token.shrub.desc: 低木 (teiboku) merges 低 “low” with 木 “tree”, describing a short shrub that doesn’t grow tall, often used as decoration in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.shrub.example: 庭に低木を植えた (Niwa ni teiboku wo ueta) - I planted a shrub in the garden.
minnanocraft.token.obsidian.desc: 黒曜石 (kokuyouseki) joins 黒 “black” with 曜石 “shining stone”, echoing the dark, glassy rock that players mine in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.obsidian.example: 洞窟で黒曜石を採掘した (Doukutsu de kokuyouseki wo saikutsu shita) - I mined obsidian in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.crying.desc: 泣く (naku) means “to cry”; the Crying Obsidian block releases particle effects resembling tears, directly referencing the verb.
minnanocraft.token.crying.example: 泣く音が黒曜石から聞こえる (Naku oto ga kokuyouseki kara kikoeru) - A crying sound can be heard from the obsidian.
minnanocraft.token.azure_bluet.desc: The term ヒナソウ (Hinasou) literally means "small plant", matching the tiny blue blossoms that generate in plains biomes in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.azure_bluet.example: ヒナソウを集めて、青い草原を作ろう。(Hinasou wo atsumete, aoi sougen wo tsukurou.) - Gather azure bluets and create a blue meadow.
minnanocraft.token.catalyst.desc: カタリスト (Katarisuto) is a katakana rendering of the English "catalyst", indicating an item that speeds reactions, analogous to a boost in Minecraft crafting or plant growth.
minnanocraft.token.catalyst.example: カタリストで鉱石の精錬時間を短縮しよう。(Katarisuto de kouseki no seiren jikan wo tanshuku shiyou.) - Use the catalyst to shorten ore smelting time.
minnanocraft.token.lichen.desc: ゴケ (Goke) translates to "lichen", a low‑growth plant that clings to stone, mirroring the lichen block that spreads on stone surfaces in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.lichen.example: ゴケを壁に貼って、洞窟を自然に見せよう。(Goke wo kabe ni hatte, doukutsu wo shizen ni miseyou.) - Attach lichen to walls to make caves look natural.
minnanocraft.token.lilac.desc: ライラック (Rairakku) is a katakana borrowing of "lilac", describing the tall purple blossoms that generate in forest biomes, used for purple dye in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.lilac.example: ライラックの花を集めて、旗に飾ろう。(Rairakku no hana wo atsumete, hata ni kazarou.) - Collect lilac flowers to decorate a banner.
minnanocraft.token.vine.desc: ツタ (Tsuta) translates to "vine", a climbing plant that wraps around blocks, just like the vine block that hangs from ceilings and climbs surfaces in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.vine.example: ツタで高い塔に登り、眺めを楽しもう。(Tsuta de takai tou ni nobori, nagame wo tanoshimou.) - Climb a tall tower with vines and enjoy the view.
minnanocraft.token.firefly.desc: ホタル (hotaru) appears in katakana; the term denotes the luminous insect, mirroring the glowing effect of the firefly block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.firefly.example: ホタルが光る洞窟で探検しよう (Hotaru ga hikaru dookutsu de tanken shiyoo) - Let's explore the cave where fireflies glow
minnanocraft.token.weeping.desc: しだれ (shidare) comes from the kanji 枝垂れ (branch‑drooping); it describes hanging foliage, analogous to the downward‑growing Weeping Vines block.
minnanocraft.token.weeping.example: しだれの蔓が壁を覆う (Shidare no tsuru ga kabe wo oou) - The weeping vines cover the wall
minnanocraft.token.barrier.desc: バリアブロック (baria burokku) is a katakana loanword for “barrier block”; it creates an invisible obstruction, matching the English term’s meaning.
minnanocraft.token.barrier.example: バリアブロックで入口を封鎖した (Baria burokku de iriguchi wo fuusatsu shita) - I sealed the entrance with a barrier block
minnanocraft.token.cookie.desc: クッキー (kukkī) is a katakana transcription of the English “cookie”; in Minecraft it functions as a consumable food item.
minnanocraft.token.cookie.example: クッキーを焼いてインベントリに入れた (Kukkī wo yaite inbentori ni ireta) - I baked cookies and added them to my inventory
minnanocraft.token.decorated.desc: 飾り (kazari) consists of the kanji 飾 meaning “to decorate” plus the suffix り; it refers to decorative blocks that add aesthetic detail in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.decorated.example: 壁に飾りブロックを貼った (Kabe ni kazari burokku wo hatta) - I placed decorated blocks on the wall
minnanocraft.token.lead.desc: リード (Rīdo) is a gairaigo from English “lead”. In Minecraft it functions as a leash to tether mobs, matching the literal meaning of a rope.
minnanocraft.token.lead.example: 牛をリードでつなげると、農場の近くに留まる。 (Ushi wo Rīdo de tsunageru to, noojoo no chikaku ni tomaru.) - Leashing a cow keeps it near the farm.
minnanocraft.token.yellowtail.desc: キビレ (Kibire) is a katakana loanword for the yellow‑tailed fish, the yellowtail. In Minecraft it appears as a tropical fish, matching its real‑world counterpart.
minnanocraft.token.yellowtail.example: 熱帯魚のキビレは、鮮やかな色を持つ。 (Nettai‑gyo no Kibire wa, azayaka na iro wo motsu.) - The tropical fish yellowtail has vivid colors.
minnanocraft.token.heavy_weighted.desc: The word 重量 (juuryoo) merges 重 (juu, “heavy”) and 量 (ryoo, “quantity”), mirroring the heavy weighted pressure plate that triggers only under massive items in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.heavy_weighted.exampl: 重い荷物を置くと、重量プレートが作動する (Omoi nimotsu wo oku to, juuryoo purēto ga sadoo suru) - When a heavy load is placed, the weighted plate activates.
minnanocraft.token.purpose.desc: 用 (yoo) means “use” or “purpose”, denoting the intended function of a block or item, such as the purpose of a command block that runs a specific command.
minnanocraft.token.purpose.example: このブロックの用はレッドストーン信号を伝えることです (Kono buroku no yoo wa reddosutoon shingoo wo tsutaeru koto desu) - The purpose of this block is to transmit a redstone signal.
minnanocraft.token.wind_charge.desc: ウィンドチャージ (windochaaji) is rendered in katakana as a gairaigo from English “Wind Charge”, referring to the wind projectile launched by special bows in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.wind_charge.example: 弓でウィンドチャージを放つと、遠くの敵を吹き飛ばす (Yumi de windochaaji wo hanatsu to, tooku no teki wo fukitobasu) - Shooting a Wind Charge with a bow blows distant foes away.
minnanocraft.token.wind_charged.desc: 蓄風 (chikufuu) merges 蓄 (chiku, “to store”) and 風 (fuu, “wind”), describing an entity that has stored wind energy, such as a wind‑charged creeper that releases a gust on detonation.
minnanocraft.token.wind_charged.example: 蓄風したクリーパーは爆発時に風の渦を作る (Chikufuu shita kurīpaa wa bakuhatsu‑ji ni kaze no uzu wo tsukuru) - A wind‑charged creeper creates a vortex of wind when it explodes.
minnanocraft.token.wire.desc: ワイヤー (waiyaa) is written in katakana as a loanword from English “wire”. In Minecraft it links redstone components, acting as an electrical conductor.
minnanocraft.token.wire.example: レッドストーンのワイヤーで回路をつなげる (Reddosutoon no waiyaa de kairo wo tsunageru) - Connect the circuit using redstone wire.
minnanocraft.token.written.desc: The term 記入済み (kinyuuzumi) combines 記 “record”, 入 “enter”, and 済み “finished”, indicating the book has been filled, matching the Written Book that holds permanent text in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.written.example: 冒険者は本に記入済みだ。 (Booken-sha wa hon ni kinyuuzumi da) - The adventurer has written in the book.
minnanocraft.token.wandering_trader.desc: The term 行商人 (gyooshoonin) combines 行 “to travel” and 商人 “trader”, describing a person who roams selling goods, just like the Wandering Trader that spawns randomly in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.wandering_trader.exam: 行商人が村にやって来た。 (Gyooshoonin ga mura ni yattekita) - The wandering trader arrived at the village.
minnanocraft.token.weakness.desc: The term 弱化 (jakka) merges 弱 “weak” and 化 “change”, referring to a reduction of strength, like the Weakness effect that lowers attack damage in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.weakness.example: ポーションを飲んで弱化した。 (Pooshon wo nonde jakka shita) - He drank a potion and became weakened.
minnanocraft.token.weapon.desc: The term 武器 (buki) combines 武 “martial” and 器 “tool”, indicating a combat instrument, such as swords and bows that serve as primary weapons in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.weapon.example: 剣は最高の武器だ。 (Ken wa saikoo no buki da) - The sword is the best weapon.
minnanocraft.token.unknown.desc: The term 不明な (fumei na) employs 不 “non-” and 明 “clear”, meaning something not clarified, like blocks or items of unknown origin in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.unknown.example: この箱の中身は不明な。 (Kono hako no nakami wa fumei na) - The contents of this chest are unknown.
minnanocraft.token.upgrade.desc: The term 強化 (kyouka) combines 強 (strong) and 化 (change), indicating the transformation of an item into a stronger state, such as when applying enchantments in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.upgrade.example: この剣を強化しよう！ (Kono ken wo kyouka shiyou!) - Let's upgrade this sword!
minnanocraft.token.valley.desc: The term 谷 (tani) denotes a low area between hills, mirroring Minecraft valleys where rivers may flow.
minnanocraft.token.valley.example: 私たちは谷を探検した。 (Watashitachi wa tani wo tanken shita.) - We explored the valley.
minnanocraft.token.vein.desc: ヴェイン (vein) is the katakana rendering of the English loanword “vein”, referring to mineral veins in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.vein.example: 地下にヴェインが見える。 (Chika ni vein ga mieru.) - A vein is visible underground.
minnanocraft.token.twinkle.desc: The term 点滅 (tenmetsu) combines 点 (point) and 滅 (extinguish), describing a rapid light change, such as blinking lamps in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.twinkle.example: 星が点滅している。 (Hoshi ga tenmetsu shiteiru.) - The stars are twinkling.
minnanocraft.token.twisting.desc: The word ねじれ (nejire) means something twisted, akin to vines that coil or winding corridors in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.twisting.example: ねじれた洞窟を進む。 (Nejireta doukutsu wo susumu.) - Proceed through the twisting cave.
minnanocraft.token.type.desc: The term 活字 (katsuji) merges 活 (katsu, "living") with 字 (ji, "character"), literally "living character", used in Minecraft to denote the "type" of a block that determines its mechanics.
minnanocraft.token.type.example: この活字ブロックを置くと、周囲の装飾が変わる (Kono katsuji burokku wo oku to, shuui no sooshoku ga kawaru) - Placing this type block changes the surrounding decorations.
minnanocraft.token.uncraftable.desc: In the phrase クラフト不可能な (kurafuto fukanoona), the katakana loanword クラフト (kurafuto, "craft") is combined with 不可能 (fukanoo, "impossible") + な, meaning the item cannot be crafted.
minnanocraft.token.uncraftable.example: このクラフト不可能なアイテムは、自然に生成されるだけだ (Kono kurafuto fukanoona aitemu wa, shizen ni seisei sareru dake da) - This uncraftable item can only be generated naturally.
minnanocraft.token.undying.desc: The Japanese word 不死 (fushi) combines 不 (fu, "non-") and 死 (shi, "death"), literally "non‑death", matching the Minecraft "Undying" status that prevents death.
minnanocraft.token.undying.example: 不死のエリトラを装備すれば、落下しても死なない (Fushi no eritura wo soobi sureba, rakka shite mo shinanai) - Wearing the Undying Elytra prevents death even on a fall.
minnanocraft.token.trail.desc: The term 流星 (ryuusei) combines 流 (ryuu, "to flow") and 星 (sei, "star"), meaning "shooting star". In Minecraft, a "Trail" creates a flowing light similar to a falling star.
minnanocraft.token.trail.example: 流星のように光の軌跡を残す矢を放て (Ryuusei no yoo ni hikari no kiseki wo nokosu ya wo hanate) - Shoot an arrow that leaves a light trail like a shooting star.
minnanocraft.token.triggerfish.desc: モンガラカワハギ (mongarakawahgi) is rendered in katakana as a loanword for the triggerfish species. In the educational mod, this fish could trigger special in‑game effects when interacted with.
minnanocraft.token.triggerfish.example: モンガラカワハギが水中で泳いでいると、近くのプレイヤーを驚かせる (Mongarakawahgi ga suichuu de oyoide iru to, chikaku no pureiyaa wo odorokaseru) - When the triggerfish swims, it startles nearby players.
minnanocraft.token.tripwire.desc: トリップワイヤー (torippu waiyaa) is a gairaigo from English “tripwire”. In Minecraft it is the string that triggers redstone when stepped on, matching its literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.tripwire.example: トリップワイヤーが作動した！ (torippu waiyaa ga sakudoo shita!) - The tripwire activated!
minnanocraft.token.mojang.desc: 何か (nani ka) means “something”. The Mojang emblem acts as a placeholder item that can stand for any resource, echoing the notion of an undefined something.
minnanocraft.token.mojang.example: 何かが光っている。 (nani ka ga hikatte iru.) - Something is glowing.
minnanocraft.token.threadfin.desc: ツバメコノシロ (tsubame konoshiro) is rendered in katakana as a proper name. “ツバメ” (tsubame) means “swallow”, and “コノシロ” (kono shiro) denotes the slender fish, evoking its long, thin shape. In Minecraft the threadfin fish matches this description.
minnanocraft.token.threadfin.example: ツバメコノシロを釣った。 (tsubame konoshiro wo tsutta.) - I caught a threadfin.
minnanocraft.token.thrown.desc: 投げられた (nagerareta) uses the kanji 投 (to, “throw”) plus the passive past suffix られた, meaning “was thrown”. In Minecraft, projectiles such as arrows are thrown, matching the term.
minnanocraft.token.thrown.example: 矢が投げられた。 (ya ga nagerareta.) - The arrow was thrown.
minnanocraft.token.tinted.desc: 遮光 (shakoo) combines 遮 (sha, “to block”) and 光 (koo, “light”), literally “light‑blocking”. In Minecraft, tinted glass limits light transmission, aligning with the term.
minnanocraft.token.tinted.example: 遮光ガラスを設置した。 (shakoo garasu wo setchi shita.) - I placed tinted glass.
minnanocraft.token.mushroom.desc: キノコ (kinoko) is a katakana loanword from English "mushroom", matching the round, colorful block that resembles a real mushroom in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.mushroom.example: 森でキノコを集めよう (Mori de kinoko wo atsumeyou) - Let's gather mushrooms in the forest
minnanocraft.token.seagrass.desc: 海草 (kaiso) merges 海 (umi) "sea" and 草 (kusa) "grass", literally “sea grass”, matching the underwater plant harvested in ocean biomes.
minnanocraft.token.seagrass.example: 海底で海草を刈り取る (Kaitei de kaiso wo karitoru) - Harvest the seagrass at the ocean floor
minnanocraft.token.lodestone.desc: ロードストーン (roodosutoon) is a katakana loan from English "lodestone", a magnetic stone that directs compasses, mirroring its in‑game purpose.
minnanocraft.token.lodestone.example: コンパスをロードストーンに向ける (Konpasu wo roodosutoon ni mukeru) - Point the compass at the lodestone
minnanocraft.token.record.desc: レコード (rekoodo) derives from English "record", referring to the music discs that play sounds in Minecraft, preserving the original meaning of a sound recording.
minnanocraft.token.record.example: レコードをジャックに入れる (Rekoodo wo jakku ni ireru) - Insert the record into the jukebox
minnanocraft.token.mycelium.desc: 菌糸 (kinshi) combines 菌 (kin) "fungus" and 糸 (shi) "thread", describing the filamentous network of fungi, which corresponds to the mycelium block covering mushroom soil.
minnanocraft.token.mycelium.example: 菌糸の上に作物を植える (Kinshi no ue ni sakumotsu wo ueru) - Plant crops on the mycelium
minnanocraft.token.string.desc: The kanji 糸 (ito) translates to 'thread' or 'string', matching the item's role as a thin material for crafting ropes, bows, and fishing rods in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.string.example: 糸で釣り竿を作ろう (Ito de tsurizao wo tsukurou) - Let's craft a fishing rod with string.
minnanocraft.token.air.desc: 空気 (kuuki) merges 空 (kuu) ‘empty/sky’ and 気 (ki) ‘spirit, air’, denoting the invisible element that fills space in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.air.example: 空気がないと呼吸できない (Kuuki ga nai to kokyuu dekinai) - Without air you cannot breathe.
minnanocraft.token.zombified.desc: The Japanese term ゾンビ化 (zonbika) is a katakana loanword meaning 'zombified', matching the Minecraft mechanic where entities become zombies.
minnanocraft.token.zombified.example: ゾンビ化した村人は危険だ (Zonbika shita murabito wa kiken da) - A zombified villager is dangerous.
minnanocraft.token.weaving.desc: 巣張り (subari) merges 巣 (su) ‘nest’ and 張り (hari) ‘weaving, stretching’, evoking the act of interlacing threads, akin to using a loom in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.weaving.example: 巣張りで布を作ろう (Subari de nuno wo tsukurou) - Let's weave a fabric.
minnanocraft.token.light_weighted.desc: 軽量 (keiryou) combines 軽 (kei) ‘light’ and 量 (ryou) ‘weight, amount’, describing the light‑weighted pressure plate that activates with a small number of items in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.light_weighted.exampl: 軽量の圧力板は少数のアイテムで作動する (Keiryou no atsuryoku-ban wa shousuu no aitemu de sakudou suru) - The light‑weighted pressure plate activates with few items.
minnanocraft.token.tomato_clownfish.desc: ハマクマノミ (Hamakumanomi) merges ハマ (hama, reef) and クマノミ (kumanomi, "clownfish"), literally "reef clownfish", matching the orange‑red tropical fish variant in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.tomato_clownfish.exam: 水槽にハマクマノミを入れて、トマトのような色で底を照らそう (Suizoo ni Hamakumanomi wo irete, tomato no yoona iro de soko wo terasou) - Place a ハマクマノミ (Hamakumanomi) in the aquarium to brighten the seabed with tomato hues.
minnanocraft.token.sunstreak.desc: サンストリーク (Sansutorīku) is a gairaigo from English "sun streak", referring to a bright solar ray that pierces the sky, analogous to the sunbeam particles that appear in Minecraft's plains at dawn.
minnanocraft.token.sunstreak.example: 日の出にサンストリークが地平線を照らし、プレイヤーを次のバイオームへ導く (Hinode ni Sansutorīku ga chiheisen wo terashi, pureiyaa wo tsugi no baioomu e michibiku) - At sunrise, a sunstreak lights the horizon, guiding players to the next biome.
minnanocraft.token.yellow_tang.desc: Kiirohagi (キイロハギ) merges kiiro “yellow” with hagi “a fish species”; in Minecraft it matches the yellow‑tang tropical fish, mirroring its bright hue.
minnanocraft.token.yellow_tang.example: Catch a Kiirohagi and place it in the ocean monument (Kiirohagi wo tsutte, kaitei shinden ni motte ikou) - Let's catch a yellow tang and bring it to the ocean monument.
minnanocraft.token.template.desc: Kata (型) means “mold” or “shape”; in Minecraft a template is the pattern applied to banners or crafting recipes, acting as a virtual mold.
minnanocraft.token.template.example: Use a template to design a banner (Kata wo tsukatte hata no dezain wo tsukurou) - Use a template to create the banner design.
minnanocraft.token.text.desc: Tekisuto (テキスト) is a katakana gairaigo from English “text”; in Minecraft it denotes written content on signs, books, or chat.
minnanocraft.token.text.example: Write text on a sign (Kanban ni tekisuto wo kakou) - Write text on the sign.
minnanocraft.token.steel.desc: Uchi‑kin (打ち金) joins uchi “to strike” and kin “metal”, meaning “struck metal”; in Minecraft steel is the hardened iron used for durable tools.
minnanocraft.token.steel.example: A steel sword forged with uchi‑kin has high durability (Uchi‑kin de tsukutta ken wa taikyuuryoku ga takai) - A sword made of steel has high durability.
minnanocraft.token.stonecutter.desc: Ishikiri (石切) combines ishi “stone” and kiri “to cut”; in Minecraft the Stonecutter block slices stone into precise variants, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.stonecutter.example: Process stone precisely with the stonecutter (Ishikiri de ishi wo komakaku kakou shiyou) - Let's finely shape stone using the stonecutter.
minnanocraft.token.strength.desc: 力 (chikara) means 'strength' or 'power', mirroring the damage boost an item provides; the kanji depicts raw energy, akin to a Minecraft axe's strength.
minnanocraft.token.strength.example: この剣は力 (chikara) を宿している。 (Kono ken wa chikara wo yadoshite iru.) - This sword holds strength.
minnanocraft.token.stripey.desc: ストライピー (sutoraipī) is a katakana loanword from English 'stripey', describing striped blocks or banners, a visual style often seen in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.stripey.example: ストライピーの旗は光る。 (Sutoraipī no hata wa hikaru.) - The stripey banner glows.
minnanocraft.token.spit.desc: 唾 (tsuba) means 'saliva'; the kanji denotes the fluid an animal can eject, similar to a wolf spitting when it attacks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.spit.example: 狼は唾 (tsuba) を飛ばす。 (ookami wa tsuba wo tobasu.) - The wolf spits saliva.
minnanocraft.token.splash.desc: スプラッシュ (supurasshu) is a katakana loanword of 'splash', indicating a liquid spreading effect, as seen with splash potions that burst on impact.
minnanocraft.token.splash.example: スプラッシュのポーションが飛び散る。 (Supurasshu no pooshon ga tobichiru.) - The splash potion bursts.
minnanocraft.token.spore.desc: 胞子 (hooshi) merges 胞 (hoo, 'cell') and 子 (shi, 'offspring, seed'), meaning 'spore'; in Minecraft, spores drift from mushrooms and fungi.
minnanocraft.token.spore.example: 胞子 (hooshi) が森に漂う。 (Hooshi ga mori ni tadayou.) - Spores drift through the forest.
minnanocraft.token.spotty.desc: スポッティー (Supottī) is a gairaigo from English “spotty”, rendered in katakana; in Minecraft it describes blocks with irregular spots, such as spotted wool.
minnanocraft.token.spotty.example: The block has a spotted pattern. (Kono burokkku wa supottī na moyoo wo motte iru.) - The block has a spotted pattern.
minnanocraft.token.with.desc: 付き (tsuki) combines the kanji 付 meaning “attach” with the verb ending き, conveying “with” or “attached”. In Minecraft it appears in phrases like “block with redstone”.
minnanocraft.token.with.example: The chest is with a lock. (Chesuto wa rokkoo to tsuki de aru.) - The chest is with a lock.
minnanocraft.token.slowness.desc: 鈍化 (donka) combines 鈍 “dull, slow” and 化 “change”, meaning “to become slow”. In Minecraft the Slowness potion slows the player’s movement.
minnanocraft.token.slowness.example: Slowness slows your steps. (Donka ga anata no ashi wo yukkuri saseru.) - Slowness slows your steps.
minnanocraft.token.smithing.desc: 鍛冶 (kanji) combines 鍛 “forge, temper” and 冶 “smelt, metallurgy”, denoting blacksmithing. In Minecraft the smithing table upgrades tools.
minnanocraft.token.smithing.example: Upgrade the armor at the smithing table. (Kanji no tēburu de boogu wo kooshin suru.) - Upgrade the armor at the smithing table.
minnanocraft.token.tool.desc: 道具 (doogu) is made of 道 “road, way” and 具 “implement”. It denotes an implement or tool, matching Minecraft’s items like pickaxes.
minnanocraft.token.tool.example: Use the shovel as a tool. (Doogu no soraiboo wo tsukau.) - Use the shovel as a tool.
minnanocraft.token.red_snapper.desc: フエダイ (Fuedai) is rendered in katakana, marking it as a loanword or stylistic choice; the components フエ (fue) and ダイ (dai) allude to 鯛 (tai), a sea‑bream type fish. In Minecraft, the Red Snapper swims in rivers with a vivid red hue, matching the name’s implication.
minnanocraft.token.red_snapper.example: 川でフエダイを釣ると、経験値が増える (Kawa de Fuedai wo tsuru to, keikenchi ga fueru) - Fishing a Red Snapper in the river grants extra experience.
minnanocraft.token.snooper.desc: スヌーパー (Sunuupaa) is written in katakana, showing it is a gairaigo from English “snooper”. It denotes a mob that sniffs out items, similar to a treasure‑hunting creature in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.snooper.example: 洞窟でスヌーパーが宝箱を探す (Doukutsu de Sunuupaa ga takarabako wo sagasu) - In caves, the Snooper searches chests.
minnanocraft.token.wheat_sheaf.desc: 麦束 (Mugi‑taba) merges 麦 (mugi, “wheat”) and 束 (taba, “bundle”). In Minecraft, the Wheat Sheaf is a bundle of harvested wheat, useful for crafting food or trading.
minnanocraft.token.wheat_sheaf.example: 農場で麦束を集めてパンを作る (Noujou de Mugi‑taba wo atsumete pan wo tsukuru) - Gather wheat sheaves on the farm to bake bread.
minnanocraft.token.shepherd.desc: 羊飼い (Hitsuji‑kai) combines 羊 (hitsuji, “sheep”) and 飼い (kai, from 飼う, “to keep”). In Minecraft, the Shepherd directs sheep to grazing areas and can collect wool.
minnanocraft.token.shepherd.example: 羊飼いは羊を牧草地へ連れて行く (Hitsuji‑kai wa hitsuji wo bokusouchi e tsurete iku) - The Shepherd leads sheep to the pasture.
minnanocraft.token.bamboo_shoot.desc: タケノコ (Takenoko) is written in katakana, a stylized rendering of the native word for “bamboo shoot”. In Minecraft, Bamboo Shoots sprout from bamboo and can be used as food or crafting material.
minnanocraft.token.bamboo_shoot.example: ジャングルでタケノコを収穫して料理する (Janguru de Takenoko wo shuukaku shite ryouri suru) - Harvest bamboo shoots in the jungle and cook them.
minnanocraft.token.shrieker.desc: Shri​ker (シュリーカー, Shurīkaa) is written in katakana as a gairaigo from English "shriek", mirroring the mob's loud scream when it spots a player, which triggers the warning mechanic.
minnanocraft.token.shrieker.example: シュリーカーが洞窟で鳴くと、すぐに近くのプレイヤーが警戒する。 (Shurīkaa ga dookutsu de naku to, sugu ni chikaku no pureiyaa ga keikai suru.) - When a shrieker screams in a cave, nearby players become instantly alert.
minnanocraft.token.slow_speed.desc: Slow_speed uses the kanji compound 低速 (Teisoku), where 低 means "low" and 速 means "speed", denoting a reduced movement rate, as seen in slow pistons or mobs.
minnanocraft.token.slow_speed.example: 低速のピストンはブロックをゆっくり押し出す。 (Teisoku no pisuton wa buroku wo yukkuri oshidasu.) - A slow-speed piston pushes blocks slowly.
minnanocraft.token.repeating.desc: Repeating is rendered as リピート (Ripīto) in katakana, a gairaigo from English "repeat", referring to loops such as redstone repeaters that continuously cycle signals.
minnanocraft.token.repeating.example: リピート回路は信号を永遠に繰り返す。 (Ripīto kairo wa shingoo wo eien ni kurikaesu.) - A repeating circuit endlessly cycles the signal.
minnanocraft.token.resistance.desc: Resistance uses the kanji 抵抗 (Teikoo), where 抵 means "to resist" and 抗 means "to oppose", matching the in‑game potion that lessens incoming damage.
minnanocraft.token.resistance.example: 抵抗のポーションを飲むと、ダメージが減少する。 (Teikoo no pooshon wo nomu to, dameiji ga genshoo suru.) - Drinking a resistance potion reduces damage.
minnanocraft.token.respawn.desc: Respawn appears as リスポーン (Risupoon) in katakana, a gairaigo from English "respawn", denoting the location where a player reappears after death.
minnanocraft.token.respawn.example: リスポーン地点に戻ると、再び冒険を続けられる。 (Risupoon chiten ni modoru to, futatabi booken wo tsuzukerareru.) - Returning to the respawn point lets you continue the adventure.
minnanocraft.token.rotten.desc: Fushuu (腐臭) merges 腐 (fuku, decay) and 臭 (shuu, stink). In Minecraft, rotten blocks emit this odor, indicating decay and often drawing hostile mobs.
minnanocraft.token.rotten.example: 腐臭が漂う洞窟でスケルトンが湧く。 (Fushuu ga tadayou dookutsu de sukuretton ga waku.) - Skeletons spawn in a cave filled with a rotten smell.
minnanocraft.token.rotted.desc: Kusatta (腐った) employs the kanji 腐 (fuku, rot) in its past‑tense adjective form, meaning “rotted”. In Minecraft, rotted wood serves as a low‑grade fuel.
minnanocraft.token.rotted.example: 腐った木材は燃料として使える。 (Kusatta mokuzai wa nenryoo toshite tsukaeru.) - Rotted wood can be used as fuel.
minnanocraft.token.sculk.desc: Sukaruku (スカルク) is a katakana transcription of the English “sculk”. It names the mysterious, spreading block that behaves like a glowing fungus in caves.
minnanocraft.token.sculk.example: スカルクの根が地下に広がる。 (Sukaruku no ne ga chika ni hirogaru.) - Sculk veins spread underground.
minnanocraft.token.duplicate.desc: Fuku (副) translates to “secondary” or “auxiliary”. In Minecraft context, a duplicate chest acts as a secondary storage mirroring the main chest.
minnanocraft.token.duplicate.example: 副のチェストはメインと同じアイテムを保持する。 (Fuku no chesuto wa mein to onaji aitemu wo hoji suru.) - The secondary chest holds the same items as the primary.
minnanocraft.token.shape.desc: Keijoo (形状) merges 形 (katachi, shape) and 状 (joo, condition). In Minecraft, shape blocks let players modify the geometry of structures.
minnanocraft.token.shape.example: 形状ブロックで建築のデザインを変える。 (Keijoo burokku de kenchiku no dezain wo kaeru.) - Use shape blocks to alter building designs.
minnanocraft.token.shaped.desc: The kanji 傘 (kasa) means ‘umbrella’; in Minecraft, ‘shaped’ recipes have a defined outline like an umbrella’s canopy, showing that the crafting pattern matters.
minnanocraft.token.shaped.example: 傘を作るために形を整える。 (Kasa wo tsukuru tame ni katachi wo totonoeru.) - I arrange the shape to craft an umbrella.
minnanocraft.token.regeneration.desc: 再 (sai) ‘again’ + 生 (sei) ‘life’; together 再生 (saisei) means ‘regeneration’. In Minecraft, the Regeneration effect slowly restores health, as if the player is reborn.
minnanocraft.token.regeneration.example: 再生のポーションを飲んで体力が回復した。 (Saisei no pooshon wo nonde tairyoku ga kaifuku shita.) - I drank a regeneration potion and my health recovered.
minnanocraft.token.potion.desc: ポーション (pooshon) is a katakana loanword from English ‘potion’. In Minecraft, potions are bottles that hold magical effects.
minnanocraft.token.potion.example: ポーションを作るために醸造台を使う。 (Pooshon wo tsukuru tame ni joozoodai wo tsukau.) - I use the brewing stand to make potions.
minnanocraft.token.potted.desc: 植木鉢 (ueki‑bachi) merges 植 ‘to plant’, 木 ‘tree’, 鉢 ‘pot’; literally ‘plant pot’. In Minecraft, ‘potted’ blocks are plants placed in pots.
minnanocraft.token.potted.example: 植木鉢にサボテンを入れる。 (Ueki‑bachi ni saboten wo ireru.) - I put a cactus into a pot.
minnanocraft.token.effect.desc: 効果 (kooka) combines 効 ‘effectiveness’ and 果 ‘result’; it means ‘effect’ or ‘power’. In Minecraft, ‘effect’ denotes the status granted by potions or enchantments.
minnanocraft.token.effect.example: 効果のあるポーションを飲む。 (Kooka no aru pooshon wo nomu.) - I drink a potion with an effect.
minnanocraft.token.pressure.desc: 圧力 (atsuryoku) merges 圧 (atsu, "press") + 力 (chikara, "power"). In Minecraft, pressure plates sense applied force, mirroring the notion of pressure.
minnanocraft.token.pressure.example: 圧力板が作動した！ (Atsuryoku‑ban ga sadoo shita!) - The pressure plate activated!
minnanocraft.token.pod.desc: さや (saya) written in hiragana denotes a native word for "pod". In Minecraft, cocoa pods are blocks that hold beans.
minnanocraft.token.pod.example: さやからカカオ豆を収穫した。 (Saya kara kakao mame wo shuukaku shita.) - I harvested cocoa beans from the pod.
minnanocraft.token.point.desc: 先 (saki) means "tip" or "ahead". In Minecraft, the tip of a sword or a forward point aligns with this meaning.
minnanocraft.token.point.example: 剣の先が光っている。 (Ken no saki ga hikatte iru.) - The sword's point is glowing.
minnanocraft.token.poison.desc: 毒 (doku) stands for "poison". In Minecraft, the poison effect slowly drains health, matching the toxin idea.
minnanocraft.token.poison.example: 毒のポーションを飲んだ。 (Doku no pooshon wo nonda.) - I drank a poison potion.
minnanocraft.token.poisonous.desc: 青くなった (aoku natta) merges 青 (ao, "blue") + く (adjectival) + なった (became). In Minecraft, poisonous mobs show blue particles, echoing "turned blue".
minnanocraft.token.poisonous.example: 毒性のあるスライムは青くなった。 (Dokusē no aru suraimu wa aoku natta.) - The poisonous slime turned blue.
minnanocraft.token.parrotfish.desc: The term ブダイ (Budai) is written in katakana, stylizing the native name for the brightly colored fish. In Minecraft, the Parrotfish swims among coral, mirroring the vivid budai appearance.
minnanocraft.token.parrotfish.example: 海底でブダイが泳いでいる。 (Kaitei de Budai ga oyoide iru.) - A parrotfish swims in the ocean depths.
minnanocraft.token.pitcher_plant.desc: Utsubokazura (ウツボカズラ) written in katakana denotes the carnivorous plant with cup-shaped leaves. In Minecraft, the Pitcher Plant lures mobs into a liquid trap, echoing the plant's cup.
minnanocraft.token.pitcher_plant.example: 沼地にウツボカズラが生えている。 (Numachi ni Utsubokazura ga haete iru.) - A pitcher plant grows in the swamp.
minnanocraft.token.plate.desc: 皿 (sara) literally means 'plate'. In Minecraft, a plate acts as a pressure plate, triggering mechanisms when stepped on, akin to a dish sensing weight.
minnanocraft.token.plate.example: 石の皿を踏んでドアが開く。 (Ishi no sara wo funde doa ga hiraku.) - Stepping on the stone plate opens the door.
minnanocraft.token.oozing.desc: 滲出 (shinjutsu) merges 滲 'seep' and 出 'exit', describing a leaking fluid. In Minecraft, oozing blocks release slime that spreads across surfaces.
minnanocraft.token.oozing.example: 壁から滲出が流れ出す。 (Kabe kara shinjutsu ga nagare dasu.) - Oozing flows out from the wall.
minnanocraft.token.open.desc: 開 (kai) means 'open'. In Minecraft, the open action opens doors, chests, or village gates.
minnanocraft.token.open.example: ドアを開くと光が入る。 (Doa wo hiraku to hikari ga hairu.) - When you open the door, light enters.
minnanocraft.token.swiftness.desc: The term 俊敏 (shunbin) merges 俊 (shun, "talented, swift") and 敏 (bin, "quick, nimble"), mirroring the speed boost given by the Swiftness potion in Minecraft, which raises the player's movement speed.
minnanocraft.token.swiftness.example: 速さの風が私を包む (Hayasa no kaze ga watashi wo tsutsumu) - The wind of swiftness envelops me
minnanocraft.token.blue_tang.desc: ナンヨウハギ (nanyouhagi) is written in katakana, marking it as a gairaigo for the blue tropical fish that spawns in Minecraft's ocean reefs.
minnanocraft.token.blue_tang.example: 青い魚が珊瑚の間を泳ぐ (Aoi sakana ga sango no ma wo oyogu) - Blue fish swim among the coral
minnanocraft.token.black_tang.desc: ヒレナガハギ (hirenagahagi) is rendered in katakana, a loanword naming the dark-colored tropical fish that appears in Minecraft's deep ocean biomes.
minnanocraft.token.black_tang.example: 暗い海で黒い魚が光る (Kurai umi de kuroi sakana ga hikaru) - In the dark sea, the black fish glows
minnanocraft.token.ornate.desc: ハナグロ (hanaguro) appears in katakana, a stylized label for the ornate fish with striking patterns, often used as a decorative aquarium inhabitant in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.ornate.example: 装飾的な魚が水槽を彩る (Soushokuteki na sakana ga suiso wo irodoru) - The ornate fish adorns the tank
minnanocraft.token.oxeye.desc: フランス (furansu) is katakana for "France"; the Oxeye Daisy in Minecraft evokes the look of French meadow flowers, explaining the foreign loanword.
minnanocraft.token.oxeye.example: フランスの野原に似た花が咲く (Furansu no nohara ni nita hana ga saku) - Flowers resembling those of French fields bloom
minnanocraft.token.style.desc: The term 風 (kaze) means "wind" and is also used for "style" or "manner" (e.g., 風流 fuuryuu). In Minecraft, wind represents fluid design, reflected in templates that adopt a breezy style.
minnanocraft.token.style.example: This template follows the wind style (kaze no dezain) - This template follows the wind style.
minnanocraft.token.ornament.desc: 装飾 (sooshoku) merges 装 (soo, "to equip") and 飾 (shoku, "to adorn"). In Minecraft it denotes decorative details such as armor trims or ornamental blocks.
minnanocraft.token.ornament.example: Adding ornament (sooshoku) to armor changes its appearance (yoroi ni sooshoku wo tsukeru to mitame ga kawarimasu) - Adding ornament to armor changes its appearance.
minnanocraft.token.music.desc: 音楽 (ongaku) combines 音 (on, "sound") and 楽 (gaku, "pleasure, music"). In Minecraft, note blocks and jukeboxes produce music that can affect mob behavior.
minnanocraft.token.music.example: When music (ongaku) plays, mobs start dancing (ongaku ga nagareru to mobu ga odoridasu) - When music plays, mobs start dancing.
minnanocraft.token.mutton.desc: 羊 (hitsuji) means "sheep". In Minecraft, the meat harvested from a sheep is the mutton item.
minnanocraft.token.mutton.example: Cook the sheep's meat (hitsuji no niku) to make mutton (hitsuji no niku wo yaite ryoori suru) - Cook the sheep's meat to make mutton.
minnanocraft.token.nitwit.desc: Mushoku (無職) merges 無 “nothing” and 職 “job”, mirroring the villager that holds no profession, the nitwit.
minnanocraft.token.nitwit.example: Mushoku no murabito wa nanimo tsukuranai. (Mushoku no murabito wa nanimo tsukuranai.) - The nitwit villager creates nothing.
minnanocraft.token.turtle_master.desc: Taatoru masutaa (タートルマスター) is a katakana loanword joining “turtle” and “master”, denoting the Turtle Master boss.
minnanocraft.token.turtle_master.example: Taatoru masutaa ga chikaku ni iru. (Taatoru masutaa ga chikaku ni iru.) - The Turtle Master is nearby.
minnanocraft.token.moorish.desc: Tsunodashi (ツノダシ) in katakana names a spiky fish, matching the Moorish Idol's pointed fins.
minnanocraft.token.moorish.example: Tsunodashi ga suichuu de oyoide iru. (Tsunodashi ga suichuu de oyoide iru.) - The Moorish Idol swims in the water.
minnanocraft.token.moving.desc: Sadoochuu (作動中) combines 作 “make”, 動 “move”, and 中 “inside”, signifying a block currently operating, such as a moving piston.
minnanocraft.token.moving.example: Piston wa sadoochuu da. (Piston wa sadoochuu da.) - The piston is active.
minnanocraft.token.luck.desc: Kooun (幸運) merges 幸 “happiness” and 運 “fate”, embodying luck that boosts loot drops and positive effects.
minnanocraft.token.luck.example: Kooun no enchanto wa takarabako wo ake yasuku suru. (Kooun no enchanto wa takarabako wo ake yasuku suru.) - The Luck enchantment makes chests easier to open.
minnanocraft.token.mannequin.desc: マネキン (manekin) is a katakana loanword denoting the mannequin that appears in Minecraft as the armor stand, echoing a static figure for displaying gear.
minnanocraft.token.mannequin.example: このマネキンに防具を装着しよう。 (Kono manekin ni boogu wo soochaku shiyoo.) - Let's equip this mannequin with armor.
minnanocraft.token.map.desc: 地図 (chizu) merges 地 (chi, earth) and 図 (zu, diagram), literally “earth diagram”; in Minecraft the map displays the world’s terrain.
minnanocraft.token.map.example: 洞窟の入口を地図で確認した。 (Dookutsu no iriguchi wo chizu de kakunin shita.) - I checked the cave entrance on the map.
minnanocraft.token.marker.desc: マーカー (maakaa) is a katakana loan from English “marker”, employed to flag locations on Minecraft maps.
minnanocraft.token.marker.example: 重要な地点にマーカーを置いた。 (Juuyoo na chiten ni maakaa wo oita.) - I placed a marker at the important spot.
minnanocraft.token.mason.desc: 石工 (sekoo) joins 石 (seki, stone) and 工 (koo, craft), meaning “stone worker”; in Minecraft the mason builds stone structures.
minnanocraft.token.mason.example: 石工が新しい壁を作ってくれた。 (Sekoo ga atarashii kabe wo tsukutte kureta.) - The mason built a new wall.
minnanocraft.token.leaf_litter.desc: 落ち葉 (ochiba) splits into 落ち (ochi, fall) and 葉 (ha, leaf), denoting fallen leaves; in Minecraft leaf litter blankets forest floors.
minnanocraft.token.leaf_litter.example: 森の床は落ち葉で覆われている。 (Mori no yuka wa ochiba de oowarete iru.) - The forest floor is covered with leaf litter.
minnanocraft.token.loom.desc: 機織り機 (kioriki) merges 機 (machine) and 織 (weave), denoting a weaving device. In Minecraft, the loom lets players craft banner patterns, mirroring its literal purpose.
minnanocraft.token.loom.example: 私は新しい機織り機で旗を作る (Watashi wa atarashii kioriki de hata wo tsukuru) - I craft a banner with the new loom.
minnanocraft.token.leaf.desc: 葉 (ha) means "leaf". In Minecraft, leaves form the canopy of trees and drop as items, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.leaf.example: 葉が風に揺れるとき、森が生きていると感じる (Ha ga kaze ni yureru toki, mori ga ikiteiru to kanjiru) - When leaves sway in the wind, I feel the forest is alive.
minnanocraft.token.leaping.desc: 跳躍 (chouyaku) combines 跳 (jump) and 躍 (leap), emphasizing a high jump. In Minecraft, the Leaping effect raises jump height, mirroring the term's meaning.
minnanocraft.token.leaping.example: 跳躍のポーションを飲んで、崖を越える (Chouyaku no pooshon wo nonde, gake wo koeru) - Drink the leaping potion to clear the cliff.
minnanocraft.token.leash.desc: リード (riido) is a loanword from English "lead", denoting the rope that ties animals. In Minecraft, the leash lets players tether mobs to a point, functioning as a tether.
minnanocraft.token.leash.example: リードでウマをつなぎ、牧場へ連れて行く (Riido de uma wo tsunagi, bokujou e tsurete iku) - Tie the horse with a leash and lead it to the farm.
minnanocraft.token.leatherworker.desc: 革細工師 (kawasaiku-shi) merges 革 (leather), 細工 (craft) and 師 (master), denoting a leather craftsman. In Minecraft, the leatherworker creates leather armor and related items, matching the profession.
minnanocraft.token.leatherworker.example: 革細工師は新しい皮の鎧を作った (Kawasaiku-shi wa atarashii kawa no yoroi wo tsukutta) - The leatherworker crafted a new leather armor.
minnanocraft.token.levitation.desc: 浮 (fu) means 'to float' and 余 (yuu) 'to hover'; together they make 浮遊 (fuyuu) 'floating'. In Minecraft, the Levitation effect lifts the player as if floating, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.levitation.example: 私は空中で浮遊している。 (Watashi wa kuuchuu de fuyuu shite iru.) - I am floating in the air.
minnanocraft.token.librarian.desc: 司 (shi) 'to administer' + 書 (sho) 'book, writing' → 司書 (shisho) 'librarian'. In Minecraft, the Librarian villager trades books, embodying the role of a keeper of written knowledge.
minnanocraft.token.librarian.example: 司書は新しい本を提供した。 (Shisho wa atarashii hon wo teikyoo shita.) - The librarian offered a new book.
minnanocraft.token.light.desc: 光 (hikari) means 'light'. In Minecraft, light sources such as torches and glowstone brighten dark spaces, directly mirroring the kanji's meaning.
minnanocraft.token.light.example: 光が洞窟を照らす。 (Hikari ga dookutsu wo terasu.) - Light shines into the cave.
minnanocraft.token.lightning_bolt.desc: 雷 (kaminari) stands for 'thunder' or 'lightning'. The Lightning Bolt spell in Minecraft summons a bolt that strikes and ignites, matching the kanji's meaning.
minnanocraft.token.lightning_bolt.exampl: 雷が木の上に落ちた。 (Kaminari ga ki no ue ni ochita.) - A lightning bolt struck the tree.
minnanocraft.token.lingering.desc: 残 (zan) 'remaining' + 留 (ryuu) 'to stay' → 残留 (zanryuu) 'lingering'. In Minecraft, lingering potions keep their effect for an extended period, embodying the notion of persistence.
minnanocraft.token.lingering.example: 残留の効果が長く続く。 (Zanryuu no kooka ga nagaku tsuzuku.) - The lingering effect lasts a long time.
minnanocraft.token.invisibility.desc: The term 透明化 (toumeika) merges 透 (transparent) + 明 (clear) + 化 (change), mirroring the potion that makes the player invisible, a literal transparent transformation.
minnanocraft.token.invisibility.example: 私の透明化のポーションで敵を見えなくした。 (Watashi no toumeika no pooshon de teki wo mienaku shita.) - I made the enemies invisible with my invisibility potion.
minnanocraft.token.item.desc: アイテム (aitemu) is written in katakana, marking it as a gairaigo from English "item", denoting any manipulable object in the game.
minnanocraft.token.item.example: 新しいアイテムをチェストに入れた。 (Atarashii aitemu wo chesuto ni ireta.) - I placed the new item in the chest.
minnanocraft.token.jigsaw.desc: ジグソー (jigusoo) appears in katakana as a loanword from "jigsaw"; in Minecraft, jigsaw blocks link structural pieces like a physical puzzle.
minnanocraft.token.jigsaw.example: ジグソーブロックで新しい村を作った。 (Jigusoo burokku de atarashii mura wo tsukutta.) - I built a new village using jigsaw blocks.
minnanocraft.token.killer.desc: 殺人 (satsujin) combines 殺 (kill) + 人 (person), meaning "murder"; in Minecraft, "killer" labels mobs or traps that kill the player.
minnanocraft.token.killer.example: 森の中で殺人モブに遭遇した。 (Mori no naka de satsujin mobu ni soogu shita.) - I encountered a killer mob in the forest.
minnanocraft.token.knot.desc: 結び目 (musubime) comprises 結 (tie) + び (hiragana) + 目 (eye), meaning "knot"; in Minecraft, knots are seen in leads and ropes that tether mobs.
minnanocraft.token.knot.example: リードの結び目で羊をつなげた。 (Rīdo no musubime de hitsuji wo tsunageta.) - I tethered the sheep with the lead's knot.
minnanocraft.token.person.desc: The kanji 人 (hito) means “person”. In Minecraft it denotes NPCs such as villagers, the human-like entities that populate the world.
minnanocraft.token.person.example: 村人は人です (Mura-bito wa hito desu) - Villagers are persons.
minnanocraft.token.kob.desc: コーブ (koobu) is written in katakana as a gairaigo from English “cove”. In Minecraft it refers to a small inlet of water that can serve as a natural shelter.
minnanocraft.token.kob.example: 川のコーブに小屋を建てよう (Kawa no koobu ni koya wo tatete yoo) - Build a hut in the river cove.
minnanocraft.token.ingredients.desc: 材料 (zairyoo) merges 材 (zai, “material”) and 料 (ryoo, “ingredient, charge”). In Minecraft it designates the items required for crafting or brewing recipes.
minnanocraft.token.ingredients.example: 鍋に材料を入れる (Nabe ni zairyoo wo ireru) - Add the ingredients to the cauldron.
minnanocraft.token.interact.desc: 交流 (kooryuu) combines 交 (koo, “exchange”) and 流 (ryuu, “flow”). In Minecraft it refers to the exchange of items or communication between players and entities.
minnanocraft.token.interact.example: プレイヤー同士の交流が重要だ (Pureiyaa dooshi no kooryuu ga juuyoo da) - Player interaction is crucial.
minnanocraft.token.healing.desc: 治癒 (chiyu) merges 治 (chi, “to cure”) and 癒 (yu, “to heal”). In Minecraft it is linked to potions or effects that restore health.
minnanocraft.token.healing.example: 回復のポーションは治癒効果がある (Kaifuku no pooshon wa chiyu kooka ga aru) - Healing potions provide a healing effect.
minnanocraft.token.heavy.desc: ヘビー (Hebii) is a loanword from English meaning heavy; Minecraft blocks such as stone or iron are heavy and emit a loud thud when they fall.
minnanocraft.token.heavy.example: このヘビーな鉱石は落とすと音が大きい。 (Kono Hebii na kooseki wa otosu to oto ga ookii.) - This heavy ore makes a loud sound when dropped.
minnanocraft.token.hook.desc: フック (Fukku) is a loanword from English “hook”; in Minecraft it is used to attach items, build traps, or fish, matching its literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.hook.example: フックを使って木の上に吊るす。 (Fukku wo tsukatte ki no ue ni tsurusu.) - Use the hook to hang it from the tree.
minnanocraft.token.indented.desc: 山形波 (Yamagata-nami) merges 山 (yama, “mountain”), 形 (kata, “shape”), and 波 (nami, “wave”); it describes wavy, stepped surfaces like indented stone bricks in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.indented.example: 山形波の壁は光が反射して美しい。 (Yamagata-nami no kabe wa hikari ga hansha shite utsukushii.) - The indented wall reflects light beautifully.
minnanocraft.token.giant.desc: ジャイアント (Jaianto) is a loanword from English “giant”; in Minecraft it denotes massive mobs or structures, such as the Ender Dragon or giant towers.
minnanocraft.token.giant.example: ジャイアントの樹は空へ伸びている。 (Jaianto no ki wa sora e nobite iru.) - The giant tree reaches up to the sky.
minnanocraft.token.glistering.desc: きらめく (kirameku) is a native verb meaning “to sparkle”; in Minecraft the Glistering effect shines like a luminous potion.
minnanocraft.token.glistering.example: きらめくエンチャントが剣を照らす。 (Kirameku enchanto ga ken wo terasu.) - The glistering enchantment lights up the sword.
minnanocraft.token.glitter.desc: Glitter (Gurittaa) is a gairaigo loanword that mimics the sparkling particles effect, similar to the glitter dust particles that appear when using sparkle items in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.glitter.example: The sky glitters with glitter (Sora ga Gurittaa de kagayaku) - The sky glitters with glitter
minnanocraft.token.goatfish.desc: Goatfish (Himeji) is rendered in katakana, marking it as a fish name; in Minecraft it denotes a slender fish that swims in deep river biomes.
minnanocraft.token.goatfish.example: I caught a goatfish in the river's depths (Kawa no shinkai de Himeji wo tsuratta) - I caught a goatfish in the river's depths
minnanocraft.token.guster.desc: Guster (Kaze maku mono) merges 風 (kaze – wind), 巻く (maku – to coil) and 者 (mono – being) to denote a wind‑wrapping entity; in Minecraft it is a block that generates air vortices when triggered.
minnanocraft.token.guster.example: The guster creates a vortex around the tower (Gasutaa ga too no mawari ni uzu wo tsukuru) - The guster creates a vortex around the tower
minnanocraft.token.harming.desc: Harming (Fushoo) combines 負 (fu – to bear, damage) and 傷 (shoo – wound), signifying injury; in Minecraft it denotes the damage a player takes from falls or attacks.
minnanocraft.token.harming.example: He was injured after falling off a cliff (Kare wa gake kara ochite Fushoo shita) - He was injured after falling off a cliff
minnanocraft.token.flopper.desc: Flopper (Furoppaa) is a katakana gairaigo naming the jumping, floating creature, reminiscent of the mob that hops in water in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.flopper.example: The flopper hops around the pond (Furoppaa ga ike no mawari de hanemawaru) - The flopper hops around the pond
minnanocraft.token.frosted_ice.desc: Frosted Ice (usui koori) merges 薄 (usui, "thin") and 氷 (koori, "ice"); its semi‑transparent texture mirrors the thin ice that forms on cold Minecraft biomes.
minnanocraft.token.frosted_ice.example: 薄氷の上で氷柱を作る。 (Usui koori no ue de hyoochuu wo tsukuru.) - Create icicles on frosted ice.
minnanocraft.token.full.desc: Full (manpai) combines 満 (man, "full") and 杯 (hai, "cup"); it denotes containers that have reached capacity, such as buckets or cauldrons in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.full.example: バケツが満杯になると水が溢れる。 (Baketsu ga manpai ni naru to mizu ga afureru.) - When a bucket becomes full, water overflows.
minnanocraft.token.gateway.desc: Gateway (gētowei) is a katakana loanword from English; it labels portals that link separate dimensions or regions in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.gateway.example: ゲートウェイを通ってエンドへ行く。 (Gētowei wo tootte Endo e iku.) - Go through the gateway to reach the End.
minnanocraft.token.fishing.desc: Fishing (tsuri) employs the kanji 釣 (tsuri, "to fish") with hiragana; it denotes the mechanic of casting a line to catch aquatic mobs in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.fishing.example: 湖で釣りをするとサーモンが出る。 (Mizuumi de tsuri wo suru to saamon ga deru.) - Fishing in a lake yields salmon.
minnanocraft.token.flesh.desc: Flesh (niku) translates to "meat"; in Minecraft it refers to raw flesh dropped by mobs such as zombies or pigs.
minnanocraft.token.flesh.example: ゾンビの肉は調理して食べられる。 (Zonbi no niku wa choori shite taberareru.) - Zombie flesh can be cooked and eaten.
minnanocraft.token.fletcher.desc: The term 矢師 (yashi) combines 矢 'arrow' and 師 'master', denoting a specialist who crafts arrows, matching the fletcher NPC who creates arrows in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.fletcher.example: 矢師は新しい矢を作る (Yashi wa atarashii ya wo tsukuru) - The fletcher crafts new arrows.
minnanocraft.token.fletching.desc: The term 矢細工 (yasaiku) merges 矢 'arrow' and 細工 'fine work', referring to the process of adding feathers to arrows, a prerequisite for bow usage in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.fletching.example: 矢細工で矢に羽根を付ける (Yasaiku de ya ni hane wo tsukeru) - Attach feathers to arrows with fletching.
minnanocraft.token.flight.desc: The term 飛翔 (hishou) joins 飛 'fly' and 翔 'soar', describing free flight, as experienced when using an Elytra in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.flight.example: エリトラで飛翔する (Erutora de hishou suru) - Soar with an Elytra.
minnanocraft.token.farmland.desc: The term 耕地 (kouchi) combines 耕 'till' and 地 'land', referring to tilled soil for crops, precisely the farmland block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.farmland.example: 耕地に小麦を植える (Kouchi ni komugi wo ueru) - Plant wheat on farmland.
minnanocraft.token.fermented.desc: The term 発酵 (hakkou) merges 発 'produce' and 酵 'fermentation', describing the process that transforms ingredients, such as the fermented spider eye used in potions in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.fermented.example: 発酵したクモの目でポーションを作る (Hakkou shita kumo no me de pooshon wo tsukuru) - Brew a potion with fermented spider eye.
minnanocraft.token.field.desc: Bun'ya (分野) merges the kanjis 分 (divide) and 野 (plain), denoting an open area; in Minecraft, a field is a cultivated plot where crops are grown, matching the literal meaning.
minnanocraft.token.field.example: In this field, crops grow. (Kono bun'ya de wa sakumotsu ga sodatsu.) - この分野では作物が育つ。
minnanocraft.token.fireball.desc: Hi no tama (火の玉) combines fire and ball, literally a fire sphere; in Minecraft, Ghast fireballs are incendiary projectiles matching this description.
minnanocraft.token.fireball.example: The fireball shoots into the sky. (Hi no tama ga sora e tobidasu.) - 火の玉が空へ飛び出す。
minnanocraft.token.fish.desc: Sakana (魚) directly translates to fish; in Minecraft, fish are edible items harvested by fishing in water bodies.
minnanocraft.token.fish.example: Let's catch and eat fish. (Sakana wo tsutte tabeyou.) - 魚を釣って食べよう。
minnanocraft.token.explosions.desc: Genbakushou (原爆症) merges origin, explosion, and syndrome, denoting a condition from blasts; in Minecraft, TNT or creeper explosions propagate damage akin to a spreading affliction.
minnanocraft.token.explosions.example: Explosions spread like radiation sickness. (Genbakushou no you ni bakuhatsu ga hirogaru.) - 原爆症のように爆発が広がる。
minnanocraft.token.eyeblossom.desc: Hitomiso (ヒトミソウ) is written in katakana, marking it as a stylized loanword; in Minecraft, it could represent a glowing flower resembling a shining eye.
minnanocraft.token.eyeblossom.example: The eyeblossom glows. (Hitomiso ga hikaru.) - ヒトミソウが光る。
minnanocraft.token.fade.desc: The verb 萎む (imu) means 'to wilt' or 'to fade', composed of the kanji 萎 (wilt) plus the verb ending む. In Minecraft, the fade mechanic makes particles or blocks gradually disappear, akin to something wilting.
minnanocraft.token.fade.example: 葉が萎むとき、光が薄れゆく。 (Ha ga imu toki, hikari ga usure yuku.) - When the leaves wilt, the light fades.
minnanocraft.token.fall.desc: 落下 (rakka) merges 落 (fall) and 下 (down). It denotes the act of falling, matching the in‑game physics when entities experience fall damage.
minnanocraft.token.fall.example: 岩が落下し、地面に激しく衝突した。 (Iwa ga rakka shi, jimen ni hageshiku shoototsu shita.) - A rock fell and collided violently with the ground.
minnanocraft.token.farmer.desc: 農民 (noomin) combines 農 (agriculture) and 民 (people). It labels the villager who farms, mirroring his function in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.farmer.example: 農民は畑で小麦を収穫した。 (Noomin wa hatake de komugi wo shuukaku shita.) - The farmer harvested wheat in the field.
minnanocraft.token.area_effect_cloud.des: エリアエフェクトクラウド is a katakana transcription of the English terms 'area effect cloud'. It denotes the particle cloud that applies status effects in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.area_effect_cloud.exa: エリアエフェクトクラウドが広がり、近くのプレイヤーに毒を与える。 (Eria efekkuto kuraudo ga hirogari, chikaku no pureiyaa ni doku wo ataeru.) - The area effect cloud spreads, poisoning nearby players.
minnanocraft.token.emperor_red_snapper.d: センネンダイ (sen'nendai) is the Japanese name for the Emperor red snapper. In Minecraft it appears in katakana, a typical choice for marine item names.
minnanocraft.token.emperor_red_snapper.e: センネンダイを釣り上げて、料理に使う。 (Sen'nendai wo tsuriage te, ryoori ni tsukau.) - Catch the Emperor red snapper and use it in cooking.
minnanocraft.token.entity.desc: エンティティ (Entiti) is a katakana loanword denoting any independent object or creature in the game, matching the English "entity" as a distinct being.
minnanocraft.token.entity.example: This block creates a new エンティティ (Entiti) when triggered - Este bloco cria uma nova entidade ao ser acionado
minnanocraft.token.dottyback.desc: メギス (Megisu) is a katakana transliteration of "dottyback", designating an aquatic mob that blends with reef blocks.
minnanocraft.token.dottyback.example: While exploring a river, you spot a メギス (Megisu) hiding among corals - Enquanto explora um rio, você vê um メギス (Megisu) escondido entre corais
minnanocraft.token.duration.desc: 時間 (じかん, jikan) merges 時 (time) and 間 (interval), referring to the length an effect or redstone signal lasts.
minnanocraft.token.duration.example: The beacon provides a 10 分間の時間 (jikan) boost - wo beacon fornece um aumento de duração de dez minutos
minnanocraft.token.custom.desc: カスタム (kasutamu) is a katakana loan meaning something modified or player‑created, such as custom textures or commands.
minnanocraft.token.custom.example: Apply a カスタム (kasutamu) skin to your armor for unique appearance - Aplique uma skin customizada à sua armadura para aparência única
minnanocraft.token.daisy.desc: ギク (giku) is a katakana representation of the daisy flower, used as a decorative block in plains biomes.
minnanocraft.token.daisy.example: Place a ギク (giku) near your base to brighten the area - Coloque um giku perto da sua base para iluminar wo ambiente
minnanocraft.token.dasher.desc: ダッシャー (Dasshaa) is in katakana, marking it as a gairaigo from English “dasher”. In Minecraft it would suit a fast‑moving mob, echoing the notion of dashing.
minnanocraft.token.dasher.example: ダッシャーが洞窟を突進した！ (Dasshaa ga dookoo wo totsushin shita!) - The Dasher rushed through the cave!
minnanocraft.token.day.desc: 日 (hi) means “sun” or “day”. Minecraft’s daylight cycle is driven by this very sun that rises and sets every 20 minutes.
minnanocraft.token.day.example: 朝になると、日が空に昇る。 (Asa ni naru to, hi ga sora ni noboru.) - When morning comes, the day rises in the sky.
minnanocraft.token.shine.desc: 照 (shoo) conveys “to illuminate” or “to shine”. Light‑emitting blocks in Minecraft, such as torches, literally 照 (shoo) the surroundings.
minnanocraft.token.shine.example: 松明が照を放つ。 (Taima ga shoo wo hanatsu.) - The torch emits light.
minnanocraft.token.light_1.desc: ライト (Raito) is katakana for the English “light”. In Minecraft it can refer to lanterns or any block that provides artificial illumination.
minnanocraft.token.light_1.example: ライトで暗い洞窟を照らす。 (Raito de kurai dookoo wo terasu.) - Light the dark cave with a lantern.
minnanocraft.token.debris.desc: 残骸 (zangai) merges 残 (zanzu, “remaining”) + 骸 (gai, “remains, bones”). It denotes scattered fragments, akin to the debris left after a structure collapses in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.debris.example: 船が沈んで残骸が海底に散らばっている。 (Fune ga shinde zangai ga kaitei ni chirabatte iru.) - The ship sank and debris is scattered on the seabed.
minnanocraft.token.crops.desc: The Japanese word 作物 (sakumotsu) merges 作 (saku, 'to make') and 物 (motsu, 'thing'), literally 'made things', matching the harvestable plants in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.crops.example: 農場で作物を収穫した。 (Noojoo de sakumotsu wo shuukaku shita.) - I harvested crops on the farm.
minnanocraft.token.core.desc: コア (ko-a) is a katakana loan from English 'core', indicating the central part of a mechanism or block.
minnanocraft.token.core.example: レッドストーン回路のコアを調整した。 (Reddo sutoon kairo no ko-a wo choosei shita.) - I adjusted the core of the redstone circuit.
minnanocraft.token.cotton.desc: 綿 (wata) translates to 'cotton', the soft fiber that appears as cotton blocks in the game.
minnanocraft.token.cotton.example: 綿のブロックでベッドを作った。 (Wata no burokkude beddo wo tsukutta.) - I made a bed from cotton blocks.
minnanocraft.token.crafting.desc: 作業 (sagyoo) combines 作 (saku, 'to make') and 業 (gyoo, 'work'), denoting the act of crafting items.
minnanocraft.token.crafting.example: 作業台で剣を作業した。 (Sagyoodai de ken wo sagyoo shita.) - I crafted a sword at the crafting table.
minnanocraft.token.crafting_1.desc: クラフト (kura-futo) is a katakana loan from English 'craft', referring to the crafting action.
minnanocraft.token.crafting_1.example: 新しいツールをクラフトした。 (Atarashii tsuuru wo kura-futo shita.) - I crafted a new tool.
minnanocraft.token.automatic.desc: 自動 (jidoo) literally means "self‑move", from 自 (self) and 動 (move). In Minecraft it describes mechanisms like redstone‑powered automatic doors.
minnanocraft.token.automatic.example: 自動ドアがレッドストーンで作動した (jidoo doa ga reddosutoon de sakudoo shita) - The automatic door was activated by redstone.
minnanocraft.token.clownfish.desc: クマノミ (kumanomi) is a katakana gairaigo from English "clown fish". In Minecraft it is the tropical fish that can be collected and used for turtle breeding.
minnanocraft.token.clownfish.example: クマノミを水槽に入れた (kumanomi wo suiso ni iれta) - I placed a clownfish in the aquarium.
minnanocraft.token.cocoa.desc: ココア (kokoa) is a katakana loanword from English "cocoa". In Minecraft it refers to cocoa beans harvested from jungle trees for cookies and chocolate.
minnanocraft.token.cocoa.example: ココアの豆を収穫した (kokoa no mame wo shuukaku shita) - I harvested cocoa beans.
minnanocraft.token.cocoa_1.desc: カカオ (kakao) is katakana for the Portuguese word "cacau". In Minecraft it denotes the cocoa pods that grow on jungle trees.
minnanocraft.token.cocoa_1.example: カカオの実を植えた (kakao no mi wo ueta) - I planted cocoa pods.
minnanocraft.token.nut.desc: 実 (mi) translates to "fruit" or "seed", commonly used for nuts. In a Minecraft mod, nuts could serve as a food item or crafting component.
minnanocraft.token.nut.example: 木の実を収穫した (ki no mi wo shuukaku shita) - I harvested the nuts from the tree.
minnanocraft.token.column.desc: The Japanese word 桁 (keta) denotes a numeric column; its kanji 木 (tree) + 形 (shape) evokes a vertical trunk, akin to stone columns used as supports in Minecraft builds.
minnanocraft.token.column.example: この塔は高い桁で支えられている。 (Kono too wa takai keta de sasaerarete iru.) - This tower stands on sturdy columns.
minnanocraft.token.cichlid.desc: シクリッド (shikuriddo) is a katakana loan from English 'cichlid', a tropical fish; Minecraft's clayfish resembles a fish, and the term preserves the biological reference.
minnanocraft.token.cichlid.example: 池でシクリッドが泳いでいる。 (Ike de shikuriddo ga oyoideru.) - A cichlid is swimming in the pond.
minnanocraft.token.clayfish.desc: クレイフィッシュ (kureifisshu) is a katakana rendering of 'clayfish', the mud‑dwelling fish introduced in the Clay Blocks update, reflecting its material.
minnanocraft.token.clayfish.example: 採掘中にクレイフィッシュの音がした。 (Saikutsu-chuu ni kureifisshu no oto ga shita.) - I heard a clayfish sound while mining.
minnanocraft.token.cleric.desc: 聖職者 (seishokusha) means 'holy worker', from 聖 (holy) + 職 (occupation) + 者 (person); in Minecraft the cleric villager embodies this as a potion‑trading priest.
minnanocraft.token.cleric.example: ポーションを求めて聖職者に近づいた。 (Pooshon wo motomete seishokusha ni chikadzu ita.) - I approached the cleric seeking a potion.
minnanocraft.token.closed.desc: 閉じた (tojita) means 'closed', the past form of 閉じる; it describes blocks like doors or chests that are not open in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.closed.example: チェストは閉じたままだった。 (Chesuto wa tojita mama datta.) - The chest remained closed.
minnanocraft.token.cartography.desc: The word 製図 (seizu) merges 製 (sei) “to make” and 図 (zu) “drawing, map”, mirroring the cartography table’s role of producing detailed maps in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.cartography.example: この製図台で新しい地図を作ろう！ (Kono seizutaide atarashii chizu wo tsukurou!) - Let's craft a new map on this cartography table!
minnanocraft.token.carved.desc: くり抜かれた (kuri nukareta) is a native verb written in hiragana meaning “carved out”, describing the hollowed interior of the carved pumpkin block in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.carved.example: くり抜かれたカボチャが灯りを放つ。 (Kuri nukareta kabocha ga akari wo hanatsu.) - The carved pumpkin emits light.
minnanocraft.token.charge.desc: 係 (kakari) means “person in charge, duty”. In Minecraft it relates to the “charged creeper”, which gains extra power when struck by lightning, as if it’s been put under a charge.
minnanocraft.token.charge.example: 雷がクリーパーを係 (kakari) に変える。 (Kaminari ga kuriipaa wo kakari ni kaeru.) - Lightning turns the creeper into a charged one.
minnanocraft.token.chipped.desc: 欠 (ketsu) conveys “missing, gap, defect”. The “chipped” anvil in Minecraft shows a missing piece, matching the kanji’s meaning of a defect.
minnanocraft.token.chipped.example: 欠 (ketsu) のある金床は修理に使える。 (Ketsu no aru kanadoko wa shuuri ni tsukaeru.) - A chipped anvil can be used for repairs.
minnanocraft.token.butcher.desc: 肉屋 (nikuya) merges 肉 (niku) “meat” and 屋 (ya) “shop”. In Minecraft the butcher villager trades meat items, mirroring a literal “meat shop”.
minnanocraft.token.butcher.example: 肉屋 (nikuya) の取引でステーキを手に入れよう。 (Nikuya no torihiki de suteeki wo te ni ireyou.) - Let's get a steak from the butcher's trades.
minnanocraft.token.butterflyfish.desc: チョウチョウウオ (Chouchouuo) appears in katakana, a stylized rendering of the native term 蝶々 (choucho) “butterfly” and 魚 (uo) “fish”. In Minecraft, the butterflyfish displays bright, wing‑like patterns, perfect for decorative ponds.
minnanocraft.token.butterflyfish.example: 私の水槽にチョウチョウウオを入れた。 (Watashi no suiso ni Chouchouuo wo ireta.) - I placed a butterflyfish in my aquarium.
minnanocraft.token.calibrated.desc: 調律 (Chouritsu) merges 調 (chou) “to adjust” and 律 (ritsu) “law, rhythm”. In Minecraft, calibrating redstone circuits or note blocks demands precise tuning, akin to instrument tuning.
minnanocraft.token.calibrated.example: レッドストーン回路を調律した。 (Reddo suto-n kairo wo Chouritsu shita.) - I calibrated the redstone circuit.
minnanocraft.token.candy.desc: 飴 (Ame) means “candy” or “sugar candy”. In Minecraft, candy‑like items appear as sugar drops or sweet treats that restore hunger.
minnanocraft.token.candy.example: 洞窟で飴を見つけた。 (Doukutsu de Ame wo mitsuketa.) - I found candy in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.cartographer.desc: 製図家 (Seizuka) combines 製 (sei) “to make”, 図 (zu) “map/diagram” and 家 (ka) “person”. In Minecraft, the cartographer villager produces detailed maps and surveys biomes.
minnanocraft.token.cartographer.example: 村人の製図家が新しい地図を描いた。 (Murabito no Seizuka ga atarashii chizu wo kaita.) - The villager cartographer drew a new map.
minnanocraft.token.budding.desc: 芽生 (Meba) merges 芽 (me) “bud” and 生 (sei) “to sprout”. In Minecraft, budding blocks spawn crystals, echoing the emergence of new buds.
minnanocraft.token.budding.example: 洞窟で芽生ブロックを見つけた。 (Doukutsu de Meba burokku wo mitsuketa.) - I found a budding block in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.bullet.desc: The kanji 弾 (dan) denotes a projectile; in Minecraft it matches items such as arrows or snowballs that travel through the air.
minnanocraft.token.bullet.example: 弾が飛んでくる！ (Dan ga tonde kuru!) - Projectiles fly!
minnanocraft.token.bunny.desc: バニー (banii) is a katakana loanword from English "bunny"; it refers to the rabbit mob that hops around forest biomes.
minnanocraft.token.bunny.example: バニーが跳ねている！ (Banii ga hanete iru!) - The bunny is hopping!
minnanocraft.token.burst.desc: 破裂 (haretsu) merges 破 (ha, break) and 裂 (retsu, split); it describes bursts such as TNT explosions in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.burst.example: TNTが破裂した！ (TNT ga haretsu shita!) - TNT burst!
minnanocraft.token.bordure.desc: 縁取り (en-tori) combines 縁 (en, edge) and 取り (tori, from 取る, to take) to mean a decorative border, similar to map edges or block outlines in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.bordure.example: 地図に縁取りを付けよう！ (Chizu ni en-tori wo tsukeyou!) - Let's add a border to the map!
minnanocraft.token.table.desc: 台 (dai) denotes a stand or platform; in Minecraft it functions as the base for crafting tables, pedestals, or workbenches.
minnanocraft.token.table.example: 作業台を置いた！ (Sagyou-dai wo oita!) - Placed the crafting table!
minnanocraft.token.table_1.desc: テーブル (tēburu) is a katakana loan from English 'table'; in Minecraft it denotes the workbench used to arrange resources.
minnanocraft.token.table_1.example: テーブルの横にかまどを置くと、作業が楽になる。 (Tēburu no yoko ni kamado wo oku to, sagyoo ga raku ni naru.) - Placing a furnace next to the table makes work easier.
minnanocraft.token.breathing.desc: 呼吸 (kokyuu) merges 呼 (ko, 'call') and 吸 (kyuu, 'inhale'); in Minecraft it denotes the need for air, especially when diving.
minnanocraft.token.breathing.example: 水中で呼吸ができないと、すぐに溺れる。 (Suichuu de kokyuu ga dekinai to, sugu ni oboreru.) - If you can't breathe underwater, you drown quickly.
minnanocraft.token.brewing.desc: 醸造 (joozoo) combines 醸 (joo, 'ferment') and 造 (zoo, 'make'); in the game it refers to the process of crafting potions at the Brewing Stand.
minnanocraft.token.brewing.example: 醸造台でポーションを作ると、冒険が楽になる。 (Joozoo-dai de pooshon wo tsukuru to, booken ga raku ni naru.) - Crafting potions at the brewing stand makes adventures easier.
minnanocraft.token.brinely.desc: ブラインリー (buraindorī) is a katakana loan from English 'brinely', used to describe salty environments like oceans.
minnanocraft.token.brinely.example: ブラインリーな海岸では、塩分が高い。 (Buraindorī na kaigan de wa, enbun ga takai.) - On briny coasts, the salinity is high.
minnanocraft.token.brute.desc: ブルート (buruuto) derives from English 'brute' and in Minecraft describes creatures or players with raw strength.
minnanocraft.token.brute.example: ブルートの敵は、強力な近接攻撃を持つ。 (Buruuto no teki wa, kyooryoku na kinsetsu koogeki wo motsu.) - Brute enemies have powerful melee attacks.
minnanocraft.token.bobber.desc: Uki (浮き) derives from the kanji 浮 meaning 'to float' plus the noun suffix -ki; in Minecraft, the Fishing Bobber literally floats on water.
minnanocraft.token.bobber.example: 川の上に浮きが揺れる (Kawa no ue ni uki ga yureru) - The bobber sways above the river.
minnanocraft.token.bogged.desc: Bogudo (ボグド) is a katakana loanword from English 'bogged', meaning stuck in mud; in Minecraft, the Bogged mob appears in swamp biomes.
minnanocraft.token.bogged.example: 沼地でボグドが現れる (Numachi de bogudo ga arawareru) - A Bogged appears in the swamp.
minnanocraft.token.blockfish.desc: Burokku fisshu (ブロックフィッシュ) merges the katakana ブロック (block) and フィッシュ (fish), literally 'block fish', matching the cubic fish entity in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.blockfish.example: 海でブロックフィッシュを捕まえる (Umi de burokku fisshu wo tsukamaeru) - Catch a Blockfish in the ocean.
minnanocraft.token.pholidae.desc: Isoginpo (イソギンポ) is the Japanese katakana term for fish of the Pholidae family, noted for red lips; in Minecraft, the Red Lipped Blenny mirrors this trait.
minnanocraft.token.pholidae.example: サンゴ礁でイソギンポが泳ぐ (Sangoshoo de isoginpo ga oyogu) - An Isoginpo swims among the coral reefs.
minnanocraft.token.berry.desc: ベリー (Berī) is a gairaigo from English 'berry', matching the red fruit item in Minecraft that restores hunger.
minnanocraft.token.berry.example: 甘いベリーを収穫して、食料を補給しよう。 (Amai Berī wo shuuka shite, shokuryoo wo hokyuu shiyoo.) - Harvest sweet berries to replenish food.
minnanocraft.token.betta.desc: ベタ (Beta) is a loanword referring to the Betta fish, known for vivid colors, represented in Minecraft as an ornamental fish swimming in rivers.
minnanocraft.token.betta.example: 川でベタを見つけて、観察しよう。 (Kawa de Beta wo mitsukete, kansatsu shiyoo.) - Find the Betta in the river and observe it.
minnanocraft.token.betty.desc: ベティー (Betī) is a katakana proper name, used for a friendly character in the mod, without lexical meaning.
minnanocraft.token.betty.example: ベティーと一緒に建築を始めよう。 (Betī to issho ni kenchiku wo hajimeyoo.) - Start building together with Betty.
minnanocraft.token.beans.desc: 隠元 (In'gen) merges 隠 'hide' and 元 'origin', suggesting hidden seeds; in Minecraft, beans are planted and sprout underground.
minnanocraft.token.beans.example: 隠元を植えて、作物を育てよう。 (In'gen wo uete, sakumotsu wo sodateyoo.) - Plant the hidden seeds and grow the crop.
minnanocraft.token.arms.desc: The term 両腕 (ryouude) merges 両 (ryou, ‘both’) and 腕 (ude, ‘arm’), referring to the two upper limbs of the player model that hold tools and weapons in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.arms.example: The player grips the pickaxe with 両腕 (ryouude). (Pureiyaa wa ryouude de pikkelu wo nigiru.) - The player holds the pickaxe with both arms.
minnanocraft.token.up.desc: 上げた (ageta) is the past form of 上げる (ageru); 上 (ue) means ‘up’ and げた marks a completed action, describing the raising of something, such as blocks that are lifted in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.up.example: The block was 上げた (ageta) and floated upward. (Burokku wo ageta de sora e ukanda.) - The block was raised and floated into the sky.
minnanocraft.token.awkward.desc: 奇妙な (kimyoona) merges 奇 (ki, ‘odd’) and 妙 (myoo, ‘peculiar’), indicating something awkward or strange, like a block placed in an odd configuration in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.awkward.example: The 奇妙な (kimyoona) tower collapsed. (Kimyoona koozoo no too ga kuzureta.) - The awkward tower fell.
minnanocraft.token.area.desc: 辺 (hen) means ‘edge’ or ‘surrounding region’, used to denote the area around a point, such as the influence zone of a beacon in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.area.example: The player entered the beacon's 辺 (hen). (Bīkon no hen ni pureiyaa ga haitta.) - The player stepped into the beacon's area.
minnanocraft.token.queen_angelfish.desc: クィーンエンゼルフィッシュ (kuīn enzerufisshu) is written in katakana, marking it as a gairaigo from English ‘queen angelfish’, naming the ornamental fish that appears in Minecraft's aquatic biomes.
minnanocraft.token.queen_angelfish.examp: The クィーンエンゼルフィッシュ (kuīn enzerufisshu) swims in the tank. (Kuīn enzerufisshu ga suiso ni oyoide iru.) - The queen angelfish swims in the aquarium.
minnanocraft.token.night_vision.desc: 暗視 (anshi) is composed of 暗 (dark) + 視 (vision), matching the Night Vision potion that lets players see in darkness.
minnanocraft.token.night_vision.example: 暗闇でも遠くの鉱石が見えるように、暗視のポーションを飲んだ。 (Kurayami demo tooku no kouseki ga mieru you ni, anshi no pooshon wo nonda.) - I drank a Night Vision potion so I could see ores far away even in darkness.
minnanocraft.token.empty.desc: 空 (sora/kuu) means "sky" (sora) and "empty" (kuu), fitting the Air block that is both empty space and the open sky in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.empty.example: 洞窟の天井が崩れ、空が見えた。 (Doukutsu no tenjou ga kuzure, sora ga mieta.) - The cave ceiling collapsed, revealing the sky.
minnanocraft.token.equipment.desc: 装備品 (soubi-hin) breaks down into 装 (to equip) + 備 (to prepare) + 品 (item), denoting items a player equips for challenges.
minnanocraft.token.equipment.example: 新しい装備品を作って、ダイヤの鎧を装着した。 (Atarashii soubi-hin wo tsukutte, daiya no yoroi wo souchaku shita.) - I crafted new equipment and equipped diamond armor.
minnanocraft.token.disabled.desc: 障害者 (shougai-sha) is composed of 障 (obstacle) + 害 (harm) + 者 (person), literally "person with a disability"; in Minecraft, "disabled" is usually rendered as 無効 (mukou) for deactivated features.
minnanocraft.token.disabled.example: 設定で自動ジャンプが無効になっているので、手動でジャンプしなければならない。 (Settei de jidou janpu ga mukou ni natteiru node, shudou de janpu shinakereba naranai.) - Since auto-jump is disabled in the settings, I must jump manually.
minnanocraft.token.disc.desc: 皿 (sara) means "plate"; despite Minecraft calling it a music disc, the kanji evokes the round, plate‑like shape of the item.
minnanocraft.token.disc.example: 洞窟で古い音楽皿を見つけた。 (Doukutsu de furui ongaku sara wo mitsuketa.) - I found an old music disc in the cave.
