minnanocraft.token.display.desc: The term 表示 (hyouji) merges 表 (hyou, “surface”) and 示 (ji, “to show”), mirroring Minecraft’s UI that displays health bars, chat, and coordinates.
minnanocraft.token.display.example: 画面に表示された座標を確認しよう。 (Gamen ni hyouji sareta zahyou wo kakunin shiyou.) - Check the coordinates displayed on the screen.
minnanocraft.token.blossom.desc: 花 (hana) literally means “flower”, referring to Minecraft flower blocks that can be harvested for petals or dye.
minnanocraft.token.blossom.example: 庭に咲く花を摘んで染料にしよう。 (Niwa ni saku hana wo tsunde senryou ni shiyou.) - Gather the blossoms blooming in the garden to craft dye.
minnanocraft.token.beans_1.desc: 豆 (mame) denotes beans; in Minecraft, cocoa beans grow on jungle tree trunks and are used for dye and chocolate.
minnanocraft.token.beans_1.example: ジャングルの木から豆を収穫した。 (Janguru no ki kara mame wo shuukaku shita.) - Harvested beans from the jungle tree.
minnanocraft.token.applies.desc: 全入 (zennyuu) combines 全 (zen, “all”) and 入 (nyuu, “enter”), used to denote that an effect applies universally across slots or items.
minnanocraft.token.applies.example: このエンチャントは全入の効果を持つ。 (Kono enchanto wa zennyuu no kouka wo motsu.) - This enchantment has an applies effect.
minnanocraft.token.anemone.desc: アネモネ (anemone) is a katakana loanword from English “anemone”, referring to the oceanic flower found on underwater structures in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.anemone.example: 海底神殿の壁にアネモネが咲いている。 (Kaitei shinden no kabe ni anemone ga saiteiru.) - Anemones bloom on the walls of the ocean monument.
minnanocraft.token.ancient.desc: 古代 (kodai) merges 古 'old' and 代 'era', denoting bygone civilizations; in Minecraft it matches ancient stone structures or ruins.
minnanocraft.token.ancient.example: 古代の遺跡で光るブロックを探す (Kodai no iseki de hikaru burokkku wo sagasu) - Search for glowing blocks in ancient ruins.
minnanocraft.token.anchor.desc: アンカー (ankaa) is a katakana loan from English 'anchor', representing the item that anchors boats to the seabed.
minnanocraft.token.anchor.example: 船をアンカーで固定する (Fune wo ankaa de kotei suru) - Drop an anchor to stop the boat from drifting.
minnanocraft.token.bolt.desc: ネジ止め (nejidome) merges ネジ 'screw' (loan) and 止め 'fastening', indicating a bolt that secures blocks.
minnanocraft.token.bolt.example: ドアにネジ止めを使う (Doa ni nejidome wo tsukau) - Secure the redstone door with a bolt.
minnanocraft.token.dune.desc: 砂丘 (sakkyuu) combines 砂 'sand' and 丘 'hill', referring to the dunes found in desert biomes.
minnanocraft.token.dune.example: 砂丘の上にオアシスを建てる (Sakkyuu no ue ni oashisu wo tateru) - Build an oasis atop a dune.
minnanocraft.token.host.desc: 主人 (shujin) merges 主 'master' and 人 'person', denoting the owner or host; in Minecraft it can mean the server host or a villager proprietor.
minnanocraft.token.host.example: サーバーの主人がイベントを開催する (Saabaa no shujin ga ibento wo kaisai suru) - The host invites players to the event.
minnanocraft.token.raiser.desc: The word 牧者 (Bokusha) merges 牧 (boku, "pasture") and 者 (sha, "person"), meaning "pasture person". In Minecraft it suits a block or mob that herds sheep.
minnanocraft.token.raiser.example: 牧者が羊の群れを導く (Bokusha ga hitsuji no mure wo michibiku) - The herder leads the flock of sheep.
minnanocraft.token.rib.desc: あばら (abara) is a native Japanese word written in hiragana meaning "rib". In Minecraft it can refer to a skeleton's ribs or a rib‑shaped bone block.
minnanocraft.token.rib.example: 骸骨のあばらが光る (Gaikotsu no abara ga hikaru) - The skeleton's ribs glow.
minnanocraft.token.sentry.desc: 略奪者 (Ryakuatsu‑sha) combines 略 (ryaku, "plunder") and 奪 (datsu, "seize") with 者 (sha, "person"), yielding "plunderer". In Minecraft it matches the Pillager or a looting sentry.
minnanocraft.token.sentry.example: 略奪者が村を襲う (Ryakuatsu‑sha ga mura wo osou) - The sentry raids the village.
minnanocraft.token.shaper.desc: 職人 (Shokunin) merges 職 (shoku, "profession") and 人 (nin, "person"), meaning "craftsman". In Minecraft it fits a block or NPC that shapes tools, like a smith.
minnanocraft.token.shaper.example: 職人が剣を鍛える (Shokunin ga ken wo kitaeru) - The shaper forges a sword.
minnanocraft.token.silence.desc: 静寂 (Seijaku) joins 静 (sei, "quiet") and 寂 (jaku, "loneliness"), yielding "silence". In Minecraft it may label a quiet biome or a silence‑granting potion.
minnanocraft.token.silence.example: 静寂が洞窟を包む (Seijaku ga doukutsu wo tsutsumu) - Silence envelops the cave.
minnanocraft.token.spire.desc: The term 尖塔 (sentou) merges 尖 'sharp' and 塔 'tower', denoting a pointed tower similar to stone watchtowers players build to scout surrounding biomes.
minnanocraft.token.spire.example: 尖塔の上からネザーの光が見える。 (Sentou no ue kara Nēzaa no hikari ga mieru.) - From the spire's summit, the glow of the Nether can be seen.
minnanocraft.token.tide.desc: 潮流 (chouryuu) combines 潮 'tide' and 流 'flow', referring to the tide's current that moves water blocks like ocean currents that can carry items.
minnanocraft.token.tide.example: 潮流が満ちると、海岸の砂が遠くへ運ばれる。 (Chouryuu ga michiru to, kaigan no suna ga tooku e hakobareru.) - When the tide rises, the beach sand is carried far away.
minnanocraft.token.ward.desc: 監獄 (kangoku) merges 監 'oversee' and 獄 'prison', indicating a confinement place, akin to dungeons players build to contain mobs.
minnanocraft.token.ward.example: 監獄の壁はエンダーの目から守る。 (Kangoku no kabe wa Endaa no me kara mamoru.) - The prison walls guard against the Ender eye.
minnanocraft.token.wayfinder.desc: 先駆者 (senkusha) combines 先 'ahead', 駆 'run', and 者 'person', describing one who paves the way, like a map or compass that guides the player.
minnanocraft.token.wayfinder.example: 先駆者は新しい洞窟へ道を示す。 (Senkusha wa atarashii dookoo e michi wo shimesu.) - The wayfinder points the way to a new cave.
minnanocraft.token.wild.desc: 大自然 (daishizen) merges 大 'big' and 自然 'nature', referring to the wild environment, such as dense forests and open plains that players explore.
minnanocraft.token.wild.example: 大自然の中で狼の群れが遠吠えする。 (Daishizen no naka de ookami no mure ga tooboe suru.) - In the wild, a pack of wolves howls in the distance.
minnanocraft.token.allium.desc: アリウム (ariumu) is a katakana loanword from Latin "Allium", naming the wild garlic flower; in Minecraft it appears as a purple flower used for decoration and brewing.
minnanocraft.token.allium.example: 庭にアリウムを植えて、夜のモブを遠ざけた。(Niwa ni ariumu wo uete, yoru no mobu wo toozaketa.) - I planted alliums in the garden to keep night mobs away.
minnanocraft.token.abandoned.desc: 放棄 (houki) merges 放 (to release) and 棄 (to discard), meaning something left unattended; abandoned villages in Minecraft are empty structures that still contain loot.
minnanocraft.token.abandoned.example: 放棄された村を探索し、隠されたチェストを見つけた。(Houki sareta mura wo tansaku shi, kakusareta chesuto wo mitsuketa.) - I explored the abandoned village and found a hidden chest.
minnanocraft.token.buried.desc: 埋もれた (umoreta) comes from 埋 (to bury) plus the suffix indicating being covered, signifying something buried; buried treasure in Minecraft requires careful digging.
minnanocraft.token.buried.example: 砂の中に埋もれた宝箱を掘り出した。(Suna no naka ni umoreta takarabako wo horidashita.) - I unearthed a buried treasure chest from the sand.
minnanocraft.token.camp.desc: キャンプ (kyanpu) is a katakana loanword from English "camp"; in Minecraft a camp comprises temporary beds, torches, and chests for shelter.
minnanocraft.token.camp.example: 山の頂上にキャンプを設置し、夜を越えた。(Yama no choujou ni kyanpu wo setchi shi, yoru wo koeta.) - I set up a camp on the mountain summit and made it through the night.
minnanocraft.token.city.desc: 都市 (toshi) merges 都 (capital) and 市 (market), denoting a large urban settlement; cities in Minecraft are expansive villages with many buildings and trade routes.
minnanocraft.token.city.example: 広大な都市を建設し、交易路をつなげた。(Koudaina toshi wo kensetsu shi, kouekiro wo tsunageta.) - I built a vast city and linked trade routes.
minnanocraft.token.desert.desc: The term 砂漠 (sabaku) merges 砂 (suna, sand) and 漠 (baku, barren land), mirroring Minecraft's endless sand dunes and cacti.
minnanocraft.token.desert.example: 砂漠でオアシスを見つけた (Sabaku de oashisu wo mitsuketa) - I found an oasis in the desert.
minnanocraft.token.mineshaft.desc: The term 廃坑 (haikou) combines 廃 (hai, abandoned) and 坑 (kou, pit/mineshaft), describing the empty tunnels generated when mining in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.mineshaft.example: 廃坑の中でレッドストーンを見つけた (Haikou no naka de reddo sutoon wo mitsuketa) - I found redstone inside the abandoned mine.
minnanocraft.token.plains.desc: The term 平原 (heigen) merges 平 (hei, flat) and 原 (gen, open field), matching Minecraft's wide, level plains.
minnanocraft.token.plains.example: 平原で羊の群れを見つけた (Heigen de hitsuji no mure wo mitsuketa) - I found a flock of sheep on the plains.
minnanocraft.token.pyramid.desc: The term 寺院 (jiin) fuses 寺 (tera, temple) and 院 (in, institution), referring to the pyramid‑shaped temple found in Minecraft deserts.
minnanocraft.token.pyramid.example: 寺院の入口でトラップチェストを見つけた (Jiin no iriguchi de torappu chesuto wo mitsuketa) - I found a trap chest at the temple entrance.
minnanocraft.token.ruins.desc: The term 遺跡 (iseki) combines 遺 (i, legacy) and 跡 (seki, trace), describing the ancient ruins players explore in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.ruins.example: 遺跡でエンチャント本を見つけた (Iseki de enchanto hon wo mitsuketa) - I found an enchanted book in the ruins.
minnanocraft.token.savanna.desc: Savanna (sabanna) is an English loanword describing open vegetation and scattered trees, matching the Minecraft savanna biome with tall grass and few trees forming wide plains.
minnanocraft.token.savanna.example: サバンナの草原で羊を放牧しよう (Sabanna no soogen de hitsuji wo hooboku shiyoo) - Let's herd sheep on the savanna plain.
minnanocraft.token.snowy.desc: Snowy (setsugen) combines 雪 (yuki) 'snow' and 原 (hara) 'plain', describing Minecraft's snow-covered biome with flat white terrain.
minnanocraft.token.snowy.example: 雪原で氷の剣を鍛えよう (Setsugen de koori no ken wo kitaeyoo) - Let's forge an ice sword on the snowy plain.
minnanocraft.token.swamp.desc: Swamp (numachi) merges 沼 (numa) 'marsh' and 地 (chi) 'land', representing Minecraft's swamp biome with stagnant water and foliage.
minnanocraft.token.swamp.example: 沼地で泥ブロックを採掘しよう (Numachi de doro burokku wo saikutsu shiyoo) - Let's mine mud blocks in the swamp.
minnanocraft.token.taiga.desc: Taiga (taiga) is a loanword denoting the cold coniferous forest, matching Minecraft's taiga biome with pine trees and snow.
minnanocraft.token.taiga.example: タイガの森で松の木を伐採しよう (Taiga no mori de matsu no ki wo bassai shiyoo) - Let's harvest pine trees in the taiga forest.
minnanocraft.token.treasure.desc: Treasure (takara) means 'treasure', used in Minecraft chests and structures to denote valuable items.
minnanocraft.token.treasure.example: 洞窟の奥で宝を見つけた (Dookutsu no oku de takara wo mitsuketa) - I found a treasure deep in the cave.
minnanocraft.token.village.desc: The Japanese term 村 (mura) translates to 'village' and reflects the cluster of houses and villagers that serve as a trading hub in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.village.example: We explored the 村 (mura) and traded with the villagers - Exploramos a vila e negociamos com os aldeões.
minnanocraft.token.warm.desc: 暖かい (atatakai) uses the kanji 暖 (warm) plus the adjective ending, describing a pleasant temperature, similar to the glow of heated wool in a desert biome.
minnanocraft.token.warm.example: The 暖かい (atatakai) sun melts the snow near the campfire - wo sol quente derrete a neve perto da fogueira.
minnanocraft.token.entry.desc: 入 (nyuu) means 'enter' or 'entry', referring to doors or portals that grant access to structures such as strongholds.
minnanocraft.token.entry.example: We found the 入 (nyuu) to the stronghold behind the vines - Encontramos a entrada da fortaleza atrás das trepadeiras.
minnanocraft.token.color.desc: 色 (iro) means 'color', fundamental for dyes that change the look of blocks and armor in Minecraft.
minnanocraft.token.color.example: She crafted red 色 (iro) dye from poppies - Ela criou cor vermelha a partir de papoulas.
minnanocraft.token.woodland.desc: 森林 (shinrin) merges 森 (forest) and 林 (grove), depicting dense tree areas where oak logs can be harvested.
minnanocraft.token.woodland.example: We gathered oak logs in the 森林 (shinrin) biome - Coletamos troncos de carvalho no bioma de floresta.
